qualityWhy: The SKILL.md gives a clear overview, provider tables, best practices and common mistakes, and the provider guides hold full code, though I judged only the main file in detail.
needs: Clerk, Auth0, WorkOS, Kinde, Stytch or Better Auth account for the chosen provider
OKX Web3 API key from web3.okx.com for x402 payments
InsForge CLI access to read JWT_SECRET
why: Fractera nodes use their own sign-in element and SQLite data, not InsForge's Postgres and JWT-based RLS, so the auth flows do not map onto the node's stack and the skill would need adapting; the x402 payment part is useful for paid endpoints but relies on an outside facilitator and a paid service. The guides also assume InsForge's backend, so the skill is best read for ideas.

summary: The skill guides an agent through verifying whether a photo or video is authentic, original and correctly captioned. It puts provenance first: finding the earliest copy and its caption, then metadata, C2PA signatures, physical consistency such as shadows and lighting, and only last signal-level forensics. It also covers the limits of AI-detector tools and the typical tells of AI-generated or deepfake media. It serves fact-checkers, investigators, insurance and KYC reviewers, and anyone needing evidence about media.
tasks: check whether a photo is recycled or miscaptioned
verify if a video is a deepfake or AI-generated
find the original source of an image
review a claim photo for manipulation before approving it
qualityWhy: The method is detailed, ordered and well-reasoned with concrete checks, but it leans on pivots to other skills and tools whose instructions are not in this bundle.
why: Useful for verifying media and checking content, but it is an investigation method rather than a building tool for a product, so value is some. It is stack-free and uses only local tools, so it can be installed as written; it refers to other skills it does not include, and the forensic tools it names are not all present, which limits what an agent can do from this bundle alone.

summary: This skill teaches an agent how an investigator can look at online targets without revealing who is looking. It covers threat modelling, the browser, network, and account traces that give a visitor away, and how to keep research identities fully separate from real ones. It also explains when a sockpuppet persona is justified, how to pick between a VPN, a residential proxy, and Tor, and how to grade exposure after each collection step. The intended audience is OSINT practitioners, journalists, due-diligence teams, and law-enforcement investigators.
tasks: set up a research account without the target noticing
choose between VPN, proxy and Tor for viewing a website
decide whether a sockpuppet persona is justified for a case
check what a platform reveals about profile viewers
qualityWhy: It is detailed and structured, with tables, checklists, a worked example and clear limits, though much of it is conceptual guidance that points to other files instead of step-by-step commands.
why: It serves covert investigation, not building, running, selling or making content for a product, so it does not fit what Fractera nodes are for. Its tactics for fake accounts also breach most platforms' terms of service and carry legal exposure.

summary: This skill walks an agent through adding Clerk, a hosted authentication service, to a project using the Clerk CLI and framework quickstarts. It covers new apps, existing projects that lack auth, and migrations from other auth systems, with checks before changing anything. It is aimed at developers who want hosted sign-in, sign-up and user management for a web or mobile app.
tasks: add Clerk sign-in to an existing Next.js app
scaffold a new app with Clerk authentication
migrate existing login to Clerk
verify Clerk auth controls render and fix setup issues
qualityWhy: It gives concrete commands, conditional branches, pre-change checks and verification steps, though it is long and assumes Clerk's own tooling throughout.
why: Clerk keeps user records, sessions and keys in its hosted cloud and competes with the node's own next-auth sign-in element, so it is a cloud auth backend the node does not use. The skill also installs Clerk's agent skills globally, which differs from the node's per-element install and would need review if the node ever adopted it.

summary: This skill teaches an agent to check whether an email, username, phone or name shows up in breach and leak data, and to read the service list and metadata in matching records as an account map. It sets a hard rule never to use or test leaked credentials, and it describes how to grade the confidence of each finding. It is aimed at incident responders, security teams and people auditing their own exposed data.
tasks: check whether an email address appeared in a data breach
audit my own leaked personal data
assess credential compromise after an incident
screen a vendor or hire for past breach exposure
qualityWhy: The skill gives clear source-selection tables, a strict ethics rule, grading criteria and a worked example, but it has no concrete commands or API call steps for an agent to follow.
needs: Have I Been Pwned API key
why: It is an investigation and personal-privacy method, not something that helps build, run, sell or make content for a product, so its value is none. It is skipped because it searches third-party breach corpora for named people's identifiers, which exposes those identifiers to outside services.
risks: Following it sends a third party's email, phone, username or name to commercial breach-search services without that person's knowledge.

summary: This skill turns an agent into a research engine that gathers what people are saying about a topic over the last 30 days, pulling posts and engagement from Reddit, X, YouTube, TikTok, Hacker News, Polymarket, GitHub and the web. It is built for analysts, marketers and writers who want a grounded, cited briefing rather than a generic web summary. It also includes a health check that diagnoses which sources are broken or unconfigured, and modes for comparisons, hiring signals, recommendations and HTML briefs.
tasks: research what people say about a product launch
compare two tools using recent community opinion
check which research sources are working
write a cited briefing on a trending topic
qualityWhy: The instructions are very detailed with routing tables, output laws, runbook references and self-checks, though the body is dense and some references were not visible to review.
needs: SCRAPECREATORS_API_KEY for TikTok, Instagram and Reddit backfill
optional X, OpenAI, xAI, Perplexity, Brave or Parallel keys
why: It is a research tool rather than a builder for sites or products, so its use is occasional for market and content research; it calls several outside APIs, some paid and some using the person's browser cookies, so the person must choose the keys and accept those calls.
risks: Can read browser cookies for X login when the person opts in, which exposes account session data to the engine.

summary: This skill lets an agent build website pages in a loop: it reads a task file, asks the Stitch design service for a screen, saves the returned HTML and screenshot locally, places the page in the site, checks it visually when Chrome tooling is present, and writes the next task. It is aimed at someone generating a multi-page marketing or product site one page at a time. The skill assumes a static site folder rather than a Next.js app.
tasks: build the next page of a marketing site with Stitch
generate a landing page from a design system and wire its navigation
keep an automated loop producing site pages one at a time
compare a generated page against its Stitch screenshot
qualityWhy: The SKILL.md gives concrete steps, a baton file format, a metadata schema and checks for existing files, though the integration step assumes a static site/public folder and the other bundled files were not reviewed.
needs: Stitch MCP server with a Google account
why: It directly helps build web pages for a product, but it needs an outside design service and its output is static HTML in site/public, which does not match a Next.js App Router node, so an agent must adapt the integration step to Blocks and React components.

summary: The skill guides an agent through reverse image searching: running a photo across several search engines, cropping and flipping it to find matches the full frame misses, and reading the earliest publication to learn its source, date and credits. It is aimed at fact-checkers, investigators, fraud and brand-protection teams, and anyone verifying where a picture came from. It also covers how to grade confidence, when face-matching tools are out of bounds, and which other investigation skills to hand off to.
tasks: trace where a photo first appeared online
check whether a profile picture is stock or reused
find the original source of a viral image or video keyframe
verify a suspected repost or recycled press photo
qualityWhy: The steps, engine-selection table, crop and flip routine, confidence grades and worked example are concrete and followable, though engine behaviour is asserted rather than verified and the pivots depend on other skills.
needs: optional paid face-search services such as PimEyes or FaceCheck.ID
why: It is an investigation and verification method rather than a tool for building sites, apps or product content, so its use for Fractera nodes is occasional, mainly checking image sources for content. It sends the images to third-party search engines, which the skill states openly; face-search services process biometric data and the skill limits their use to authorised cases.

summary: This skill guides an agent through building custom sign-in and sign-up screens with Clerk's hooks, using separate instructions for the older Core 2 SDK and the current Core 3 SDK. It also covers styling Clerk's prebuilt components with the appearance prop, including colors, fonts, logos, themes and CSS. The intended users are frontend developers who want authentication screens that match their brand.
tasks: build a custom sign-in page with useSignIn
style Clerk login forms to match our brand colors
apply a shadcn-compatible theme to Clerk components
add a custom sign-up flow with useSignUp
qualityWhy: The appearance section has concrete examples and pitfalls, but much of the detail is delegated to external documentation links and the reference files were only listed, not verified.
why: Clerk is a hosted authentication service, which the node replaces with its own sign-in element built on next-auth, so this is a cloud backend for a different auth stack and not usable on a local-first node.

summary: This skill guides an agent to edit existing Chinese text (articles, reviews, documents) so it reads more naturally, removing filler, repetition and templated phrasing while keeping facts, certainty levels and the author's voice. It gives a priority order for constraints, style rules per genre, a catalogue of 31 editing patterns with before/after examples, and a delivery checklist. It is aimed at writers and editors who polish Chinese prose.
tasks: polish a Chinese blog post to remove filler phrases
edit a Chinese product description so it reads naturally
review a Chinese document for repetitive or templated wording
rewrite a social media post in more natural Chinese
qualityWhy: It is detailed and internally consistent, with explicit priorities, worked examples, file-protection rules and a delivery checklist, though it is long and some patterns overlap.
why: Editing Chinese prose is useful for content making on a node, but it is only occasionally needed rather than central to building or running a product. It is a stack-free text skill, so it can be installed as written and needs no outside service.

summary: Gives an agent a diagnostic checklist for animations that drop frames or stutter in web pages. It explains which CSS properties are cheap to animate, when work should move off the main thread, how React state updates cause per-frame re-renders, and when will-change actually helps. The guidance is aimed at developers shipping interfaces to real devices, not at choosing easing or deciding whether motion should exist.
tasks: fix a choppy drawer animation
find why a hover animation stutters on phones
replace layout-property animations with transform and opacity
decide between CSS and Motion for a page transition
review a React component that animates through state
qualityWhy: The skill gives an ordered diagnostic workflow, a symptom table, concrete before-and-after code, and a reporting template that an agent can follow step by step.
why: It directly serves building and polishing web frontends on a node, and it is stack-free enough to apply to the node's Next.js and React setup without adaptation. Some findings need a recording on a real device, which the agent cannot produce on its own, and the version-specific Motion advice may age as libraries change.

summary: This skill guides an agent through checking a website's search visibility, covering both classic search engines and AI answer engines. It can run a free technical audit of a page's title, description, headings, schema, robots.txt and sitemap, and it can gather keyword and SERP data from the DataForSEO API. It also explains how to write JSON-LD structured data and how to make content easier for AI engines to cite. The people it serves are site owners, marketers and builders who want more traffic from search.
tasks: audit my site's SEO and technical health
add FAQ or Article schema markup to a page
find keyword ideas and search volume for a blog post
check whether AI crawlers like GPTBot can reach my site
compare my keywords against a competitor's
qualityWhy: The instructions are concrete, with runnable scripts, templates and validation steps, but several performance figures are presented without sources and the script descriptions are a little inconsistent.
needs: DataForSEO account with DATAFORSEO_LOGIN and DATAFORSEO_PASSWORD (paid, needed for keyword, SERP, competitor and backlink scripts)
why: Site search visibility is directly useful for a node that hosts websites and content. The free audit script works without a key, but keyword, SERP, competitor and backlink work needs a paid DataForSEO account. Some of the quoted visibility percentages are unverified claims and should be treated with caution.

summary: This skill lets an agent explore Clerk's Backend REST API: list spec versions and tags, read endpoint schemas, and run authenticated requests for users, organizations, invitations and metadata. It is aimed at developers who manage authentication and user accounts for a web product. It also includes a delete-user action that is flagged as permanent.
tasks: list all users created in the last 7 days
create an organization and invite a member as admin
update a user's public metadata plan
look up the schema of a Clerk API endpoint
qualityWhy: The file gives concrete curl templates, mandatory safety checks, a metadata-overwrite warning and spec-extraction scripts, though it has some inconsistent guidance about scopes and no explicit verification steps.
why: Clerk is a cloud sign-in and user-management service, which the node's rules classify as a cloud backend, so value is none and the skill is skipped. It also uses a Clerk secret key and calls a third-party cloud API for user data.

summary: The skill guides an agent through Clerk authentication patterns in Next.js: choosing server versus client auth APIs, protecting routes and Server Actions, handling API route 401 versus 403 responses, caching per user, and wrapping auth-dependent UI in Suspense for Cache Components builds. It also covers custom JWTs for external APIs and manual token verification for standalone servers. It is aimed at developers who already use Clerk for sign-in in a Next.js app.
tasks: protect a Next.js page or Server Action with Clerk
fix next build errors with auth under Cache Components
pass a Clerk JWT to an external API
show content based on Clerk roles or permissions
qualityWhy: The instructions are concrete, with code examples, a decision table of references, and a pitfalls table, though the references were not fully reviewed.
needs: Clerk account with NEXT_PUBLIC_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY and CLERK_SECRET_KEY
why: Node auth is its own sign-in element based on next-auth, so the Clerk-specific APIs (auth(), useAuth, Clerk middleware) do not fit the node's stack and the skill must be adapted to next-auth before use; the Next.js caching and Suspense patterns are still useful ideas.

summary: Guides an agent through creating, running and maintaining end-to-end tests and reusable modules for Android and iOS apps on the Momentic platform. It covers v2 YAML editing rules, live device validation through MCP tools, caching and timing behavior, and troubleshooting device, infrastructure and assertion failures. It is aimed at QA engineers who test mobile apps.
tasks: write an end-to-end test for a mobile login flow
fix a failing Android test in CI
create a reusable module for onboarding steps
validate a checkout flow on an iOS simulator
qualityWhy: The file gives concrete workflows, file-format rules, pitfalls and troubleshooting steps, though it defers many syntax details to external links and tool descriptions.
needs: Android or iOS device, simulator or emulator
why: It is a testing skill for mobile apps, not for building, running or selling a web product, so it does not serve what a Fractera node is for. It also depends on Momentic's cloud-hosted remote devices and managed app channels, which fits the cloud-service rule for skipping.

summary: This skill teaches an agent to write webhook endpoints that receive Clerk's lifecycle events, such as user, organization, session, and billing changes, and verifies each delivery's signature before acting on it. It covers syncing Clerk data into an app's own database, sending notifications, and testing locally through the Clerk CLI. The audience is developers who already use Clerk for sign-in and want their backend to react to account changes.
tasks: sync Clerk users into my app database
send a welcome email when someone signs up
react to organization membership changes
test Clerk webhooks on localhost
handle subscription and payment events from Clerk billing
qualityWhy: The SKILL.md gives complete, runnable handlers, a payload reference, a pitfalls table and a testing flow, though the referenced frameworks file was not visible to judge.
needs: Resend API key (only for the email example)
Slack webhook URL (only for the notification example)
why: It is built around Clerk, a cloud sign-in and identity service that the node replaces with its own sign-in element and local SQLite, so it does not serve local-first building. Its handlers would depend on a hosted backend's event feed.

summary: This skill teaches an agent to find, install and customize shadcn/ui components, which are copied into the project as editable source rather than imported from a library. It covers the CLI commands, the cn() class-merging helper, variant styling, theme variables, and composing blocks such as login forms and dashboards. It is aimed at frontend developers building React applications on the node.
tasks: add a login form to a Next.js page
build a sortable data table
change the theme colors in globals.css
set up shadcn/ui in an existing project
wrap a shadcn button with a loading state
qualityWhy: It gives concrete commands, code samples, a setup check script and a troubleshooting list, but some parts are generic and the Tailwind 3 setup guidance is out of date for Tailwind 4.
why: shadcn/ui is part of the node's own frontend stack, so this directly serves building application UI. The Tailwind 3 references (tailwind.config.js, @tailwind directives) and the verify script that checks for tailwind.config.js do not match a Tailwind 4 node, so an agent must check those against the node's real setup before following them.

summary: This skill lets an agent query a WeChat Reading account through a remote gateway: searching the book store, listing the bookshelf, reading stats, personal notes and highlights, public reviews, and recommendations. It is aimed at a reader who wants their reading history and notes handled from a chat. The visible file sets strict rules for parameters, pagination, timestamps and links, and points to separate reference files for each area.
tasks: search for a book and show its details
export my highlights and notes from a book
summarise my reading time this month
recommend books similar to one I like
qualityWhy: The visible SKILL.md gives concrete request examples, pagination rules, field-interpretation priority and display formats, but the referenced files were not included, so completeness cannot be fully confirmed.
why: It is a personal reading assistant rather than something for building sites, apps or content, so the value is only occasional; it also depends on a remote Tencent gateway that holds the user's reading data. It is marked skip because it tells the agent to pause and follow any upgrade_info.message returned by the server, which could direct the agent to run unverified remote instructions.
risks: Instructs the agent to obey server-supplied upgrade_info.message immediately, which could lead to downloading and running unverified remote code.

summary: The skill guides an agent through SEO work on a rendered site: running Lighthouse SEO and Agentic Browsing checks, inspecting robots.txt, sitemaps, canonicals and headers, then fixing titles, meta descriptions, headings, images, links and structured data. It is written for web developers and site owners who want technical and on-page search fixes. It stresses not promising ranking changes and reporting that search-engine validation is still pending.
tasks: improve SEO for my website
fix missing or duplicate meta tags
add JSON-LD structured data to product pages
review sitemap and robots.txt setup
run an SEO audit with Lighthouse
qualityWhy: Concrete examples, checklists and reference links are given, with sensible caveats about what SEO checks can prove, though some sections stay generic.
why: It directly serves building and running a site, and it is a stack-free set of web guidance rather than a replacement for the node's stack. Some items such as Search Console and Screaming Frog are optional outside tools, and it depends on Lighthouse being available, which is a doubt rather than a blocker.

summary: This skill guides an AI agent through writing a long-form book by calling a hosted Proseify tool server. The agent first confirms whether the author wants a novel or a novella, picks a genre, and reads that genre's style guidance. It then searches a public-domain text collection for sample passages, plans the chapters, drafts every chapter in order, and runs a self-edit pass with checks for weak prose. The target audience is authors and small publishers who want fiction that does not read like generic AI output.
tasks: write a full novel of about 80,000 words
draft a novella chapter by chapter
revise a manuscript to remove generic AI prose
check a book's chapters for thin or summarised content
qualityWhy: The skill gives a clear ordered workflow, a per-chapter checklist, and named pitfalls, but its core steps depend entirely on the vendor's tools and some editing rules are subjective.
why: It serves book writing, which is a form of content making, but only for authors who want long-form fiction, so the value is occasional rather than central. It needs a paid or keyed Proseify service, and the manuscript and planning requests go to that outside server, which the skill does not state plainly.

summary: This skill teaches an agent how to set up and manage Clerk Organizations for multi-tenant and B2B apps. It covers org switching, role and permission checks, member invitations, verified domains, and enterprise SSO, and it asks the developer before turning the feature on. It is aimed at developers building team workspaces and per-company products on a Clerk-authenticated app.
tasks: add team workspaces with org switching to an app
gate admin pages with org roles and permissions
invite teammates to a company account
set up enterprise SSO for a customer organization
qualityWhy: The instructions are concrete, with code samples, CLI commands, error tables and checks, though they are long and lean on external reference files.
why: Node's own sign-in is next-auth 5, not Clerk, so this skill is built for a different auth stack and must be adapted to the node's roles before use. Its hosted user, org and SSO data lives in Clerk's cloud, which conflicts with the local-first design, so it is only useful as a reference for ideas.

summary: This skill turns an agent into a design studio that makes high-fidelity HTML prototypes, 1920×1080 slide decks, timeline-driven animations and videos, infographics, and social-media image sets such as Xiaohongshu cards. Before building, the agent must present three design directions as real drafts and wait for the person to pick one. It also tells the agent to check facts and brand assets first, and to run lint checks and save a short list of the person's taste preferences. The skill is aimed at designers and content makers who want output that does not look AI-generated.
tasks: make a clickable HTML prototype for a landing page
build a 1920×1080 slide deck for a pitch
create a 15-second promo animation and export it as MP4
design a Xiaohongshu image carousel with cover
review an existing design and score how good it looks
qualityWhy: The SKILL.md gives clear steps, gates, checks and fallbacks, but it points to many reference and script files that are not included in the bundle, so parts cannot be followed as provided.
why: It directly serves making prototypes, decks, animations and social posts, which a Fractera node is for, and its output is standalone HTML and media files kept locally. The 'install' rating assumes the scripts and reference files exist; the bundle only includes SKILL.md, so the Python tools and the direction-review workflow are unverified. It also says production web apps are out of scope, so it fits the node's design work rather than replacing its Next.js stack.

summary: This skill helps an agent design, adapt and schedule recurring marketing workflows that run on a cadence, such as weekly SEO scans, ad-fatigue checks, churn watches and reply triage. It guides the agent to define a trigger, bounded steps, a self-check, state handling and a stop condition for each loop, and to add human checkpoints before anything publishes or spends. It is written for marketers and founders who want always-on marketing systems.
tasks: set up a weekly marketing review
run an ad fatigue check every few days
watch for churn signals daily
run my SEO on a daily schedule
triage outbound replies
qualityWhy: The SKILL.md gives a clear anatomy, cadence rules, guardrails pointers and anti-patterns, with a large catalog and templates in reference files, though the body itself defers many details to those files.
why: It is stack-free planning guidance for recurring marketing work, useful now and then for a product's marketing, but it is not a build tool for the node's app code. Its loop bodies call other marketing skills and may point to ad, email or social services that the person would need to pick and authorise themselves.

summary: This skill lets an agent read cell values from a Google Sheets spreadsheet through the gws command-line tool, using a spreadsheet ID and a range such as Sheet1!A1:D10 or a whole sheet name. It is read-only and does not change the file. It is aimed at people who keep working data in Google Sheets and want an agent to pull it into a report, script or other process. Advanced options fall back to the raw values.get API.
tasks: read values from a Google Sheet
pull rows from a spreadsheet range
fetch sheet data for a report
qualityWhy: It gives a usage line, a flag table and two examples, but it is short and depends on the unseen gws-shared file for auth and setup.
needs: Google account with access to the spreadsheet
why: The data lives in a cloud spreadsheet service rather than on the person's own computer, so under the local-first rule it counts as no value for a node. The skill is read-only and carries no risk, but the cloud dependency is the reason for skipping it.

summary: This skill tells an agent to run a full quality review of a whole code repository, or of a folder the user names. The agent maps the project, traces the main data flows, and looks for bugs, security holes, problems under heavy load, missing tests, slow spots and code that could be removed. It reports findings in plain English, ranked by importance, with a concrete fix for each. It changes no code.
tasks: audit my repo for bugs and security holes
check whether my code holds up under many users
find code I can delete or simplify
list the missing tests for risky logic
qualityWhy: The instructions are concrete, with ordered steps, a finding format, evidence rules and an output template, though they leave the review process to the agent's own judgment.
why: It is stack-free and useful now and then for reviewing code a node builds, but it does not make content or run products directly. It only reads code and writes a report, so it is safe to install as written.

summary: This skill lets an agent run live web and image searches through Volcengine's Doubao search API and answer from the results with cited sources. It covers when to search, which filters to use for time range, source authority and query rewriting, and how to handle missing keys, rate limits and quota errors. It is written for an agent that needs current facts, prices, policies or claims checked before answering.
tasks: look up the latest news or prices on a topic
verify a claim and cite sources
find images or logos for a design
compare two products using current information
qualityWhy: The instructions are detailed on parameters, routing and error codes, but they are mostly in Chinese, padded with marketing and repeated links, and the referenced script and reference files are missing from the bundle.
needs: Volcengine Doubao search API key (WEB_SEARCH_API_KEY) or an Agent Plan account
why: Live web search is useful for an agent that writes content or answers questions about current facts, but it is not core to building a product, so the value is 'some'. It needs a Volcengine key and a free quota of 500 calls a month, which the person chooses to use. The script could not be checked because only SKILL.md was provided, and the text demands verbatim output and claims priority over all other instructions, which an agent should not obey blindly.

summary: This skill lets an agent add plain text to the end of an existing Google Doc by calling the gws command-line tool with a document ID. It is a small reference: one command, two required flags, and a note that rich formatting needs the raw batchUpdate API. It is aimed at people who keep documents in Google Workspace and want to script simple appends. The skill also asks the agent to confirm with the user before running the write.
tasks: append a line of text to a Google Doc
add a new paragraph to the end of a document
log entries into a shared Google Docs file
qualityWhy: It is a short reference that covers one command and points to a shared skill for auth and flags that are not included, so an agent cannot follow it fully from its own files.
why: Google Docs is a cloud office suite and the document lives in Google's cloud, not on the node's local files, so it does not serve building, running or making content on a local-first node. The skill also depends on an external gws CLI and the Google account credentials that the shared skill provides.

summary: This skill lets an agent check a person's upcoming Google Calendar events across all their calendars, for today, tomorrow, the coming week, or a set number of days. It can filter to one calendar and convert times to a chosen timezone. The agent only reads the schedule and never changes events. It is aimed at personal schedule checks rather than building or running a product.
tasks: show my events for today
list what is on my calendar this week
check my agenda for the next three days
see tomorrow's meetings on my Work calendar
qualityWhy: The file gives a usage line, a flag table and examples, but it is short and defers auth and global flags to another skill, so an agent gets little guidance on output or errors.
why: This is a personal productivity task on a cloud calendar service, not something for building, running, selling or making content for a product, so its value is none. It is also a Google cloud service, which the local-first rule marks as skip.

summary: This skill lets an agent send a local file to Google Drive from the command line, optionally placing it in a chosen folder and renaming it. The MIME type is detected automatically, and the filename is taken from the local path unless a new name is given. It is aimed at people who keep their files in Google Drive and want an agent to move files there. The skill itself is a short reference for one upload command.
tasks: upload a report to a Google Drive folder
rename a file while uploading it to Drive
push a CSV export into a shared Drive folder
qualityWhy: It gives a clear usage line, a flag table and examples, but it is a thin reference with no error handling or verification steps.
needs: Google account with Drive access through gws authentication
why: Google Drive is a cloud file store, which the node's local-first design excludes, so the skill is not useful for building or running a node. The skill also depends on the gws command-line tool and a Google account, and its only purpose is to send files to Google's servers.

summary: This skill guides an agent through hardening a Better Auth setup: managing the signing secret, configuring rate limits for sign-in and sign-up, and setting trusted origins and CSRF protection. It also covers session expiry, cookie attributes, OAuth token encryption, IP tracking and audit logging through database hooks. It is aimed at developers who run their own login system and want to prevent brute-force attacks and misconfiguration.
tasks: harden the login system against brute force attacks
configure secure session and cookie settings
set trusted origins for a multi-domain app
add audit logging for sign-ins and account changes
encrypt stored OAuth tokens
qualityWhy: The skill gives concrete configuration snippets, default values, and a pre-deployment checklist, though a few examples reference undefined helpers such as waitUntil and it has no verification steps.
why: Fractera handles sign-in with its own element built on next-auth 5, so Better Auth itself is a replaced stack and the agent should only borrow the security principles (rate limits, origin checks, cookie hardening, audit hooks) and apply them to next-auth. The skill is useful for security thinking, but it is not directly installable on a node.

summary: This skill acts as the main entry point for an analytics instrumentation pipeline. Given a pull request, branch, file, directory, or a plain-language feature description, it reads the relevant code, finds user-facing actions worth tracking, and produces a tracking plan with file locations, tracking calls and event properties. It is aimed at developers who want to add product analytics to code changes.
tasks: instrument this PR with analytics events
add tracking to the checkout flow
what analytics events does this file need
produce a tracking plan for the onboarding feature

summary: This skill lets an agent audit a website's search-engine basics: page titles, meta descriptions, headings, canonical tags, robots directives, structured data, image alt text and internal links. compare my pages against target keywords

why: It is useful for running and maintaining sites, but it audits external pages through a hosted scraping service rather than building the node's own data. It is installable as written once the person supplies their own Firecrawl key, and optional Alexandria measurements need separate provider terms that the skill says must be approved by a person.

summary: This skill lets an agent read an article, find the places where a picture would help, and plan one illustration per place. It calls an outside image generation service, which the person chooses and must set up. Only SKILL.md was reviewed; the other reference and script files were not checked for hidden behaviour.

summary: This skill guides an agent to write and review interface copy, covering labels, error messages, empty states, confirmations and status text. summary: The skill guides a salesperson or sales agent through handling objections in live conversations. It covers price, timing, competitor, authority and trust objections for B2B and B2C, with separate guidance on price triage and compliance limits.

build an objection library for a sales team
decide whether to disqualify a stalled deal

why: It is a stack-free sales method that a node could use to help build sales content or a sales-focused product, but it is aimed at human sales reps on calls rather than building or running a site, app, or agent, so its use on a node is occasional. Its references to other skills in the mbfinotti/sales-skills set would need those installed, and its advice on a 'humanizer' pass and on rehearsal is advisory only.

summary: This skill builds a sequenced discovery question set for a sales call: pain, root cause, impact and urgency, sized to the call length, with follow-up ladders, branch triggers and a list of questions to avoid. It serves sales reps and founders preparing B2B first meetings and high-ticket B2C consultations. The agent asks the user a short interview first, then assembles a call sheet from the bundled reference files.

list follow-up questions for a prospect who gives vague answers

why: Sales discovery prep is a direct business task for people selling products on a node, and the skill is a stack-free planning and writing aid with no outside service. It is mostly methodology, so an agent gets no code or data benefit beyond the call sheet itself.

summary: This skill tells an agent to run the gws command-line tool to produce a weekly digest for a Google Workspace user, combining the calendar agenda for the current week with a count of unread email. It is read-only and offers table or JSON output. It serves a person who wants a quick overview of their personal schedule and inbox. count my unread emails
get a weekly digest of calendar and inbox

why: A personal calendar and inbox digest is not for building, running, selling or making content for a product, so value is none and use is skip. It depends on a Google account and the gws CLI, which is outside the local-first stack.

summary: The skill plans a touch-by-touch outbound sales cadence: which channel and day for each step, how many touches and how far apart, multi-threading across contacts at one account, exit and suppression rules, recycling after a cooldown, and the capacity arithmetic behind it. summary: This skill lets an agent run the gws command-line tool to pull today's calendar events and open tasks from a Google account and combine them into a standup summary. why: This is personal office productivity built on Google Workspace, which does not serve building, running, selling or making content for a product, and it depends on a cloud service holding the person's calendar and tasks, so it is skipped rather than installed on a local-first node.

summary: This persona lets an agent act as a project manager inside Google Workspace. summary: This skill guides an agent to turn the buyer signals a salesperson supplies, such as funding rounds, hires, launches, reviews or consumer behaviour, into two or three ranked reasons to reach out. summary: The skill guides an agent through reviewing one completed sales call from its transcript, scoring opener, discovery, objection handling and close against anchored 0-4 behavioural descriptors, with every judgement backed by a verbatim quote. why: It is a sales-process skill with no stack, so it is not about building, running or making content for a product on a local node; it is not relevant to a site, web app, AI agent or media workflow. It is a sales-process skill for reps, which the node is not built for, so it is marked skip.

The references it links (capacity math, fair-share allocation, validation checks) were not in the files shown to me, so their content is unverified, and its benchmark figures are cited as current but may age.

summary: This recipe tells an agent how to find a file in Google Drive, give a specific person read access to it, and email that person a link with a short message. summary: Gives an agent a method for designing how a sales team groups and scores its accounts: choosing which signal layers (firmographic, technographic, intent, usage) define fit, building a weighted fit score calibrated against closed-won deals, keeping fit and readiness as separate axes, mapping expansion whitespace inside existing customers, and encoding the model in the CRM. qualityWhy: The file is a clear set of best-practice rules but gives no concrete example Dockerfile, no build or verification steps, and little per-language guidance, so an agent has to fill in the details itself.

summary: This skill gives an agent a catalogue of 40 NestJS rules grouped into ten categories such as architecture, dependency injection, security, performance and testing, each with incorrect and correct code examples. qualityWhy: The SKILL.md gives a clear priority table and a concise rule index with per-rule files containing examples, though the individual rule files were not reviewed here, so completeness is inferred from the index.
why: Fractera nodes use Next.js and their own Blocks and next-auth stack, not NestJS, so the skill is useful only as reference for backend ideas and must be adapted to the node's stack rather than installed as written. summary: This skill tells an agent to pull names, email addresses and phone numbers from a Google Workspace domain directory and write them into a Google Sheets spreadsheet using the gws command-line tool. why: It copies a cloud contact directory into another cloud service (Google Sheets), so it does not keep data on the person's own computer and falls under the cloud-service rule for value none. The skill also copies other people's personal data out of the directory, which the node should not do without a clear reason.

summary: The skill guides an agent through designing REST and GraphQL APIs: resource-oriented URLs, HTTP method semantics, versioning choices, pagination, error formats and deprecation. summary: The skill guides an agent through diagnosing how an already chosen topic should become content. summary: This skill lets an agent fetch a web page with a local headless Chrome and turn it into clean markdown, optionally saving it with its images and videos beside the file. summary: The skill guides an agent through listing a person's Google Tasks lists and then pulling the unfinished tasks from them, so overdue items can be spotted and ranked. summary: This skill tells an agent to search a Gmail account for messages carrying a chosen label, read the content of a message, and send it on to another address with a new subject and body. summary: The skill makes an agent take a vague business term, phrase or quoted sentence and break it apart: what different speakers mean by it, where it gets misused, what its limits are, and a plain-language restatement. summary: This skill lets an agent create a feedback survey in Google Forms from the command line and then email its link to a list of recipients through Gmail. summary: This skill walks an agent through setting up a post-mortem after an incident: it creates a Google Docs template with Summary, Timeline, Root Cause and Action Items sections, books a one-hour Google Calendar review with the team, and posts a short notice to a Google Chat space. It tells the agent how to list and read the examples from GitHub, check deprecated and renamed entries, and merge dependencies and config without overwriting the user's setup. It is aimed at developers building mobile apps with Expo.

The skill itself has no harmful steps, and its feedback command sends reports to an external Expo CLI only when the agent chooses to.

summary: The skill guides an agent through designing or reviewing a PostgreSQL-specific schema: choosing key strategies, column types, constraints, indexes, and partitioning. It also covers gotchas such as unquoted identifier casing, NULL handling in unique constraints, and missing foreign-key indexes. Its detailed reference file adds data-type catalogs, JSONB indexing, workload patterns, and extensions. The audience is developers who need a sound relational data model for an application.
tasks: design a PostgreSQL schema for a new app
review existing table definitions for indexing and constraint problems
choose data types for money, timestamps and IDs
plan partitioning for a large events table
qualityWhy: Concrete rules, a type-avoidance table, worked DDL examples and a pointer to a detailed reference, though it gives few explicit review checklists or step-by-step procedures.
why: Schema design knowledge is useful for a node, but the node's data lives in its own SQLite element, so PostgreSQL-specific rules such as TIMESTAMPTZ, identity columns, partitioning and extensions do not apply directly and must be adapted to SQLite. The skill is therefore read for its ideas rather than installed as written.

summary: This skill makes an agent reformat a plain text or markdown article so a reader can scan it: it adds headings, bold key lines, lists, tables and code markers without changing the author's words. It also fills in frontmatter with a title chosen from several hook options, plus a summary and description. It then runs a local typography script for CJK/English spacing, emphasis and optional quote fixes, and writes the result to a new file. It suits people preparing blog posts, articles or landing copy.

generate a title, summary and description for article frontmatter

why: It works on local markdown files for writing and publishing content, with no cloud service involved. The scripts use bun or npx, which pulls the npm packages (including autocorrect-node) at run time; these are ordinary local tool dependencies and not a risk, but the person should know that packages are fetched from the npm registry.

summary: This skill guides an agent through connecting to an iOS simulator via argent MCP tools. why: The skill is useful only for iOS simulator testing of mobile apps, which a Fractera node does not do for building or running sites, web apps, agents, or content, so its value is none. It depends on an external MCP toolset rather than the node's own stack, and the node's use cases do not need it.

summary: This skill tells a coding agent to write the expected product behavior as Momentic end-to-end tests before implementing a feature, so the tests act as the contract the code must satisfy. decide which Momentic tests a code change affects
prepare test data for a durable end-to-end checkpoint

It is built around Momentic, which is an external testing platform and not one of the node's own elements, so an agent should read it for the test-first habit and apply it with the node's own testing setup rather than install it as written.

It assumes the argent toolset (debugger-status, list-devices and others) is present, so the agent needs those tools to follow it fully.

why: It helps test and drive apps a node builds, which is useful now and then rather than core to building or running sites; it is local device control with no cloud service and no install-time command, so it can be installed as written. The skill only describes the argent MCP tools and does not itself call an outside service.

summary: This skill tells an agent to check a hosted brand guide before making or reviewing anything branded as Warp or Oz, covering visual style, colors, typography, voice, naming and components. Its real content lives on an external page the skill tells the agent to treat as the source of truth, so the outcome depends on what that page says, which I could not check from these files.

summary: Builds a local, self-contained D3 walkthrough page that helps a reviewer orient to a pull request through four toggleable canvas views: system overview, data flow, code dependencies and user actions. summary: This skill guides an agent through profiling a React Native Hermes app on a simulator to measure re-renders and CPU cost, using the argent profiler tools. Some interaction and profiler tools are not described in this file and need the argent project to exist.

summary: The skill guides an agent through building a single-file horizontal-swipe web slide deck with presenter mode, speaker notes, audience-screen sync and image layouts. summary: This skill guides an agent through testing an iOS or Android app's UI by repeating a loop of acting on the screen, capturing screenshots, and checking results using argent MCP tools. summary: This skill guides an agent through profiling a running iOS simulator or Android app for native CPU hotspots, UI hangs and memory leaks. summary: This skill lets an agent generate text and images through Google Gemini's web interface, using the person's own signed-in Google account rather than an official API key. summary: The skill turns an agent into a documentation writer that follows the Diátaxis framework, sorting every document into one of four types: tutorial, how-to guide, reference, or explanation. summary: This skill tells an agent to convene a small council of subagents, each on a different AI model and with a different angle, to examine the same technical question in parallel. summary: This skill checks a piece of Chinese writing for signs that it was produced by an AI, and reports each flagged passage with its quote, the problem, and a severity level. why: It is useful for reviewing written content such as posts, articles and video scripts, but it is a text-review habit rather than something that builds or runs a site, so it is occasional rather than central; it needs no outside services and is stack-free, so it can be installed as written.

summary: This skill guides an agent through auditing and fixing animation performance in UI code. summary: This skill is a reference index of Vue 3 debugging guides: each entry maps a symptom (a warning, a null ref, a stale value, a hydration mismatch) to a short markdown note explaining the cause and fix. summary: The skill turns a topic into a discussion among several thinkers, each standing for a distinct theory such as a decision framework or a mental model. summary: The skill guides an agent through Docker container work: reviewing Dockerfiles and Compose files, building multi-stage images, hardening containers with non-root users and secrets handling, shrinking image size, and diagnosing build, network and healthcheck problems. summary: This skill acts as a router for a 31-skill advertising collection: it detects whether a project is new or existing, runs a capped interview, and sends the paid-ads task to the one matching sibling skill or says none fits. summary: This skill guides an agent through designing a multi-stage retargeting sequence for ad campaigns, using the site's own conversion-lag data to set recency windows, behavioural-depth tiers, message and offer ladders, mutually exclusive audiences with exclusion rules, and per-stage frequency caps. The skill's hand-offs point to other skills in another package that the node does not have, and it is a planning aid, not a build tool.

summary: This skill guides an agent through reconciling the numbers reported by ad platforms, analytics tools, and the system of record (a CRM for B2B or an order system for B2C). It asks the agent to normalize both sides to a common basis, sort every unit of the gap into timing, definitional, or unexplained residual, and report the residual without forcing it to zero. The output is a structured report with a variance table, defect list with owners, and known deltas for future periods, aimed at marketing analysts and media buyers.

It names no cloud service, and its cited benchmarks are self-reported heuristics the agent should treat as triage aids, not standards.

summary: This skill walks an agent through choosing which paid advertising channel families a business should fund for a new campaign. It ends with one funded primary channel, a funding-floor check, a test with pass and kill rules, and a measurement plan. The intended users are founders and marketers choosing a first or next paid channel for B2B or B2C offers.

Its benchmark figures are directional and vendor-sourced, so an agent should verify current numbers before committing spend; it also points to sibling skills in another repository for adjacent steps.

summary: This skill helps a marketing leader or founder plan a hire for a paid-advertising role. summary: This skill walks a developer through pull request review comments one at a time, collecting a decision for each (fix, explain, acknowledge, or custom). summary: This skill makes an agent run a very strict code-quality review of a branch's changes, looking for needless complexity, oversized files, tangled conditionals and weak type boundaries. summary: This skill gives an agent a checklist of modern JavaScript habits: const by default, arrow functions, destructuring, async/await over promise chains, immutable updates, optional chaining, and pure functions.
