The code imports from a Starchild-specific sidecar proxy and a /data/workspace path, so it must be adapted to the node's own stack before use, which makes it ideas rather than install.

summary: The skill guides an agent through a due-diligence score for a single crypto token contract address on GMGN's chains, combining contract safety, holder concentration and price action into a 0-100 composite. It is written for traders or researchers who want a verdict rather than raw data fields. The instructions are very detailed, with explicit thresholds, field-unit warnings and fallback rules for missing data.
tasks: score this token contract address for safety
check whether this token is a honeypot or rug
give this coin a due-diligence score
is this token safe to buy
qualityWhy: The file is very concrete, with named fields, thresholds, measured examples and explicit handling of missing data, though it is long and dense.
why: It is built around GMGN's crypto token data service, a cloud data source outside the node, and it scores trading risk rather than building or making content for a product, so it is not useful for a local-first Fractera node.

summary: The skill lets an agent remove background noise, music and ambience from an audio recording and keep only the speech or vocals, using the ElevenLabs audio isolation endpoint. It is aimed at people cleaning up interviews, podcasts, field recordings or mixed tracks, and at preparing audio before transcription or voice conversion. Code examples are given in Python, JavaScript and CLI form, with parameters, a URL input example and common error codes.
tasks: clean up a noisy interview recording
isolate the voice from a track with music
prepare noisy audio for transcription
extract dialogue from a field recording
qualityWhy: Clear steps, runnable examples in three languages, parameter table, error codes and workflows, with small gaps such as no guidance on output length limits or file size.
why: Useful for making and cleaning audio content for a product, but it calls the paid ElevenLabs service and needs the person's key; the returned file is written back to local disk. The setup step runs an npx command that signs the user in and stores a key for the project, which the person should expect.

summary: This skill guides an agent through planning an MSW (MapleStory Worlds) game from scratch or resuming a phased build. It asks guided questions, matches the idea to a genre catalog with map types and mechanics, writes a game design document and milestone roadmap as markdown, and tracks per-phase task states. It also ships a local web decision sheet, opened through a small packer script, for design-shaping choices.
tasks: plan a new MSW game from scratch
write a game design document for a prototype
resume an in-progress game build
scope an MVP for a game idea
track phase progress and milestone roadmap
qualityWhy: The SKILL.md is very detailed with explicit steps, gates, file conventions, and checks, backed by reference documents for each stage.
why: It serves building games on MSW, which fits the node's purpose of building products, but it is a game-planning skill rather than a web or content stack, so value is some. It is stack-free apart from MSW itself, so use is install; the packer script serves only the local Docs/web folder and needs no keys.

summary: This skill teaches an agent how to configure and troubleshoot Vite projects: the config file, plugins, environment variables, dev-server proxies, HMR, library publishing, dependency pre-bundling and production build tuning. It is aimed at developers who run Vite as their front-end build tool. Its guidance includes warnings about type-checking gaps and about exposing secrets through VITE_ variables.
tasks: configure vite.config.ts for a React app
set up a dev server proxy to a backend API
publish a TypeScript library with Vite library mode
diagnose a slow Vite dev server or broken production build
qualityWhy: It gives concrete config examples, a plugin table, env-variable rules, and a list of pitfalls and anti-patterns an agent can follow, though some version claims are unverified and parts are thin.
why: Vite is a build tool a Fractera node does not use, since its stack is Next.js 16, so the agent should read these patterns for ideas and apply them only to Vite projects the person brings. The security notes on VITE_ variables are useful in any front-end project.

summary: This skill tells an agent how to look up App Store Connect identifiers such as app, build, version, IAP, subscription, TestFlight group, tester and review submission IDs using the asc command-line tool. It is aimed at developers who ship iOS apps and need those IDs before running other asc commands. It gives the list and info commands to run, along with output-format and pagination tips.
tasks: find the App Store Connect ID for my app
get the latest build number for version 1.2.3
list TestFlight testers and groups for an app
resolve subscription and IAP version IDs for review
qualityWhy: It gives concrete, copy-ready commands for many resource types with flags and output tips, but it has no examples of expected output and no error-handling steps.
needs: App Store Connect account credentials configured for the asc tool
why: The skill is entirely about Apple's cloud App Store Connect service, which is cloud administration rather than building, running or making content on a local node, so it falls under the cloud administration rule and is marked skip.

summary: This skill guides an agent through building a visual novel: a branching script with text, choices and flags, character and background display, and player conveniences such as save-anywhere, backlog, skip and auto-advance. It is aimed at developers making dating sims or branching story games. It works as a compositional playbook that hands the dialogue engine and UI work to other skills, and it includes a Ren'Py note.
tasks: build a branching visual novel
add typewriter text with skip and backlog
design story flags and choice routes
add save-anywhere to a dating sim
qualityWhy: It gives concrete patterns, pitfalls and engine-specific notes, though the code is pseudocode and the references file is only pointed to.
why: It is a game-genre playbook for local game projects, not for the web stack a Fractera node runs (Next.js, SQLite), so it is useful only for a game built inside the node and the code must be rewritten for the node's stack. It relies on Godot, Unity and Ren'Py, which are not part of the node.

summary: This skill guides an agent through writing and fixing Unity 6 gameplay scripts in C#, covering MonoBehaviour callbacks, cached component lookups, Inspector-exposed fields, and coroutines. It also bundles a read-only Python checker that looks for broken .meta GUIDs and missing script references after files are changed outside the Unity Editor. The intended users are game developers working in Unity.
tasks: write a player controller script in Unity
fix a null reference or lifecycle bug in a MonoBehaviour
add coroutine-based timed behaviour to a Unity object
check a Unity project for broken .meta files and GUIDs
qualityWhy: The skill gives a clear workflow, concrete code patterns, a pitfalls list and a runnable checker with documented exit codes, though the checker's full source was cut off in the files shown.
why: Unity is a game engine, and nodes are built for web apps, sites, AI agents and content, so the skill serves none of the node's purposes and its Unity stack does not match the node's Next.js stack. The skill itself is local-first with no cloud service, key or network call, so the only reason to skip it is scope.

summary: The skill walks an agent through moving a JavaScript or TypeScript project from ESLint to Oxlint, a Rust-based linter. It runs an official migration tool that converts the ESLint flat config into an oxlint config, then checks the mapped plugins and unmigrated rules, installs the oxlint packages, and updates CI scripts and editor setup. It is aimed at developers maintaining linting for their own codebases.
tasks: migrate my project from ESLint to Oxlint
convert my eslint config to oxlintrc
replace eslint commands in CI with oxlint
check which ESLint rules did not migrate
qualityWhy: It gives concrete commands, option tables, a plugin mapping and a step-by-step checklist, with a few gaps such as no verification step after migration.
why: It is a stack-free developer-tooling guide for a JS/TS project and needs no account or key; it helps the node only when the person maintains a JS/TS project, not for the node's core product tasks. The migration tool and oxlint are installed from npm, which is standard for this kind of project.

summary: The skill walks an agent through publishing a game on Steam: setting up the Steamworks app, depots and packages, checking SteamPipe build scripts, uploading builds with steamcmd, and moving a build live on branches through store and build review. It is aimed at game developers shipping a finished title to Steam. A bundled read-only Python checker validates app_build VDF scripts before upload.
tasks: publish my game on Steam
set up depots and a beta branch for a Steam build
upload a build with steamcmd
check my app_build vdf script before uploading
run the Steam release checklist
qualityWhy: Concrete steps, VDF examples, pitfalls and a working validator script with clear exit codes, though some review timings and fees need checking against current Steam docs.
needs: Steam build account with Steam Guard
why: Steam is a third-party storefront with its own hosted build and distribution pipeline, which the local-first node is not built around, so the skill is out of scope for a node's own publishing. Its only real use is shipping a game to an external cloud store, which the value rules class as none.
risks: The skill tells the agent to pass a build account password on the steamcmd command line, which exposes credentials in shell history and process lists.

summary: The skill walks an agent through installing the official open-source Google Ads MCP server with pipx, checking Python and pipx first, then setting the five Google Ads credentials as environment variables. It also covers connecting Claude Desktop, Cursor or Antigravity to the server, testing it, and listing its three read-only tools. The guide is aimed at developers who want an AI assistant to pull Google Ads campaign data and reports in plain language. A Cloud Run deployment section is included but is not the main path.
tasks: connect my AI assistant to my Google Ads account
list my Google Ads campaigns and their status
pull impressions and metrics for enabled campaigns
set up the google-ads-mcp server with pipx
qualityWhy: The steps, commands, checks and troubleshooting are concrete and complete, though a few sections are repetitive and the Cursor config path is questionable.
needs: Google Cloud OAuth client ID and secret
Google Ads customer ID and optional manager account ID
Google Cloud project for the optional Cloud Run deployment
why: It serves a narrow need for reading ad-campaign reports, which is only occasionally useful for building or selling a product, and it depends on an outside Google Ads account. The Cloud Run section moves the server to the cloud, but the local pipx path is the main route. It is marked skip because the Cloud Run step as written exposes the server publicly.
risks: The Cloud Run step deploys with --allow-unauthenticated, so anyone can reach an endpoint that reads Google Ads data, and it passes the developer token and OAuth client secret as command-line env vars, which leaves them in shell history and deployment logs.

summary: This skill lets an agent look up flight options and fares on Google Flights' public search page, for one trip or a round trip. It compares lowest and average prices across dates, months, and years, and returns booking search links without completing any purchase. It is aimed at a single traveller checking fares for personal trips.
tasks: find the cheapest flight between two airports
compare fares across several travel dates
get a Google Flights search link for a trip
qualityWhy: SKILL.md is mostly a pointer to a remote CLI for the real instructions, though the bundled Python helper is substantive.
why: Flight fare lookup is personal travel planning and does not help build, run, sell or create content for a product, so value is none. It also scrapes a third-party search page, and its setup fetches and runs code from npm at runtime, so use is skip.
risks: Runs the npm package @nomadamas/k-skill via npx at runtime and keeps it auto-updated, so the instructions an agent follows can change without review.

summary: This skill teaches an agent to build networked games in Godot 4.7 using its high-level multiplayer system. It covers hosting and joining over ENet, defining RPCs with the @rpc annotation, assigning per-node authority, and replicating state with MultiplayerSpawner and MultiplayerSynchronizer. It is written for game developers who need server-authoritative multiplayer in a Godot project.
tasks: add online multiplayer to a Godot game
host and join an ENet game server
write RPC functions for player actions
sync player positions across peers
qualityWhy: The skill gives concrete, runnable GDScript patterns, a clear workflow, and a useful pitfalls list, with a reference file for deeper topics.
why: Godot is a game engine and not part of the Fractera stack of Next.js, SQLite and web tooling, so game networking does not serve building sites, web apps, agents or content on a node. The skill itself is sound, but it does not fit what nodes are for.

summary: This skill gives an agent a structured way to diagnose misbehaving LLM applications by checking twelve layers, from the system prompt through memory, tool use, and output delivery, to find where an answer gets corrupted. It walks through scoping the audit, collecting evidence from source, logs and config with ripgrep searches, and mapping each failure to its layer and root cause. It ends with severity-ranked findings and a code-first fix plan. It is aimed at developers who are building agent features or about to ship one.
tasks: audit an agent that gives wrong answers after new prompt layers were added
find hidden retry or repair LLM calls before a release
trace why old conversation topics leak into new chats
produce a severity-ranked report on an agent's tool-calling reliability
qualityWhy: The skill is concrete and complete, with a layer table, phased workflow, search commands, severity model, output order and a JSON report schema, though its examples are thin.
why: It is a stack-free diagnostic method that directly helps build and ship AI agent features on a node, and its ripgrep searches work on any codebase. It only reads and reports, and it does not depend on a particular framework or outside service.

summary: This skill lets a coding agent write a markdown file and open it in a side panel of the cmux terminal app. The panel renders headings, code, tables and lists, and re-renders whenever the file changes on disk. It suits a person who wants to follow an agent's plan, task list or changelog while the agent works in the terminal.
tasks: show a plan or task list beside the terminal
preview a changelog while coding
display notes that another process updates live
qualityWhy: The instructions give concrete commands, options, a ready AGENTS.md snippet and a write-then-open workflow, but they say little about error cases such as a missing cmux install.
why: It runs locally with no cloud service, but it only helps with reading plans and docs during development and does not build or run a site, app or content for the node. It assumes the cmux desktop app is installed, which SKILL.md does not state, and I did not review the reference files in detail.

summary: This skill gives an agent a set of conventions for handling failures in TypeScript, Python and Go applications. It shows how to define typed error classes with codes and status codes, return results without throwing where failure is routine, and turn errors into consistent API responses. It also covers retries with exponential backoff, React error boundaries, and friendly user-facing messages. It is aimed at developers building production web apps and APIs.
tasks: add typed error classes to an API
add retries with backoff to an external call
show friendly error messages in the UI
wrap React components in an error boundary
review endpoints for missing error handling
qualityWhy: It gives concrete code for each pattern and a review checklist, though some snippets lack imports or helpers and the circuit breaker named in the description is never shown.
why: Its TypeScript and Next.js examples match the node's stack directly, so an agent can use them as written when building apps and APIs. The Python and Go sections are extra and do not conflict with that. The circuit breaker mentioned in the description has no code, so an agent would need to write that part itself.

summary: The skill guides an agent through diagnosing common problems with the ClickHouse Node.js client, such as dropped connections, data type conversion surprises, and TLS or proxy setup failures. It maps each symptom to a dedicated reference file with detailed fixes. It is aimed at developers who run ClickHouse from Node.js code, including Next.js server-side routes.
tasks: fix socket hang up errors in my ClickHouse Node.js app
why are my large integers coming back as strings
configure TLS for the ClickHouse Node client
debug a parameterized query that isn't interpolating
qualityWhy: The index table maps symptoms to specific reference files and the runtime restrictions are clearly stated, but the SKILL.md body itself contains only the index and links, so the detailed steps live in files I could not see.
needs: a ClickHouse server reachable from the node
why: The skill directly serves building and running data-backed apps on a node, but it targets ClickHouse as the database. The node's own SQLite element is the only door to data, so an agent would need to adapt the advice rather than follow it as written, which puts it under ideas.

summary: The skill has an agent audit an existing XML sitemap for a site, checking format, size limits, URL status, lastmod accuracy, and whether listed URLs are canonical and indexable. It can also generate new sitemaps from industry templates, splitting large sets into a sitemap index and documenting the structure. It is aimed at SEO-focused site owners and marketers.
tasks: audit my site's XML sitemap for errors
generate a sitemap for my online shop
split a large sitemap into a sitemap index
check whether sitemap URLs are indexable and return 200
qualityWhy: It gives concrete validation rules, limits, a severity table and an error-handling flow, though the generation step leans on an external templates folder and some steps are high-level.
why: It is an SEO audit and generation skill that suits a site built on a node, but it is not a build or content tool and it relies on a plugin-root script and a sibling templates folder that may not exist in a node install. It makes network requests to fetch the site's pages, which is expected for an audit and not a risk.

summary: The skill teaches an agent to write Godot 4.7 game code in C# on .NET 8: subclassing nodes as partial classes, using PascalCase lifecycle methods with a double delta, declaring exports and signals as attributes, and fetching nodes with typed lookups. It also covers calling between C# and GDScript and the pitfalls of the build setup. It is aimed at game developers who want C# instead of GDScript.
tasks: write a Godot player controller in C#
convert a GDScript script to C#
wire Godot signals as C# events
set up a Godot .NET project with the .csproj build
qualityWhy: Concrete examples cover lifecycle, exports, signals, instancing and GDScript interop, with a useful pitfalls list, though the reference file is only summarised here.
why: Godot is a game engine and the node's stack is a web app stack (Next.js, SQLite), so the skill is only useful for building games, not the node's main purpose. It is built for the Godot .NET stack, which the node does not run, so it should be read for ideas rather than installed as written.

summary: The skill lets an agent search Danawa's public product listings, then compare the lowest prices across shops, including shipping, card discounts and interest-free installments. It is aimed at a person looking up a purchase for themselves. The visible SKILL.md does not contain the working steps; it tells the agent to fetch them at runtime from a remote npm CLI, so the instructions the agent actually follows are not in these files.
tasks: compare prices for a product across shops on Danawa
find the cheapest total buying price including shipping
check card discounts and installment options for an item
qualityWhy: The SKILL.md is a wrapper that only points to a remote CLI and the scraping script is cut off, so no complete steps or checks can be judged from the files.
why: It helps a person look up shopping prices, which is occasionally useful but does not directly serve building, running, selling or making content for a product. It is skipped because the stub runs a remote npm package at each use and the update command changes every installed skill; the script also scrapes Danawa, and the disclaimer warns against systematic collection.
risks: The stub runs `npx -y @nomadamas/k-skill@0` to fetch and execute code from npm at runtime, which the agent would then follow as its instructions.
The stub's `update` command reinstalls and changes every coding-agent skill install, which goes beyond this skill's scope.

summary: This skill gives an agent a reference of Redis patterns in Python: cache-aside and write-through caching, session storage, fixed and sliding-window rate limits, single-node distributed locks, Pub/Sub and Streams, key naming, TTLs, connection pooling, and eviction policies. It is aimed at backend developers who run Redis next to an application server. The agent can use it to choose a structure for a given job and to review how keys and expiry are set up.
tasks: add caching to an API endpoint
rate-limit requests per user
coordinate a background job across workers with a lock
set up event messaging with Pub/Sub or Streams
qualityWhy: The patterns are concrete and mostly runnable, with clear tables and anti-patterns, though some snippets rely on an undefined db object and the stampede lock only works inside one process.
why: Redis is not part of the node's stack, and the node sends all data through its SQLite element, so Redis would need to be adapted to that rule. The examples are Python while the node is TypeScript, so the ideas must be rewritten in the node's own stack.

summary: Walks a developer from zero to a first working Google Ads API request: getting a developer token, OAuth client and refresh token, the customer and manager IDs, then picking a language library or raw REST and running a campaign-listing script. It also includes fixes for USER_PERMISSION_DENIED and DEVELOPER_TOKEN_NOT_APPROVED. The audience is developers who build tools that read or manage ad accounts.
tasks: set up Google Ads API credentials
write a script that lists campaigns
fix USER_PERMISSION_DENIED with login_customer_id
understand why a developer token is not approved
choose a client library or REST for Google Ads
qualityWhy: Concrete steps, exact config templates and error checklists are given, but it leans on runtime-resolution directives and some mandatory-format rules that add noise.
needs: Google Ads account with developer token
Google Cloud project with OAuth client
why: Useful for building apps that read Google Ads data, but it only helps a site or agent that needs ad-campaign data; it is not a core building or content tool for a local node. It calls the Google Ads service with the person's own account and keys, which is a paid-service choice the person makes, and it does not touch local storage directly.

summary: This skill teaches an agent to run the Firecrawl command-line tool for live web work: searching the web, reading or scraping pages, mapping a site's URLs, bulk crawling a site section, downloading a site, interacting with pages that need clicks or logins, and setting up change monitors. It routes specialised needs to sibling skills for research papers, US law, developer questions, and local file parsing. It is aimed at people doing web research and content gathering.
tasks: search the web for sources on a topic
scrape a page's content into markdown
find a specific subpage on a large site
bulk extract all docs pages from a site
monitor a page for changes and get alerts
qualityWhy: The skill gives a clear escalation workflow, a command table, output conventions and reference routing, though many details are delegated to other files and some steps assume the CLI is installed.
needs: Firecrawl account or API key (a keyless free tier is mentioned)
why: Web research and scraping help content and product work, but Firecrawl is a paid hosted service that fetches pages through its own cloud, so the person must choose it knowingly; it is not a local-first tool. Its output is written to local files under .firecrawl/, which fits the node.

summary: This skill lets an agent cut the background out of a photo by calling the Pilio service through its command-line tool. It targets portraits, products and other images that need transparent cutouts. The agent runs one command on a local file and, if the job is still in progress, waits for the result. The skill points people to Pilio's website as an alternative to doing the same job by hand.
tasks: remove the background from a portrait photo
make a transparent cutout of a product image
clean up backgrounds on a batch of pictures
prepare a logo or image for a shop listing
qualityWhy: The instructions are clear and short, but they give only one command with no output path, no error handling and no examples of the returned result.
needs: Pilio API key in the PILIO_API_KEY environment variable
why: Background removal serves image making for shops and content, and Pilio only processes the image and returns the result to local files, so it is usable on a local-first node. The image is uploaded to Pilio's cloud, which the person must accept, and pnpm dlx fetches an unpinned npm package on every run. Output file location and error handling are not described.

summary: The skill guides an agent through a local SEO audit of a website, scoring Google Business Profile signals, reviews, on-page local content, NAP consistency, citations, local schema and link authority. It is aimed at small and multi-location businesses and their marketers who want to improve map pack and AI-search local visibility. It produces a structured markdown report with a score, prioritized actions and quick wins, and points to other SEO skills for geo-grid tracking and AI visibility work.
tasks: audit local SEO for my business website
check my Google Business Profile signals
review NAP consistency and citations
add LocalBusiness schema to my location pages
plan a multi-location store page structure
qualityWhy: The skill is detailed, with scoring weights, explicit checks, output sections and error handling, though it leans on external reference files and some statistics are cited without local verification.
why: It directly serves a node building and running business websites, with no cloud service required, and it is a stack-free audit habit that works on the node's own pages. Some cited statistics are time-sensitive and unverified, and the reference files it loads (../seo/references) must be present in the install for full use.

summary: This skill guides an agent through a technical SEO audit of a website, covering whether search engines and AI crawlers can reach, render and index its pages. It checks robots.txt, sitemaps, canonicals, HTTPS and security headers, URL structure, mobile parity, Core Web Vitals and structured data, then reports a scored breakdown with prioritized fixes. The audience is site owners and developers who want to find and fix search-visibility problems on their own sites.
tasks: audit a website's technical SEO
find out why pages are not getting indexed
check Core Web Vitals and page speed
review robots.txt, sitemaps and AI crawler rules
check HTTPS and security headers
qualityWhy: The checklist is concrete, with thresholds, named checks, error-handling steps, and a fixed output format, though it depends on plugin scripts whose files are not included.
needs: Google API credentials for PageSpeed Insights, CrUX and Search Console (optional)
why: It directly serves running and promoting a website on a node, and it is not tied to a cloud host. It calls the plugin's own scripts through a CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT path that is not in these files, so an agent would need that runner installed; the optional Google and DataForSEO integrations need the person's own keys and send the audited URL to those services.

summary: The skill guides an agent through designing systems, services and architectures in a structured sequence: gathering requirements, sketching a high-level design, going deeper on data models and APIs, planning for scale and reliability, and weighing trade-offs. It is aimed at people who need to decide how a system should be built before writing code. The output is a structured design document with diagrams, stated assumptions and a list of things to revisit as the system grows.
tasks: design a system for a new product
decide how a service should be architected
model the data and API for a feature
plan service boundaries and scaling
qualityWhy: The framework is clear and ordered, but it is a generic checklist with no worked examples, templates or concrete checks an agent can follow step by step.
why: It is stack-free planning advice that helps when designing a node-based product, so it is useful now and then rather than daily, and it can be installed as written. It is thin, so an agent would need to supply most of the detail itself.

summary: The skill guides an agent through end-to-end testing of Windows native desktop apps (WPF, WinForms, Win32/MFC, Qt) using pywinauto over Windows UI Automation. It covers stable AutomationId setup, a page-object layout with waits and screenshots, per-test filesystem sandboxing, optional Job Object containment, a Windows Sandbox option, and CI on windows-latest. It is aimed at developers who want automated GUI tests for their own desktop software.
tasks: write E2E tests for a WPF login window
set up a pywinauto test suite for a Qt app
diagnose a flaky desktop UI test
add AutomationIds to WinForms controls for testing
run desktop E2E tests in GitHub Actions
qualityWhy: Concrete and mostly complete, with code for pages, fixtures, waits, CI and Qt quirks, though a few snippets are inconsistent (e.g. the basic fixture references APP_ARGS-less config and the Tier 2 Job Object and timeout notes are thin).
why: It is a testing skill for Windows desktop apps, which is not what a Fractera node builds (web apps, sites, content), so it is useful only occasionally for testing a desktop product. It is written around pytest and pywinauto with Windows-only tooling, so an agent on a node would need to adapt it to the node's own test setup rather than install it as written. Doubt: the Tier 2 and timeout guidance is loosely specified.

summary: This skill tells an agent that a project uses the eve framework to read the framework's bundled documentation before writing code. It is a pointer rather than a guide: it names the docs folder inside the installed package and the commands to install or scaffold an agent. The agent would then use that documentation to build or fix durable backend AI agents, where instructions, tools, skills, channels, schedules and subagents are files on disk. The audience is developers building backend agents.
tasks: build a durable backend AI agent
add a tool, skill or subagent to an agent project
debug an eve agent project
set up a scheduled agent run
qualityWhy: The SKILL.md only points to the bundled docs and says not to rely on the skill for guidance, so it gives no steps, examples or checks of its own.
why: Building AI agents fits what nodes are for, but eve is a separate agent framework and not the Next.js stack a node uses, so the agent should read its ideas and build in the node's own way. The skill has no content beyond a pointer, and what the bundled docs contain is unknown from these files.

summary: This skill acts as a router for UI work: when an agent gets a clear UI goal, it decides whether the task is UI-related, picks a category through the ui-skills CLI, and loads only the one to three most specific UI skills needed before implementing. It is aimed at developers using coding agents such as Codex, Cursor, or Claude Code who want focused design and craft guidance. The skill itself contains only routing rules and CLI commands, so the actual UI guidance lives in the separate skills it points to.
tasks: pick the right UI skill before building a component
clean up layout or visual styling in an existing page
route a redesign request to the narrowest useful UI guidance
decide whether a request needs UI skills at all
qualityWhy: The protocol and selection rules are clear and actionable, but the file is only a router with no examples, checks, or concrete UI guidance of its own.
why: It is a generic UI-routing layer rather than a stack-specific skill, and it depends on an external npx CLI registry to deliver any real content, which a node would only use now and then. It is built around a generic frontend workflow rather than the node's Next.js 16 stack, so it should be read for its selection ideas and adapted to the node's own Blocks catalogue and stack instead of installed as written.

summary: This skill guides an agent through writing a new skill for Claude Code plugins: a folder with a SKILL.md whose frontmatter description holds trigger phrases, a lean body in imperative form, and optional references, examples and scripts. It walks through a six-step process from gathering concrete use cases to validating and iterating. The target audience is plugin developers who want to author or improve skills.
tasks: create a new skill for a plugin
improve a skill's description and trigger phrases
organize a skill with progressive disclosure
review a SKILL.md for best practices
qualityWhy: It gives a clear, ordered process, a validation checklist, good and bad examples and a directory layout, though some of it repeats itself and it assumes Claude Code plugin conventions.
why: It is a meta-guide for writing skills, useful now and then when a node builder authors a skill, but it is written for Claude Code plugins rather than the Fractera node's own skill layout, so it should be read for its ideas and applied the node's way. No risks found in the file contents.

summary: The skill guides an agent through MySQL and MariaDB work: schema design with sensible column types, composite and generated-column indexing, EXPLAIN-driven index tuning, upserts, keyset pagination, full-text search, and short lock-aware transactions. It also covers connection-pool setup in SQLAlchemy and mysql2, slow-query diagnostics, replica read-after-write pitfalls, least-privilege users, and a review output format. It is aimed at backend engineers running production MySQL or MariaDB databases.
tasks: design a MySQL schema with proper indexes
review a migration before it runs on a large table
debug slow queries or deadlocks in MariaDB
set up a connection pool for a MySQL backend
replace deep OFFSET pagination with keyset pagination
qualityWhy: It is concrete and checkable, with SQL and code examples, version-specific caveats, diagnostics commands and a review output template, though it leaves some items as bullet points without full worked examples.
why: The skill is a stack-free database reference, but the node replaces its own database engine with SQLite as the only data door, so MySQL-specific schema, pool and replication advice would need adapting to SQLite and the node's own data element rather than being installed as written. Its activation is narrow, so it is only occasionally useful on a node.

summary: This skill guides an agent through auditing a web page for how well it can be cited by AI search surfaces such as Google AI Overviews, AI Mode, ChatGPT, Perplexity and Gemini. It covers scoring citability, passage structure, entity and brand signals, server-side rendering, and robots.txt access for named AI crawlers, then produces a GEO-ANALYSIS report with prioritised changes. It is aimed at site owners and SEO or content teams who want their pages surfaced in AI-generated answers.
tasks: audit a page for AI Overviews citability
check robots.txt for AI search crawlers
rewrite passages so answer engines can quote them
score a site's GEO readiness
suggest schema and entity signals for AI discoverability
qualityWhy: The instructions are detailed with scoring weights, crawler tables, output sections and error handling, though some sections are long on statistics and a few claims are third-party and unverified.
needs: DataForSEO account (optional, for ChatGPT scraping and LLM mention tracking)
why: It directly serves making and running a site for AI search visibility, and it is stack-free apart from optional tooling. It is marked install-with-service because the optional DataForSEO integration needs a paid account; many statistics are third-party and were not re-verified, and the skill refers to a plugin path ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} that may not exist on a node.

summary: Walks an agent through a five-step smart contract security workflow: run Slither, check upgradeability and ERC conformance, generate inheritance and access diagrams, document invariants for fuzzing, and review manual risk areas like front-running and cryptography. It is aimed at developers securing Solidity projects end to end before check-in or deployment.
tasks: run a security audit on a smart contract project
triage a Slither report
check contract upgradeability and ERC conformance
document invariants for Echidna fuzzing
qualityWhy: The SKILL.md gives a clear structure and useful rationalization table, but the steps are high-level summaries, with the detailed commands pushed to a separate WORKFLOW_STEPS.md file that was not included in the provided content.
why: The skill is about auditing Solidity smart contracts on-chain, which is outside what a local-first Fractera node is built for: the node's web, app, content and data work does not involve smart contracts, so it is not useful here. It is marked skip because value is none.

summary: This skill lets an agent look up Korean intercity bus timetables, fares and remaining seats on the official Tmoney site, using plain HTTP requests rather than a browser. It can optionally place a temporary seat hold and save the official card-entry page, then hands the person off to that official checkout. It is aimed at an individual planning their own trip, not at building or selling anything.
tasks: search intercity bus timetables for a route and date
check remaining seats and fares for a bus
hold a seat and hand off to official checkout
qualityWhy: The instructions are concrete, with a runnable script, named endpoints and explicit approval rules, though the script was only partly visible and the skill depends on a remote CLI.
needs: Tmoney intercity bus service at intercitybus.tmoney.co.kr
the person's own Tmoney account for seat hold and checkout
why: Booking a personal bus ticket is not something a node is for, since it does not help build, run, sell or create content for a product. It also carries risks, so it should be skipped.
risks: The skill runs an unpinned remote npm package via npx each time and auto-updates it, which means downloading and executing remote code.
The script disables TLS certificate verification for its requests to the Tmoney host.

summary: This skill lets an agent search Korean official statistics tables on KOSIS, the national statistics portal, and pull their metadata and cell data through a read-only Python helper. It is aimed at people who need official Korean figures such as population, households, prices or employment. The helper covers search, metadata, parameter data, bulk data, indicators and table listings, with error hints for common API failures. The SKILL.md file itself is only a stub that fetches its real instructions at runtime from an npm package.
tasks: look up the latest Korean population figures from KOSIS
find an official statistics table on household counts
fetch yearly consumer price data for a Korean content article
check the metadata and units of a KOSIS table
qualityWhy: The bundled instruction.md, helper script and tests are concrete, with parameter rules, error-code guidance and test coverage, though the stub SKILL.md defers the real instructions to a runtime download.
needs: k-skill proxy at k-skill-proxy.nomadamas.org (default route, unless --direct is used)
why: The skill gives occasional value for citing official Korean figures in content, not core building of a product. It is marked skip because the SKILL.md tells the agent to run an npm package with npx, including an update command that rewrites every installed skill, and the helper's default route sends the API key to a third-party proxy.
risks: SKILL.md runs remote npm code via npx (`npx -y @nomadamas/k-skill@0 instruct ...`), and the instructions it prints can change at any time, so the reviewed content is not what runs.
The `npx -y @nomadamas/k-skill@0 update` command rewrites all coding-agent skill installs on the machine without asking.
By default the helper sends the KOSIS API key and query parameters to a third-party proxy (k-skill-proxy.nomadamas.org) rather than directly to kosis.kr.

summary: This skill guides an agent through checking how many other sites link to a website, which pages get those links, and the anchor text used. It also flags suspicious link sources, compares a site's links with a competitor's, and lists link-building opportunities. It is written for site owners and SEO workers who want to understand or improve a site's search standing. It uses whichever data sources are configured, from paid providers down to free public web-graph data, and it refuses to give a numeric score when the data is too thin.
tasks: audit a website's backlink profile
find toxic links and prepare a disavow list
compare a site's backlinks with a competitor's
check whether known backlinks are still live
qualityWhy: The steps, source preference order, scoring thresholds, fallback cascade and pre-delivery checks are concrete and followable, but the scripts it calls are not in the folder and it cannot run as shipped.
why: It is useful only when a site's link profile is the specific goal, so its value is occasional rather than core to building a node. It needs the claude-seo plugin's scripts, which are not in this folder, and most of its depth depends on paid or keyed services the person must choose to set up; Common Crawl alone gives only low-confidence rank data.

summary: This guide teaches an agent how to build a backend that fetches movie and TV data from The Movie Database (TMDb) through the tmdb-client Motoko package, running inside an Internet Computer canister. It covers authentication with a read token, mapping TMDb's mostly optional responses into simpler records, user sessions for favorites and watchlists, rate limits, and a list of operations the package omits. It is aimed at developers making movie catalogs, title pages, cast pages and discovery feeds.
tasks: build a movie search feature
show now playing and upcoming films on a landing page
create a title page with cast and crew
add a user's favorites or watchlist from TMDb
make a trending or top-rated carousel
qualityWhy: The instructions are concrete, with working code, credential and session steps, and pitfalls, but they are tied to Motoko and a few parts (accountId, guest ratings) are explicitly untested.
needs: TMDb user account for favorites, watchlists and ratings
why: Movie data is useful for sites and content, but this skill is written for Motoko canisters on the Internet Computer, which Fractera nodes do not use, so an agent would need to port the TMDb calls and sessions to Next.js server code and SQLite. The guidance on the TMDb API itself (endpoints, image URLs, rate limits, the optional-field handling) is reusable.

summary: This skill teaches an agent to deploy and manage services on the Elestio hosting platform through its official CLI or MCP connector. It covers catalog templates for databases and apps, clustering, CI/CD pipelines, backups, firewalls, domains and billing. It is aimed at people who run hosted infrastructure on a cloud provider they pick.
tasks: deploy PostgreSQL or Redis on a managed VM
set up a database cluster with replicas
run catalog software like Vaultwarden as a pipeline
configure backups, firewall or custom domain for a service
qualityWhy: The skill is detailed, with decision trees, command references, payload rules and error tables that an agent can follow, though it is long and leans on an external account flow.
why: Elestio is a cloud hosting and cloud VM platform that provisions remote servers at AWS, Azure, Hetzner and similar providers, which the node's local-first design excludes, so value is none and it is skipped.
risks: Stores and passes an Elestio API token and S3 backup keys through CLI flags, exposing secrets in shell history and logs.

summary: This skill guides an agent through a local-evidence production readiness audit of an application before launch, after a merge, or when someone asks what might break in production. The agent inspects git state, CI, migrations, auth boundaries, webhooks, environment handling and rollback paths in the repo itself, then returns a scored ship-or-block recommendation with specific fixes. It is aimed at engineers and founders preparing a release.
tasks: audit this app before launch
what would break in prod after this merge
check whether the release is ready to ship
list blockers and high-value fixes before deploy
qualityWhy: The skill gives a clear evidence checklist, risk lenses, a scoring table with caps, an output format and an example, though it is generic about how to inspect a specific stack.
why: It directly serves checking a product before it goes live and runs on local evidence only, with no outside service required. Its scoring bands are judgement aids rather than certainty, and the skill itself says it is not a compliance audit.

summary: The skill guides an agent through inspecting Blender characters, armatures and animations by first extracting structured scene data (bones, bounding boxes, contacts, facing vectors) and only then using screenshots to confirm findings. It helps diagnose foot sliding, ground penetration, backwards imports, leg crossover and scale drift, and ends with a structured pass/fail report. It is aimed at people who review or fix 3D character animation.
tasks: diagnose foot sliding in a retargeted walk cycle
check whether an imported avatar faces the right direction
inspect a Blender rig for ground penetration and scale drift
produce a motion inspection report before rendering
qualityWhy: It gives a clear workflow, report template, worked examples and numeric thresholds, though it lacks a concrete exporter script.
why: It is a stack-free animation review method that a node could use when working on 3D assets, but it serves the making of 3D content only occasionally rather than the core building of sites or apps. It needs Blender installed locally, which is not a cloud service, so no outside service is required.

summary: This skill lets an agent look up Korean intercity bus timetables on the KOBUS booking site, check seats, place a temporary seat hold, and prepare a handoff to the official payment-information page. It is aimed at a traveller booking a trip for themselves. The SKILL.md itself only fetches its real instructions from an npm package at run time, and the bundled Python helper and its tests do the actual HTTP work.
tasks: find a bus timetable between two Korean cities
hold a seat on a KOBUS express bus
prepare a bus ticket checkout handoff
qualityWhy: SKILL.md is a wrapper that only points to a remote CLI for the real instructions, so the visible files are thin, although the helper script and its tests are concrete.
why: Booking a personal bus ticket is not a building, running, selling or content-making use for a node, so the value is none and the skill is skipped. It also runs a remote npm package on each use and turns off TLS certificate checks, so it carries risks.
risks: npx -y downloads and runs the latest @nomadamas/k-skill@0 package from npm every time the skill is used.
The helper script disables TLS certificate verification with an unverified SSL context and lowers the cipher security level.

summary: This skill gives an agent a checklist of small design-engineering details that make a user interface feel more polished. It covers nested corner radii, optical icon centering, borders versus shadows, text wrapping, tabular numerals, image outlines, motion timing, interaction states and hit-area sizes. make buttons and icons feel tactile
fix awkward heading wrapping and jumpy counters
review a UI for animation and hit-area issues
qualityWhy: It gives concrete rules, code snippets and a before/after review format, but it has no step-by-step workflow for applying the changes to a real codebase.
why: It is a stack-free set of CSS and UI habits that directly improve the front end of sites and apps built on a node, with no outside service needed. Its CSS examples are generic, so an agent should apply them to the node's Tailwind and shadcn/ui components rather than copy them blindly.

summary: This file is a redirect notice saying the seo-content-writer skill has been merged into a newer content-writer skill in another repository. It gives no writing steps, checks or examples of its own. It points to a bundle install command and a frozen copy of the old skill. An agent reading only this file learns where the current skill lives but cannot write SEO content from it.
tasks: write an SEO blog post
find the current content-writer skill
plan search-focused landing page copy
qualityWhy: The file is only a signpost to another repository and contains no instructions an agent could follow.
why: The topic (SEO content writing) suits a node that builds sites and blogs, but this file itself does nothing and the working skill lives in a different bundle. The redirect's install command would need its own review before anyone runs it.

summary: This skill teaches an agent to enable the Google Analytics Admin API in a Google Cloud project with the gcloud CLI, set up application default credentials, and use the official client libraries to list accounts and properties. Google account with Google Analytics access
gcloud CLI with Application Default Credentials
Google Analytics edit scope for configuration changes

summary: This skill lets an agent strip visible watermark overlays from PNG, JPG, JPEG, or WEBP images by calling the Pilio command-line tool. It uploads the picture, receives a task ID, and waits for the asynchronous job to finish before handing back the result. why: It is a narrow image-editing helper that calls an outside service and returns the result to local files, so it fits content work only now and then. The image is uploaded to Pilio, which the skill does not state plainly, and the skill does not say where the cleaned file is saved.

summary: This skill tells an agent to explain how a part of a codebase works, such as its architecture, runtime flow, or where responsibilities sit between packages. For small questions it runs one explanation pass. For larger subsystems it first splits the question into several angles, has parallel read-only explorers gather findings, then merges them into one onboarding-style walkthrough. walk me through the request lifecycle before I change it
which package should own this new feature
give me an onboarding overview of the data layer
explain how this subsystem fits together across files

why: It helps a developer on a node understand existing code before building or changing a site or app, but it does not make content or serve end users directly. It is stack-free and needs no outside account, and it only runs read-only subagents, so it is safe to install as written.

summary: This skill teaches an agent to set up Unity 6.3 LTS character animation: Animator Controllers, state machines, parameters, blend trees, layers with Avatar Masks, and humanoid IK. It includes C# snippets for driving the Animator from script, plus a list of common pitfalls. The audience is Unity game developers animating characters.

why: Unity character animation is game-engine work, which falls outside what Fractera nodes are for (sites, web apps, AI agents and content). The skill is a sound local guide, but it has no use on a node.

summary: This skill tells an agent to upscale or enhance an image by calling the Pilio command-line tool, which uploads the file to Pilio's service and returns a task. If the task has not finished, the agent polls it until the result is ready. improve the clarity of a photo
enhance product images for a shop
check the status of an upscaling task
qualityWhy: The file is a short wrapper that gives two shell commands and a link, with no description of inputs, output location, options, error handling or result checks.
why: Image enhancement directly serves making content and products, but the skill's only install path runs an unpinned npm package through pnpm dlx with the API key in the environment, and it sends the user's images to an outside service. The risk of executing remote code with a secret makes it unsafe to install as written.
risks: pnpm dlx fetches and runs the latest @pilio/cli package from npm without pinning a version or checking it, while the API key is in the environment.

summary: This skill lets an agent search Daangn, a Korean secondhand marketplace, through its public web endpoints and fetch details for individual listings. Its SKILL.md is only a launcher: it tells the agent to run a remote npm CLI to receive the real instructions, so the substantive guidance is not in the files reviewed. It is aimed at individuals looking for items to buy.
tasks: search Daangn used goods for a keyword in a given region
check the price and status of a used-goods listing
list items on sale near a neighborhood
qualityWhy: SKILL.md is a stub that points to a remote CLI for its instructions, and the bundled script is a read-only fetcher with no steps, checks or examples for an agent to follow.
why: It is a personal lookup of a third-party marketplace and does not help build, run, sell or make content for a product, so value is none. It also depends on undocumented internal Daangn endpoints and describes an official-account surface that needs the person's account, which adds legal and access uncertainty.
risks: SKILL.md has the agent run 'npx -y @nomadamas/k-skill@0 instruct' and 'update' on each use, which downloads and executes an npm package and rewrites installed skills, and the instructions it prints can change without review.

summary: This skill guides an agent to build miniature, believable product interfaces, such as app windows, dashboards, phones, notifications and cursor walkthroughs, as still illustrations or short animated demos. create a phone and notification mockup for a hero section
turn a product screen into a still marketing image

why: Its output directly serves building landing pages, hero sections and feature cards for a product, and its kit is React with plain CSS, so it fits the node's stack without a service. The scripts (film.mjs, dev.mjs and others) were not visible, so their behaviour is unverified, and the kit files were partly hidden.

summary: This skill teaches an agent to work with QuickBooks Online through a Motoko package for the Internet Computer. It covers creating, reading and updating customers, invoices, payments, items and accounts, emailing invoices, and running queries against the Intuit accounting API. run a QuickBooks query for accounting data

QuickBooks OAuth 2.0 access token per user

The package is also written for Motoko on the Internet Computer, not for the node's Next.js and SQLite stack, so it would need rebuilding even if the data location were acceptable.

summary: This skill gives an agent ready-made React and Next.js animation snippets for common interface parts such as buttons, modals, toasts, staggered lists, route transitions, scroll reveals and expanding cards. set up page transitions in the App Router
add scroll-reveal effects to landing page sections
animate toast notifications stacking

why: The skill is useful for building UI on a Fractera node, but it imports from a '@/lib/motion-tokens' file and a 'motion-foundations' skill that the node does not provide, and it assumes a Radix or focus-trap dependency, so it must be adapted to the node's own stack before it is used. No risks were found in the file.

summary: This skill guides an agent through building or editing any user interface, covering color, layout, components, decorative elements, app dashboards, motion and page performance. It gives each anti-pattern a description, the reason it reads as generic AI output, and a concrete fix, and it ends with a checklist to run before delivery. why: It is directly useful for building and polishing node-hosted UIs and needs no outside service. It is written as a rules layer that references a core file and rule numbers not in this package, so it works best alongside those files; it is not tied to a foreign stack.

summary: This skill gives an agent a two-tier memory system for remembering workplace shorthand, nicknames, acronyms and project codenames. A small hot-cache file holds the most-used people and terms, while a deeper memory folder holds a full glossary, person profiles, project notes and company context. look up who a person is or what a project is called

Nothing in it is a security risk.

summary: The skill has an agent read a git repository's commit history for a chosen period or between version tags, sort the commits into groups such as features, improvements, fixes, breaking changes and security, and rewrite the technical messages as plain customer-facing release notes. It is aimed at product teams and developers who publish release notes, weekly updates or a public changelog page. The instructions are short and mostly examples, with no scripts or checks.

generate a weekly product update summary from git history
turn commit messages into customer-friendly update notes

why: Release notes help a node's product owners and the sites or apps they build, but the need is occasional rather than daily. It is a stack-free text skill that only needs git, so it can be installed as written; the output still needs human review.

summary: The skill guides an agent to write BigQuery SQL that uses built-in AI and ML functions such as forecasting, anomaly detection, key-driver analysis, semantic search, vector search, classification, embeddings and Gemini-based generation. It is aimed at data analysts and engineers who want predictions or GenAI inside queries on Google Cloud. The files are a SKILL.md index plus reference pages for each function with syntax, arguments and examples.
tasks: forecast next month's sales in BigQuery
detect anomalies in a metrics table
run semantic search over product descriptions
extract structured fields from support tickets with Gemini
qualityWhy: The reference files give concrete syntax tables, output schemas and runnable examples for each function, though the SKILL.md itself is mostly an index with little workflow guidance.
needs: Vertex AI connection for remote models
why: The skill is built entirely around BigQuery, a cloud data warehouse that runs the data and models on Google's servers, which the local-first node rules treat as a cloud place to keep data, so value is none and use is skip.

summary: This skill tells a coding agent to stop giving the first obvious answer to an open-ended question. It runs five isolated generator passes, each under a different thinking frame such as a hardware engineer, a speedrunner or a competitor trying to break the design. The agent then scores the ideas for novelty, viability and fit, groups them by underlying angle, and deepens the best three. It is meant for architecture, naming, API shape and fuzzy design decisions, with a pre-flight check so it skips simple or closed questions. The person gets a shortlist with traps flagged, not a pile of ideas.
tasks: brainstorm architecture options for a new feature
generate product or project naming ideas
explore unconventional API or SDK designs
work through a fuzzy bug with several hypotheses
tools: Agent (Task) tool for parallel isolated sub-agent calls
qualityWhy: The skill gives a clear two-phase loop, a frame table, output format, a pre-flight gate and anti-patterns an agent can follow, though scoring weights and the trap rules are somewhat loose.
why: It is a stack-free reasoning method for design and planning decisions, so it helps occasionally when shaping a product, but it does not build, run or sell anything by itself. It costs about 10 sub-agent calls per run, which is a cost to weigh and not a risk. The optional companion npm CLI (adhd-agent) is not needed to use the skill.

summary: This skill lets an agent look up apartment, office-tel and store listings in a Seoul neighbourhood on the public Daangn Realty map, filter them by property type and trade type, and read price, area and floor details from article pages. It runs a read-only Python search and detail tool that parses the page data and returns JSON. It is aimed at a person doing personal property research, not at bulk collection. Its contact, visit-booking and contract steps are only described as a scope for the official-account surface, not implemented in these files.
tasks: find rental apartments in a Seoul neighbourhood
compare monthly rent and deposit prices across nearby districts
look up floor, area and subway details for a listing URL
filter listings by property type and trade type
qualityWhy: The SKILL.md is mostly a pointer to an external CLI, but the bundled Python scripts are concrete and runnable, and the main instruction file was not among the files provided.
why: The listing data is public and the tool is read-only, so it is useful now and then for a personal property search, and it runs locally with no cloud service or key. It is skipped because the setup runs npx -y on a remote npm package at runtime and can auto-update every installed skill, so the person would be running code they have not reviewed.
risks: Runs 'npx -y @nomadamas/k-skill@0 instruct' and 'update', executing a remote npm package without review and changing skill installs automatically.

summary: This skill gives an agent a shared set of motion values for a React or Next.js interface: duration and easing tokens, named spring presets, and a gate that turns animation off for reduced-motion users or weak devices. It also sets rules for keeping server and client renders consistent, so animated components don't cause hydration errors. Frontend developers building marketing pages, dashboards or product UIs would use it before writing any animated component.
tasks: add a reduced-motion safe fade-in to a landing page section
set up shared animation duration and spring presets for a Next.js app
fix a hydration mismatch caused by an animated component

summary: This skill tells an agent to drive a real Chrome browser through the chrome-devtools-axi command-line tool. The agent can open pages, click through flows, fill forms, read page content, check console errors and network requests, take screenshots, and run performance audits. It is aimed at people who are testing or debugging a website or web app, or pulling content from one. The file itself contains almost no operating steps; it sends the agent to the CLI's own help output for those.
tasks: test a web page in a real browser
click through a signup or checkout flow
debug console errors on a website
take a screenshot of a page
audit page performance
extract content from a web page
qualityWhy: The SKILL.md is a wrapper that only points to the CLI's --help output and gives no concrete steps, examples or checks of its own.
why: A local browser tool for testing and debugging a web app serves building a product directly, and it needs no cloud account or key. The skill runs an unpinned npm package via npx -y, so the agent gets whatever version is current and the package's code is not reviewed here; pinning a version would be safer, but this is how the tool is meant to run, so it is not treated as a risk. The skill's value rests almost entirely on the external CLI documentation.

summary: This skill is meant to rewrite Korean text that reads as machine-written so it sounds like a person wrote it, keeping the meaning intact. It names specific AI habits to catch, such as translation-style phrasing, stock filler, and heavy nominalization, and can stretch or shrink a draft to a target character count. The SKILL.md itself contains none of these rules. It only tells the agent to fetch and follow instructions from an npm package at runtime, so the actual method cannot be checked from the files provided.
tasks: make my Korean blog post sound less like AI
fix awkward translated Korean sentences
rewrite this Korean draft to about 1000 characters
polish a Korean social media caption to read naturally
qualityWhy: SKILL.md is a stub that only points to a remote CLI and a URL for its real instructions, so nothing checkable is given here.
why: The topic (Korean writing that reads naturally) directly serves content making, but the skill depends on running an npm package at runtime and following its output as instructions, which is a risk the node should not accept without review. Its instruction.md was not included, so its real content is unknown.
risks: Runs npx -y to download and execute an npm package at each use and follows its output as primary instructions.
The update command runs a global update across every installed coding-agent skill, which goes beyond this skill's purpose.

summary: Guides an agent through 3D physics in Unity 6.3 LTS using the built-in PhysX engine: adding Rigidbodies and Colliders, applying forces in FixedUpdate, handling collision and trigger callbacks, setting collision layers, and running raycasts. It also covers joints via a reference file. The audience is game developers building 3D Unity projects.

connect two bodies with a joint

why: The node's stack is Next.js and React for web apps, sites and content, and this skill is for Unity game development, which is not what nodes are for. It is a high-quality skill but has no fit with the node's purpose.

summary: This skill teaches an agent how to write Claude Code slash commands as Markdown prompt files with optional YAML frontmatter. why: It documents how to build Claude Code commands, which is developer tooling for the agent itself rather than something that builds or runs a product's sites, apps, or content on a local node. Its format targets Claude Code's directories, not the node's own skill folder layout.

summary: This skill guides an agent writing, reviewing, or debugging JavaScript for n8n Code nodes. It first checks whether a native node or a short expression can do the job, and only then covers the closed list of cases where Code is justified. review a Code node for return-shape and webhook-body mistakes

why: It is an n8n-specific workflow skill, so it is not for the node's own product stack, and its guidance targets n8n rather than Fractera's Code-free runtime. It would be used now and then to write logic in n8n workflows, not to build the site itself; because it is built for a different engine (n8n), it should be read for ideas and adapted to the node's own stack.

summary: The skill guides an agent through diagnosing network interface problems such as CRC errors, drops, flapping, and duplex or speed mismatches on routers, switches, and Linux hosts. It stresses comparing counter increments over time instead of absolute totals, and checking both ends of a link before replacing hardware. It also includes a Python parser for Cisco-style interface output. The intended users are network operators and people running their own servers or homelab networks.
tasks: diagnose packet loss on a server's network link
find why a switch port shows CRC errors
compare counters on both ends of a cable
check whether a slow connection is caused by a congested uplink
parse show interfaces output into a table
qualityWhy: The skill gives a clear diagnosis flow, a counter reference table, examples and anti-patterns, but the parser covers only Cisco-style output and the Linux steps lack worked examples.
why: It is a stack-free networking diagnosis guide that helps with hosting and running servers, but it does not directly help build sites or content, so its value is occasional. The parser targets Cisco IOS output only, so Linux hosts need manual reading of the commands shown.

summary: The skill guides an agent through MongoDB query and index optimization, using MCP tools to read indexes, explain plans, sample documents and Atlas Performance Advisor output before suggesting compound indexes. suggest an index for a find with sort
review slow query logs on an Atlas cluster

find anti-patterns in update queries

MongoDB Atlas API credentials for Performance Advisor (optional)
why: Query and index tuning is central to building and running a node's data layer, and the skill works on the node's own SQLite-free MongoDB data only when the user connects a MongoDB database, which is a choice the person makes. Its Atlas Performance Advisor path needs a cloud account, so it is marked install-with-service rather than install; it also expects a MongoDB backend, so an agent should confirm the node actually uses MongoDB before applying it.

summary: This skill has an agent keep a shared TASKS.md file in the working directory as a plain-text task list with Active, Waiting On, Someday and Done sections. pull action items from meeting notes into my tasks

why: It is a stack-free personal tracker that is local and useful now and then, but it does not directly serve building, running or selling a product. The dashboard setup step points to ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}, which will not exist on a node, so that step would fail and should be skipped.

summary: This skill guides an agent through writing production Apex code for Salesforce: services, selectors, domains, batch and queueable jobs, triggers, invocable methods, REST resources and similar classes. It sets naming conventions, bulkification and security rules, and requires running a code analyzer and tests before reporting. It is aimed at developers working on Salesforce orgs.

why: It builds Salesforce Apex, a cloud platform the node does not host or replace, so it does not serve local-first Fractera products; the cloud backend makes it a skip.

summary: This skill teaches an agent how to write hookify rules: small markdown files with YAML frontmatter that Claude Code reads to watch for risky shell commands, file edits, prompts or stop events. warn when console.log is added to a file
add a completion checklist before the agent stops
write a regex pattern for a bash command

why: It is a local developer-tooling aid for Claude Code guardrails rather than a way to build or sell a product, so it is useful only now and then. It needs no outside service, and its stack fits the node.

summary: This skill is a router and overview for assistant-ui, a React library for building AI chat interfaces. build a copilot that can use app tools and context

optional Assistant Cloud account for hosted thread persistence

summary: This skill gives an agent a Python pipeline for preparing raw credit data before a loan model is built. why: It runs locally on the person's own data files with no outside service, but it serves a niche analytics job rather than building, running or selling a web product or content, so it is only occasionally useful on a node. The stack is standalone Python and does not conflict with the node's own stack. I could only see part of analysis.py and example.py, so the rest of the code is unreviewed.

summary: This skill guides an agent through writing Python scripts that log into network routers, switches and firewalls over SSH using the Netmiko library. summary: This skill guides an agent through a structured maturity review of a smart contract or blockchain codebase using a nine-category rubric covering arithmetic, auditing, access control, complexity, decentralization, documentation, transaction ordering, low-level code and testing. Hugging Face token for some models

summary: This skill guides an agent through reviewing APIs, configuration schemas and crypto library designs for misuse-prone choices, such as dangerous defaults, algorithm selection, and silent failures. Its reference files are general, not tied to Next.js or the node's SQLite and next-auth elements, which is acceptable because it only reads code.

summary: The skill gives an agent a planning and review checklist for changing a home or small-lab network: splitting it into VLANs, moving DHCP and DNS filtering to a local resolver such as Pi-hole or AdGuard Home, and adding VPN remote access. It tells the agent to stay read-only at first, inventory the existing setup, stage changes, keep a rollback path, and avoid exposing admin interfaces. why: It serves home network administration, which is not what a Fractera node is for (building, running, selling or making content), and it is not a cloud service either. Its own advice says not to produce router or firewall commands without a confirmed platform, so it adds little for a node.

summary: The skill has an agent review one supplied web page for SEO, covering on-page elements, content quality, technical meta tags, schema markup, images and rough Core Web Vitals risks. summary: The skill gives an agent a review checklist for Cisco IOS and IOS-XE configuration. It covers read-only show commands for collecting evidence, wildcard mask conversion, ACL direction and placement checks, interface hygiene, and before/after verification for change windows. why: Fractera nodes are for building and running sites, apps, agents and content, and this skill is network-device administration with no link to those uses. It is a stack-free checklist, so it would otherwise be installable, but it does not serve what nodes are for.

summary: This skill teaches an agent to drive a Chrome browser from the terminal through the chrome-devtools-mcp command-line tool. The agent can open and navigate pages, take snapshots and screenshots, click and fill forms, read console and network logs, run performance traces, and run Lighthouse audits. It suits people testing, debugging or automating the web apps and sites they build on a node.
tasks: test a login form in the browser
take a screenshot of a page for review
run a Lighthouse audit on my site
debug console errors and network requests
record a performance trace of a page load
qualityWhy: The instructions give a clear workflow, many concrete command examples and a snapshot example, but the setup is only in a separate installation file and there is little on error handling.
why: Risk first: by default the CLI has unrestricted filesystem access, so upload_file and file-saving flags can read or write any file on the computer, and a malicious page could steer an agent into uploading private files such as ssh keys; it becomes usable once run with --allowUnrestrictedPaths=false. Otherwise it is local-first, needs no keys or cloud service, and directly serves testing and debugging of sites and apps; the installation file was not provided, so the setup steps are unverified.
risks: By default the CLI allows file access anywhere on the computer (--allowUnrestrictedPaths=true), so upload_file could send private local files such as ssh keys or .env to a web page an agent visits.

summary: This skill helps an agent look up Korean cinema information from CGV, Megabox and Lotte Cinema, including currently showing films, showtimes and remaining seats. On the Dolshoi runtime it can also carry out follow-up actions through the chains' official interfaces. The SKILL.md file is only a launcher: it tells the agent to fetch the real instructions at run time from an npm package. For a person checking movie times, that is the whole use.

list films currently showing at CGV, Megabox or Lotte Cinema
see how many seats remain for a screening
qualityWhy: The SKILL.md is a stub that only points to a remote CLI for its real instructions, so nothing concrete can be judged from the visible files.
why: Movie showtime lookup serves a person's own entertainment, not building, running, selling or making content for a product, so its value is none. It is also skipped because the skill downloads and runs an npm package at every use.
risks: It runs `npx -y @nomadamas/k-skill@0` each time, which downloads and executes an npm package without review, and the instructions it prints can change at any time.
Its `update` command upgrades the CLI and every coding-agent skill install, which goes beyond this skill's own folder.

summary: This skill gives an agent a decision dossier for a crypto wallet address on GMGN: it runs four pass/fail checks on whether the trading record is genuine, whether the edge still holds this week, whether a copier could get filled in time, and whether the wallet cuts losses. It then returns a verdict and a size cap for a memecoin trader deciding whether to copy the wallet. The workflow depends on a gmgn-cli tool and a GMGN API key, and it is read-only.
tasks: check whether a wallet is worth copying
analyze a wallet address before following its trades
see what a wallet is buying right now
judge whether a trader's recent edge still works

why: The skill is built around a cloud data service (GMGN) that supplies all wallet and trade data and is queried live, so it does not fit a local-first node's purpose of building, running or selling products and content. Because its value is none, it is skipped.

summary: This skill gives an agent a layered writing standard for technical documents: it picks one Diátaxis mode (tutorial, how-to, reference, or explanation) per document, then applies Google developer style, STE-style short instructions, and Global English rules for unambiguous sentences. It is aimed at engineers writing docs, RFCs, readmes, PR descriptions, or commit messages. It also asks the agent to run the unslop skill on its output and to suggest new entries for that skill's catalog without editing it.

summary: The skill reads a multi-step plan document, splits it into steps, classifies each step by its main tag, and produces a ready-to-paste ECC slash command for each step. summary: The skill guides an agent through checking whether a reported security bug is real or a false positive. why: It is a stack-free security-review habit useful now and then for a node's own code, not for building or selling directly. Only SKILL.md was provided in full, so the referenced checklists were judged from their titles and descriptions.

summary: This skill lets an agent search Korea's K-Startup database for government startup support programs, open calls, startup content and statistical reports.
