why: It is a stack-free-in-spirit guide for building Expo apps, which is exactly what a node serves, and it needs no outside accounts. The examples assume the Expo and TanStack/Zod stack, which the node does not replace, so it fits as written.

summary: This skill makes an agent work as a product designer: it plans user research, builds journey maps, sets up information architecture, writes design tokens and component specs, and runs usability tests. Its three Python scripts score a UI against Nielsen's heuristics and accessibility checks, produce journey maps from templates, and calculate System Usability Scale and task metrics. It is written for product teams and their designers.

critique a screen against usability heuristics
score a usability test with SUS and task metrics
define design tokens and component specs
plan a five-user usability test

why: It is stack-free design method and tooling that directly helps a team build and improve a product's interface, and the scripts use only the Python standard library. The scripts were only partly visible, so their full contents are unverified, and the MIT + Commons Clause licence restricts commercial resale of the skill itself.

summary: The skill guides an agent in deciding how to divide a skill's content between its main SKILL.md file and separate reference files, to save context and keep triggering reliable. It explains telling apart triggering problems from disclosure problems, when splitting is worth it, and which split patterns work or fail. It also describes how to evaluate a skill's architecture by measuring which files actually get loaded. It is aimed at people who author and maintain agent skills.
tasks: decide whether to split a long SKILL.md into reference files
refactor a skill so it loads less context
diagnose why a skill does not trigger reliably
write pointer sentences for reference files
qualityWhy: It gives explicit decision rules, trade-offs, anti-patterns, a checklist and output steps, though some thresholds are acknowledged as starting points.
why: It is a meta-skill for authoring skills, not for building a Fractera product, so it is only occasionally useful to a node. It is written for Claude Code skill folders, so an agent on a node would need to adapt it to the node's own skill layout and tooling rather than install it as is.

summary: Draws a 12-house Tarot spread using a cryptographically random script, then has the agent read the house and card meanings and map them onto a concrete next step. It is meant for vague or casually delegated requests where the agent would otherwise pick arbitrarily between approaches. The skill explicitly limits the cards to tie-breaking and discovery, requiring ordinary engineering evidence for any security or correctness decision.
tasks: decide which approach to take when the request is vague
break a tie between several reasonable designs
pick the next angle to investigate in an audit
choose a direction when the user says whatever you think
qualityWhy: Concrete steps and a tested script, but the content is largely whimsical tarot meaning mapping with little guidance on concrete technical decisions beyond generic interpretation rules.
why: It is a playful decision-making gimmick with no product-building, content or data function for a Fractera node, so it does not serve what nodes are for. It also carries no risk in itself, but its value is none, so it is skipped.

summary: This skill teaches an agent to build evaluation datasets for LLM applications and keep them in LangSmith. It covers turning exported traces into input/output examples, uploading them through the langsmith CLI or SDK, and listing, inspecting, exporting or deleting datasets and their examples. The CLI feedback section also asks the agent to send notes about CLI problems to LangSmith, which is an additional outbound step.
risks: The setup section tells the agent to pipe a remote install script from the internet straight into sh.

summary: The skill teaches an agent to add continuous profiling to an application using Grafana Pyroscope, either by adding a language SDK, by running Alloy's eBPF profiler across a cluster without code changes, or by sending SDK data through an Alloy receiver. It also explains how to check that profiles are arriving and how to query them with ProfileQL. The target users are developers and operators who need to find CPU or memory hotspots, compare profiles to spot regressions, or link a slow trace to its profile.

deploy cluster-wide eBPF profiling with Alloy
link a slow trace to its flame graph

Grafana Cloud is optional, and if chosen, profiles leave the node, so the person should decide that knowingly. The skill needs a Pyroscope server before it does anything useful.

summary: This skill tells an agent how to answer questions about a PDF, from quick factual lookups to full summaries and structured data pulls. It sets out the kinds of questions to expect, plus output templates for Q&A answers, summaries, extraction tables and side-by-side comparisons across several documents. It is aimed at people who need to review contracts, research papers or financial reports without reading every page. The guidance is mostly templates and prompting tips, and it names no concrete extraction steps of its own.

summarize a contract into key points
extract names, dates and figures from a document into a table
compare terms across two or more PDFs

needs: an AI model provider that reads the document text
why: PDF question answering helps with office documents now and then, but it does not directly serve building, running or selling a product. It depends on an office-mcp server that a Fractera node does not provide, so an agent would have to supply its own PDF text extraction (for example a local PDF library) before following it.

summary: This skill guides an agent to design and build production-grade frontend interfaces such as websites, landing pages, dashboards, app screens and React components. It asks the agent to settle the audience and tone first, commit to one concrete aesthetic direction, and then implement working HTML/CSS/JS or framework code with real states, responsive layout and accessibility. It is aimed at people building product UI or redesigning existing screens.

build a responsive analytics dashboard
redesign an existing app screen
create a React component with polished styling
beautify a website's typography and layout

The license is Apache-2.0, stated in LICENSE.txt, which I did not review in detail.

summary: This skill is a reference for operating Goldsky Turbo data pipelines, which index blockchain data and write it to database sinks. tasks: pause or restart a blockchain data pipeline
find out why a Turbo pipeline is throwing an error
check whether deleting a pipeline loses its progress
scan pipeline logs for common problems

database sink credentials stored as Goldsky secrets

summary: The skill gives an agent a unified pipeline for converting many documents at once between formats such as Markdown, DOCX, PDF, HTML, PPTX, XLSX. It walks through a Python converter class that dispatches to Pandoc, markitdown, pdf2docx, LibreOffice and Marp, plus a parallel batch runner with progress reporting. convert all Office files in a folder to Markdown

why: Document format conversion is useful for building and publishing content on a node, but it runs entirely on local tools (Pandoc, LibreOffice, markitdown) with no cloud service, so it can be installed as written. Doubts: the Markdown-to-PDF step with plain pandoc will likely fail without a LaTeX engine, and the metadata claims more model support than the content justifies.

summary: The skill lets an agent query a public Streamable HTTP MCP server run by Hongik Medicare to list animal pharmacies by region, search veterinary medicines, and find pharmacies that stocked a product in the last six months. It is read-only and aimed at pet owners and people looking for veterinary drugs. The bundled Python script wraps the MCP handshake and tool calls so the agent can run them from the command line.

search for a veterinary medicine by keyword
find pharmacies that recently sold a specific animal drug
qualityWhy: The SKILL.md is mostly a pointer to an external CLI instruction, and the visible script is a clear, usable MCP client, but the instruction body was cut off so the full workflow cannot be checked.
why: The skill queries a third-party hosted MCP endpoint rather than working with local data, files or media, so it does not serve building or running a product on a local node. The SKILL.md also tells the agent to run an npx command that pulls and executes remote code at runtime, which is a risk.
risks: SKILL.md instructs the agent to run `npx -y @nomadamas/k-skill@0 instruct` and `update`, which fetches and executes remote code from npm on every run.

summary: This skill guides an agent through designing, generating and reviewing OmniStudio Data Mapper definitions inside a Salesforce org. sf CLI authenticated to a Salesforce org
why: The skill builds data mappers for Salesforce, a cloud CRM and backend whose data lives in the cloud rather than on the node, so it does not serve local-first building, running or content making. Its scripts and instructions show no security issues, but the cloud dependency alone makes it unsuitable.

summary: Guides an agent through writing a professional training or workshop report as a Word document. It interviews the trainer about session metadata, walkthrough, participant feedback, and recommendations, drafts the report in Markdown with a humanization pass, and only generates the .docx once the content is confirmed. produce a .docx report from my workshop notes

why: It is a stack-free writing and documentation workflow rather than a product-building skill, so it is useful now and then for reporting on training events rather than for daily node work. It depends on a separate docx skill for the final Word output, which the person must install, and it writes only local files.

summary: This skill guides an agent to keep validation, type narrowing and error handling at system edges such as CLI arguments, config files, network calls and external APIs. why: It is a stack-free design habit that helps structure code on a node, so it is useful now and then rather than central to building or selling a product. It contains no risky instructions.

summary: This skill guides an agent in turning a vague information need into precise web search queries, using operators like site:, filetype: and date limits. why: It is a stack-free research habit guide that helps occasionally with sourcing content, but it cannot run searches itself, so the person must supply results. The frontmatter declares an office-mcp create_docx tool that the instructions never call, which is harmless but unexplained.

summary: This skill teaches an agent to write, validate, deploy and operate Goldsky Mirror pipelines, which stream onchain data from a Goldsky subgraph or raw dataset into a database or message queue. a user-managed sink database or queue with a Goldsky secret

summary: This skill guides an agent through designing and checking a multi-step guided form, called an OmniScript, inside a Salesforce org. summary: This skill tells an agent how to run one operation over many files at once, such as converting, extracting or renaming a folder of documents. It sketches a parallel Python worker pool with a progress bar and a checkpoint file so long jobs can resume after a failure. It is aimed at people who need to handle large document batches.

The batch_convert tool from office-mcp is undefined here, so its availability is unknown.

summary: This skill describes how an agent could manage an Obsidian vault: creating daily, meeting, book and Zettelkasten notes from templates, linking people and project notes, writing Dataview queries, and clipping web pages into notes. It also sketches graph checks such as finding orphan notes and suggesting links. It is aimed at people who keep a personal knowledge base.

It depends on an external notes-mcp server and Obsidian's folder conventions, not the node's own SQLite or file elements, so it would need adapting to the node's stack before use.

summary: This skill guides an agent through diagnosing a failing Goldsky Mirror pipeline, the hosted service that streams blockchain data into a user's database. The agent checks authentication, reads the pipeline's desired and runtime status, pulls monitor output and the pipeline definition, and matches the errors against known causes such as bad secrets, unreachable sinks, undersized resources, or stuck snapshots. check whether a pipeline's sink credentials are still valid

why: Mirror pipelines run on Goldsky's own cloud and write into an external database, so this is a cloud-run service rather than local-first tooling, and it does not serve building or running a node's own sites, apps or content. The skill itself is safe: it asks before destructive actions and does not read secrets directly.

summary: This skill lets an agent inspect a Salesforce org that runs OmniStudio: it detects which OmniStudio namespace is installed, counts OmniScripts, Integration Procedures, FlexCards and Data Mappers, and maps how they call each other. an authenticated sf CLI session for that org
why: It analyses OmniStudio metadata inside a cloud Salesforce org, which is cloud administration and not something a local Fractera node builds, runs or sells, so it is not useful for a node's purposes. It has no harmful instructions, so the skip comes from its scope alone.

summary: This skill guides an agent through building, debugging and operating Temporal durable-execution applications in several languages, covering workflows, activities, workers, signals, queries, versioning and local dev servers. summary: This skill teaches an agent how to set up and debug Goldsky Edge, a managed EVM RPC endpoint service, including endpoint creation, authentication options, rate-limit tiers, supported chains, special capabilities such as flashblocks, and error code meanings. tasks: configure a Goldsky Edge RPC endpoint for an EVM chain

summary: This skill makes an agent look up the published Google skills catalog on GitHub, pick at most three entries that match a developer's platform question, and then follow those remote skill files. summary: This skill guides an agent working on the cmux macOS terminal app's codebase through debugging: adding debug event logging to a unified log file, profiling tagged builds by attaching to a pid, using a Debug menu for tuning panels, and avoiding known runtime pitfalls in terminal rendering, hit testing, SwiftUI lists and drag-and-drop. summary: This skill makes an agent review written text for phrasing that reads as machine-generated, such as stock word choices, formulaic openers, and padded transitions. summary: This skill guides an agent through creating a React Native library with the create-react-native-library command-line scaffolder. The intended users are mobile developers who write JavaScript that talks to native iOS or Android code.

summary: This skill guides an agent through building an online shop's storefront: product listings and pages, navigation, cart, checkout and order confirmation. summary: This skill guides an agent through adding structured logging to TypeScript web apps and services, replacing scattered console output with one rich event per request and typed error objects that carry a reason and a fix. why: Logging and error context directly serve building and running a product, so the value is high. The core library and the local file-system and memory drains work without any account, but many examples default to external drains that need keys, so it is marked as install-with-service. The skill also fetches the evlog CLI from npm on demand, which the skill itself says to confirm with the person first; I only read the first 40,000 characters, so the redaction and AI-SDK sections were not checked.

summary: The skill lets an agent look up published Korail KTX-family railway operating timetables for a given route, date and time window, reading the official timetable spreadsheet from Korail's board. why: Useful for travel lookups but not core to building, running or selling a product, so value is some. It uses only public Korail files with no key, and it is read-only, so use is install; the schedule may lag live changes and the source is an outside public site.

summary: This entry is a placeholder that no longer holds working instructions. It says the content-refresher skill was merged into a newer content-writer skill in another repository, and it links there along with a frozen copy of the old file. summary: This file is a signpost, not a working skill: it says the performance-reporter skill has been merged into performance-monitor in a different bundle and points to the new location and an install command. summary: This skill gives an agent templates and conventions for running a Jira project: issue lifecycle, sprint setup, bug and feature templates, JQL search queries, and sprint or velocity dashboards. summary: This skill guides an agent through setting up AWS Site-to-Site VPN, an encrypted IPsec link between an on-premises network and AWS. why: The skill is cloud networking administration for AWS, a cloud service the node does not provide, so it is not useful for building or running a local-first product. It would be skipped regardless of its quality.

summary: The skill guides an agent through React 19 development: choosing Server versus Client Components, wiring Server Actions with validation, and using hooks like useOptimistic, useActionState and useTransition for instant feedback and non-urgent updates. make a search filter stay responsive on a large list
type component props and context in TypeScript

The Zod example uses a library the node may not include, and the examples use `any` types, which an agent should tighten.

summary: The skill teaches an agent to work with OKLCH, a perceptually uniform color space, in web projects. summary: This skill tells an agent how to write git commit messages in the conventional style used by Sentry. It covers choosing a type and optional scope, keeping subjects short and imperative, wrapping body lines, and adding footers that link or close issues. It is aimed at developers who save their project work with git.

add an issue reference to a commit
mark a breaking change in a commit

why: It is a stack-free habit for saving changes with git, so it helps occasionally when building a node's project rather than serving its core purpose directly. It has no outside service dependency and works as written.

summary: This skill turns an agent into a paid-advertising conductor for twelve ad platforms. summary: The skill guides an agent through writing a structured crypto research report on a token or blockchain project, covering tokenomics, supply and vesting, on-chain metrics, competitors, valuation and risks. It is aimed at analysts and investors who want a template-driven write-up. The agent is told to produce the report as a DOCX or XLSX file using office document tools. The skill itself cannot fetch live prices or chain data, so the user supplies the figures.

assess risks of a layer 2 network

why: This is financial research for crypto assets, not a tool for building, running or selling a product or making content for one, so its value to a node is none. It is also not local-first: it relies on the office-mcp server and on outside price and on-chain sources the user would supply.

summary: This skill acts as a router for Claude Code's ECC slash-command set. Given a described workflow, it picks the matching command family, gives the order to run the commands in, and states when to stop. Without a description, it lists every command family read live from the commands folder. It only advises and never runs the commands it names, and it points to other skills for single-command docs and prompt rewrites.

list all ECC command-group recipes
decide when to stop an autonomous command loop

summary: The skill is a single Markdown guide that tells an agent how to plan and run customer success work: multi-phase onboarding programs with checklists, a weighted health score model with automated alert rules, quarterly business review slide templates, expansion signal and conversation frameworks, and churn-prevention save offers. summary: This skill guides an agent through connecting applications to Amazon RDS for Oracle, covering network paths, security groups, TLS and native encryption, and credentials kept in AWS Secrets Manager. summary: This skill guides an agent through writing a product requirements document, moving from rough notes to a structured PRD. summary: The skill guides an agent to write professional business emails for situations such as client replies, meeting follow-ups, polite declines, apologies and cold outreach. summary: This skill adds a Stop hook to Claude Code that runs when an agent tries to finish a session. It checks free disk space, whether the project's learning-log files were touched today, and whether the final text contains phrases that suggest shortcuts were rationalized. On a complex task it can block the stop, which pushes the agent to record what it learned first. It is aimed at developers who want session hygiene enforced mechanically rather than trusted.
tasks: block the agent from finishing until learning logs are updated

Its install step copies the script into ~/.claude and edits global settings, which differs from the node's per-element installation, so the person should scope it to the element deliberately. The rest of quality-gate.py past the 8000-character cut is unseen.

summary: Guides an agent through setting up, running and fixing PHPStan static analysis in WordPress plugin, theme and site projects. A bundled Node script reports the existing PHPStan setup of a repo.

summary: This skill teaches an agent to turn plain Markdown notes or outlines into slide decks using the Marp format. summary: This is a routing guide for building native Salesforce mobile apps on iOS or Android. It helps an agent decide whether a request needs the Mobile SDK (login, offline sync, push), the Agentforce SDK (embedded agent chat), or both, then hands off to the matching platform skill. It contains no implementation steps itself. It is aimed at developers building Salesforce-connected mobile apps.

summary: This skill guides an agent through adding or changing ASP.NET Core Web API endpoints using either controllers or minimal APIs, with typed responses, correct status codes, and CancellationToken handling. summary: This skill is a set of templates and YAML rules for an expense-management workflow: reading receipt images, sorting expenses into categories, checking them against spending policy, routing approvals by amount, and building monthly reports. summary: This skill guides an agent through removing the stock phrasing and structural habits that make text read as machine-written. Its contribute sub-flow can open a pull request, and the references it depends on were not supplied, so an agent should confirm those files exist before relying on the full flows.

summary: This skill makes an agent review code it has just written or changed before the work is shown or committed. It checks naming, function size, comments, SOLID and DRY principles, and a set of failure patterns common in AI-generated code, such as swallowed errors, invented library calls, and dead code. It has three modes: a guard pass after edits, a live mode applied while writing, and a structured review that reports findings without editing. It is aimed at developers and coding agents who ship application code.

why: It is a stack-free judgement layer that works in any language and directly improves the code a node's agents produce for sites, apps and tools, with no network or key required. The skill is only instructions and does not replace the project's own linters or tests.

summary: The skill lets an agent pull text out of scanned pages, photos and image-only PDFs using local Tesseract OCR. It can also make searchable PDFs, preprocess noisy images (deskew, denoise, threshold, shadow removal), and parse receipts and business cards into JSON fields. It is aimed at people who need to turn paper or scanned documents into usable data. The instructions are a short workflow, and the bundled Python scripts do the work.

It uses no cloud service or key. I could only see about 8,000 of the 27,804 bytes of scripts/ocr_processor.py, so the rest is unverified. Receipt and card parsing are heuristic and will be unreliable on poor scans.

summary: This skill guides an agent through filling PDF forms with supplied data, reading values back out of completed forms, and running batch fills from a spreadsheet or CSV. It mostly provides templates, field maps, validation rules and sample report formats for people handling forms such as W-9s or job applications. It describes an MCP server it depends on but gives few concrete steps for performing the fill.

validate form data before filling
qualityWhy: Most of the file is templates, example reports and tables, with no step-by-step procedure for performing a fill, and its own limitations say it only provides guidance.

The skill depends on an office-mcp server the node does not provide, and it is generic guidance rather than runnable instructions, so an agent should read it for ideas and build the fill logic on the node's own tools.

summary: This skill walks an agent through setting up service level objective alerts in Google Cloud Monitoring, using PromQL. why: It configures alerting for Google Cloud resources, which is cloud administration rather than building, running or making content on a local-first node, so it does not serve those uses.

summary: This skill guides an agent through creating invoices from line items and templates, sending them to clients, and tracking which ones are paid or overdue. summary: Teaches an agent to turn finished work into short learning entries that name a reusable pattern, its root cause, and a recognizable signal, rather than a diary of events. summary: This skill gives an agent a design-first way to build web interfaces: it makes the agent propose colour, type, layout and motion options and wait for approval before applying them. It then guides the build with Tailwind and shadcn/ui conventions, accessibility checks, responsive rules and a short review checklist. summary: The skill is a long reference document describing how an agent should automate QuickBooks bookkeeping: creating invoices and recurring billing, categorising expenses from receipts, matching bank feeds, and producing P&L, balance sheet, cash flow and aging reports. summary: This skill teaches an agent to set up and troubleshoot Goldsky Boost, a free caching layer placed in front of an RPC provider the user already pays for. The agent can point an existing Alchemy, QuickNode or Infura endpoint through Boost, diagnose auth and cache-miss problems, and read cache headers to measure savings. debug why my eth_getLogs calls show zero cache hits
check x-cache and x-edge-billable headers on RPC responses

why: Boost is an RPC caching service for blockchain apps and does not serve the node's core uses of sites, web apps, AI agents or content creation, so its value is none. The skill also depends on a cloud RPC service and cloud provider accounts, which the local-first rule treats as skip.

summary: This skill gives an agent a set of design rules for command-line tools that other AI agents will call through a shell. summary: This skill guides an agent through diagnosing slow SwiftUI screens, scrolling hitches, excessive view-body updates and list identity churn, starting from code review and then moving to Instruments traces and before/after measurements. It is written for iOS developers who maintain SwiftUI apps. It gives a triage list, common code smells with fixes, lazy-container guardrails, and a review checklist. It does not help build or run a Fractera node's web product, content or agents directly.

review list identity and lazy loading in SwiftUI

why: The skill targets native iOS SwiftUI apps built with Xcode and Instruments, which fall outside what a Next.js and SQLite local-first node is for. Its subject is not the node's web stack, so it has no direct use there.

summary: This skill gives an agent a set of rules for behaviour that is reachable from several places in an app, such as a keyboard shortcut, a command palette, a context menu, a CLI command or a settings screen. why: It is a stack-free set of design habits that applies to any node app with several entrypoints, so it is useful now and then but not a core building tool; it is written for cmux, so an agent would need no adaptation beyond reading the principles.

summary: This skill guides an agent to write a blameless engineering post-mortem after a bug fix has been found, reproduced and validated. write up an RCA after the debug session
close out this bug with an engineering writeup

why: It is a stack-free writing skill that helps engineers document a bug fix, so it is useful now and then rather than core to building a Fractera product; it has no need for an outside service beyond optional JIRA posting, which requires explicit approval.

summary: This skill is a reference guide for running a WooCommerce store with an AI agent. summary: The skill gives an agent a guide for shrinking PDF file sizes, with preset compression levels, a table of image downsampling and JPEG quality settings, optional structure cleanup, and report templates. Since the skill advises rather than acts, it is not directly installable as a working tool.

summary: This skill guides an agent in building a Salesforce Lightning Web Component that uses native phone features such as barcode scanning, biometrics, location, NFC, calendar, contacts, document scanning, geofencing, AR capture, in-app review and payments. why: It targets Salesforce LWC development inside a cloud CRM platform, which is not part of building, running or selling a Fractera site, app, agent or content, so it does not fit a local-first node. It is not risky, but it is not useful here.

summary: This page is a redirect notice: the rank-tracker skill no longer lives in this repository and has been moved to a bundle. summary: The skill gives an agent a short two-rule discipline for refactoring and code review: merge repeated decisions into one source of truth passed as a simple flag, and keep diffs as small as possible. summary: This skill guides an agent writing Angular code: it checks the project's Angular version first, scaffolds with the Angular CLI, and runs a build after generating code. summary: This skill tells an agent to stop doing non-trivial work by hand and instead write a small script, codemod, generator, or rerunnable check that does or verifies the job. It applies to edits, migrations, analyses and checks, and it asks for the first unit to be done by hand so the recipe can be learned before the tool is built. why: It is a stack-free working habit that helps an agent build reliable scripts for Fractera work such as bulk content edits or migrations, but it does not serve building or selling directly. Its links point to sibling principle skills that are not included in this single-file package, so those references will be dead on install.

summary: This skill lets an agent browse a directory of websites built for AI agents, like entries, and submit, edit or delete its own listings. It works through MCP tool calls authenticated with ATXP, and an agent that wants to vote in a browser must set a cookie first. why: The directory is for promoting and discovering agent-facing sites, which is only occasionally useful to a node that builds and sells products, and it relies on a paid external service. The skill is marked skip because it has the agent run npx packages fetched at runtime and place a session cookie in a URL query string.

The skill has the agent put the auth cookie in a URL query string, where it can leak into logs and browser history.

summary: This skill teaches an agent to call the Brave Search web endpoint and read back ranked results with titles, URLs, snippets, thumbnails and metadata. It covers filters for freshness, language, country and SafeSearch, pagination, location headers, and Goggles for custom ranking. It is aimed at developers building search features and at agents that need current web lookups.

why: Web search is useful for agents and research tasks, though it is a lookup rather than a core building or content tool. It calls an outside paid service, so queries leave the node for Brave; the key is read from an environment variable as expected.

summary: This skill guides an agent through building webhook endpoints that receive events from outside services such as Stripe, GitHub and Slack. It covers HMAC signature checks, routing events to handlers, mapping payloads to internal shapes, retries with dead-letter queues, and basic monitoring. why: Webhook receiving fits a node that has a Stripe element and form-driven features, but the skill is written for a generic Express server and an unnamed integration-mcp server, so it must be rebuilt on the node's Next.js routes and SQLite element. Its debugging suggestions to public capture sites like webhook.site should not be used with real customer payloads.

summary: The file is a redirect notice saying this skill has moved to another repository bundle. summary: This skill teaches an agent to add transactional email sending through Mailtrap's Email API. It covers Bearer-token authentication, separating sandbox from production endpoints so test mail never reaches real inboxes, and verifying a sending domain with SPF, DKIM and DMARC before launch. summary: This skill guides an agent through revising an existing OpenSpec change, the planning documents that describe a proposed code change. It needs the openspec CLI installed and a project already set up with OpenSpec; it calls no outside service and does not replace the node's stack.

summary: This skill lets an agent look up Korean coastal ferry information from KOMSA's MTIS system, including sailing schedules, vessels, ports, licensed routes, operating routes and service status. It sends each query through a relay server rather than calling KOMSA directly. The main audience is a developer adding Korean ferry timetables to a travel or transport app.

summary: This skill guides an agent through building the backend of a Medusa commerce application. summary: This skill guides an agent through writing feature specs stored in a project's .walden/specs folder: requirements in EARS form, a design with reviewed alternatives, and a task plan whose steps are executable proofs. install the entity-optimizer skill from the marketing bundle
qualityWhy: It is only a signpost with no steps, examples or checks, so it teaches an agent nothing about entity optimization.
why: The file only points elsewhere and has no usable content for building, running or selling anything on a node, so it should be skipped in favour of the active bundle version if that is evaluated separately.

summary: This skill guides an agent through scoring a sales lead and deciding whether to pursue it. It offers three qualification frameworks (BANT, MEDDIC and GPCTBA/C&I) with fill-in templates, plus a fit-and-engagement scoring model. It also defines a standard report with flags, gaps, next steps and a disqualification checklist. The intended users are sales people and small teams who want consistent prioritisation of inbound or outbound leads.
tasks: score this lead against BANT criteria
qualify a prospect using MEDDIC
build a lead scoring model for our pipeline
write a lead qualification report with next steps
prioritise a list of leads from a spreadsheet
qualityWhy: The frameworks and report templates are clear and reusable, but the scoring points are not fully summed, qualification thresholds are missing, and there are no worked examples or step-by-step procedure.
why: It is a stack-free sales habit guide, useful now and then for a business run on a node, but it is not about building or making content for a product. The spreadsheet tools it names come from an office MCP server, not the node's stack, so those steps may not work unless that server is present; the core templates still work without it.

summary: Teaches an agent to transcribe or translate audio files on the local machine using the Whisper command-line tool, with no API key needed. It gives a quick-start command for transcribing to text or subtitles and notes on model downloads and model size trade-offs. It is aimed at people who want offline speech-to-text for recordings, voice notes or video soundtracks.
tasks: transcribe an audio recording to text
make subtitles (SRT) from a video's audio
translate a spoken recording into English
choose a faster or more accurate Whisper model
qualityWhy: The instructions are short and correct for the CLI, with two working examples and a few notes, but they lack error handling, supported formats, and checks on output.
why: Speech-to-text of local media fits building content and transcripts for a product, but it is a narrow, occasional use rather than core to running a site. The model runs locally with no key; the first run downloads model weights from the internet, which is a one-time network step. The note that the default model is 'turbo' is install-specific and may not match a fresh install, so an agent should check it.

summary: This skill guides an agent through backend architecture decisions using domain-driven design, clean/onion layering and hexagonal ports and adapters. It helps with modeling aggregates and bounded contexts, isolating use cases from infrastructure, and refactoring dependency direction, while warning against applying the full pattern set to simple CRUD. It points to focused reference files for layers, strategic and tactical DDD, ports, CQRS and events, testing and a cheatsheet.
tasks: design aggregate boundaries for an order domain
refactor a service so business logic does not depend on the database
review dependency direction between backend layers
plan bounded contexts and context mapping
add an outbox for reliable event publishing
qualityWhy: The SKILL.md is well organised with a clear decision table and reference routing, but its own instructions are general principles; the concrete steps and examples sit in the reference files, which were not supplied for judging here beyond their names and sizes.
why: It is a stack-free architecture guide, so it is useful now and then for backend design work on a node, but it is written for generic backend code and must be applied to the node's Next.js and TypeScript stack rather than installed as written. Its reference files were not read, so their depth and any hidden instructions are unverified.

summary: This skill guides an agent through judging job applications against a role's requirements. It has the agent split criteria into must-have and nice-to-have items, weight them, and score each candidate with templates and rubrics. The output is a per-candidate report and a ranked list with interview recommendations. It is aimed at HR staff and hiring managers.
tasks: screen a resume against job requirements
rank a batch of applicants for a role
draft interview questions for a candidate
qualityWhy: It offers useful templates and scoring tables, but it gives no step-by-step procedure for reading documents or checking the results, and it leans on a generic report format.
needs: office-mcp server for reading PDF and DOCX files
why: Hiring screening is an internal HR process of one company and does not help build, run, sell or make content for a Fractera product, so it is not useful for what nodes are for. It is skipped for that reason, not for any harmful behaviour in the files.

summary: This skill tells an agent to rethink an existing design when a new requirement arrives, instead of patching it on. The agent is asked to imagine the requirement was there from the start, read all affected files, and carry the change through types, docs, examples and rationale. It is a general software-design habit rather than a tool, aimed at developers changing a codebase.
tasks: integrate a new requirement into an existing design
refactor a codebase around a changed assumption
update types, docs and examples after a design change
plan an incremental redesign of a module
qualityWhy: It gives a short, generic set of four bullets with no steps, examples or checks an agent can verify against.
why: It is a stack-free design habit that can help when changing code on a node, but it offers little concrete guidance and no node-specific instructions. It is useful now and then rather than central to building, running or selling a product.

summary: This skill lets an agent run a trading strategy against past price data and report how it would have performed. It covers eight built-in strategies, metrics such as Sharpe, Sortino and max drawdown, equity curves, trade logs and grid-search parameter tuning. It is aimed at traders and analysts who want to test an idea before risking money on it.
tasks: backtest a moving-average strategy on BTC
compare several trading strategies on historical data
optimize strategy parameters with a grid search
calculate Sharpe ratio and max drawdown for a strategy
qualityWhy: It gives concrete commands, a configuration file, an output description and an error reference, but the strategy and test files were not shown, so completeness is only partly verified.
why: It is a self-contained Python analysis tool, so it is useful now and then for an app that offers trading or market analysis, but it does not build, run or sell sites or content. It fetches price data from Yahoo Finance and optionally CoinGecko, so it is not fully local, and its results are historical simulations only.

summary: This skill makes an agent copy the author's locally edited ljg-* skills into a GitHub repository. It first pushes the org-mode master branch, then converts the files to Markdown on an md branch and pushes that too. It checks the README for missing skills, bumps the plugin version, and can run a dry run. It is written for one person's own skill-publishing workflow, with hardcoded paths and repository.
tasks: sync updated skills to the GitHub repo
push skills to master and md branches
dry-run a skill publish before pushing
convert org skill files to Markdown
qualityWhy: The steps, flags, tests and gotchas are concrete and complete, but the paths, remote and macOS-specific sed syntax are hardcoded to one author's setup.
why: It publishes skill files to one author's public GitHub repository, which is not building, running, selling or making content for a node's product. It also carries a risk, so it is skipped.
risks: The script can run `git reset --hard origin/md`, which discards unpushed local md-branch commits.
It rsyncs everything in the skill folders, including untracked files and backups, into a public repository without a per-file review.

summary: This skill is a builder for an existing project. It reads a feature spec and the project's conventions, then writes application code for UI pages and components or for backend logic, and updates the matching scope file as the work moves forward. It first checks that a load bearing design decision is already recorded; if one is missing it stops and sends the work to an architecture step. It is written for teams that already have a spec-driven workflow.
tasks: build a page from an approved design
implement a backend API or service from a spec
add a feature to an existing project and update its scope
record an assumed decision before building
qualityWhy: The instructions are detailed and gated with clear steps, checks and fallbacks, but they depend on several sibling files and on a docs/scope convention that a node does not ship with.
why: It is a general purpose build workflow that fits the node's stack in part, but its gate and scope rules depend on a docs layout and a /architect command the node does not provide, so it would need adapting to the node's own conventions. Its builder steps are useful for product work, but the workflow is process heavy and tied to another team's tooling.

summary: This skill guides an agent to fill Word, Excel and similar documents from templates with placeholders, using Jinja2-style syntax via docxtpl, openpyxl and python-docx. It covers single renders, CSV-driven mail merge that generates one file per row, and conditional blocks. It is aimed at people producing letters, contracts, reports, certificates and order confirmations in bulk.
tasks: mail merge personalized letters from a CSV
generate certificates from a Word template
fill an order confirmation document with customer data
create bulk contracts from a template
qualityWhy: The examples are concrete and runnable, but the skill is thin: the Excel helper ignores Jinja2 syntax it claims to support, the MCP tool named in the metadata is never described, and there are no error-handling or validation steps despite the best-practices list.
why: Document templating helps people generating documents for a product, but it is a generic Python recipe rather than a node feature, so it is only occasionally useful. It runs locally on files with no outside service, and the stack is Python libraries rather than the node's own stack, so it is usable as written in an installed folder.

summary: The skill gives an agent a reference-style playbook for security operations: detection rules for authentication, exfiltration and malware, correlation rules, alert routing by severity, incident response stages, compliance check mappings (PCI-DSS, HIPAA, SOC 2), and KPI reporting. It is aimed at security teams and operations staff who run SIEM-based monitoring. The file describes an MCP server with query, alert, incident and compliance tools, but it does not show how to call them.
tasks: set up brute-force login detection rules
draft an incident response playbook for ransomware
map logging controls to PCI-DSS or SOC 2
build a daily security briefing report
qualityWhy: Mostly YAML and ASCII diagrams of concepts with placeholder queries, fabricated-looking dashboard numbers and no executable steps, checks, or verifiable examples an agent can follow.
why: It is about enterprise security operations and SIEM monitoring, not building, running or selling a local-first site, app or content, so it does not serve what nodes are for. It also depends on an external security MCP server and cloud-style services such as PagerDuty and Slack, so it is skipped.

summary: This skill tells an agent how to fix visual regression diffs that a person has already rejected in a Meticulous test run, along with failing non-visual checks and Agent swarm fix prompts. The agent reads reviewer comments, inspects screenshots and DOM differences, edits the code, replies on each thread, commits with a Meticulous co-author trailer, pushes, and confirms the fixes on the new run. It is aimed at front-end teams who review UI changes before merge.
tasks: fix rejected visual diffs from a test run
apply review comments to the UI code
confirm reviewed screenshot fixes on the next CI run
report which regressions were fixed and which were not
qualityWhy: The steps are concrete and ordered, with exact commands, output-field handling, and checks for carry-forward decisions, but it depends on external CLI behaviour that is not documented here.
needs: Git hosting access (GitHub, GitLab or Bitbucket) for pushing and PR comments
why: It helps only a project that already runs Meticulous visual testing, which is a hosted third-party service and not one of Fractera's core uses, so the value is moderate. Its workflow is tied to Meticulous's own hosted service and to commits pushed to a git host, so it is not a fit for a local-first node; an agent would need the Meticulous service and its key.
risks: Pushes commits and posts PR comments to a remote host, and asks the agent to add a co-author credit to Meticulous's GitHub App address.

summary: This skill guides an agent to produce PDF invoices from structured order or client data. It offers two routes: drawing the page directly with ReportLab, or filling an HTML template with Jinja2 and rendering it through WeasyPrint. The agent is told to check required fields and to calculate totals itself rather than trust supplied values. It is aimed at small businesses and freelancers who bill clients.
tasks: generate a PDF invoice for a client
batch create monthly invoices from order data
make an invoice template with company branding
add tax and totals to an invoice automatically
qualityWhy: It has usable code for two PDF routes and a data schema, but the steps are thin, the office-mcp tools are named without explanation, and it skips page overflow and validation details.
why: Invoices serve a shop or service business, but the skill is a Python script set with no Node or Next.js link, so an agent would have to rebuild the PDF step in the node's own stack. It relies on local libraries and needs no cloud service, which keeps the data on the person's machine. The office-mcp references assume a server this node does not provide.

summary: The skill guides an agent through Mailchimp email marketing: planning and sending campaigns, building audience segments and tags, setting up welcome, abandoned-cart and post-purchase automations, running A/B tests, and reading performance reports. It is written as a reference of configuration sketches and API snippets rather than runnable steps. It is aimed at marketers and shop owners who send newsletters or lifecycle email.
tasks: set up a welcome email series for new subscribers
send a newsletter campaign to a segment
run an A/B test on subject lines
build an abandoned cart recovery email flow
analyze last month's campaign open and click rates
qualityWhy: It is mostly YAML and report mockups with no concrete calls, checks or error handling, and the API snippet uses an undefined client object and invented fields.
why: Email marketing is useful for a node that sells or publishes content, but the skill is a thin reference that its own text does not verify and depends on a hosted Mailchimp account that is outside the node's local-first data. An agent would need to check every endpoint against the real Mailchimp API before using it.

summary: This skill tells an agent how to judge a draft or already-published piece of content before or after it goes out. The agent reads only the opening (title, cover, first line or first seconds) to predict whether viewers will keep reading or watching, which audience groups the content reaches, and what viewers gain from it. It then estimates likely reactions such as stopping, watching through, commenting, saving, sharing and following, and assesses the commercial value of the traffic. For creators and businesses it returns a short verdict with up to three revision suggestions. It does not verify facts or predict view counts.
tasks: check whether a post's opening will keep readers from scrolling away
estimate which audience groups a draft article or video script will reach
assess the commercial value of traffic for a product or service
diagnose why a published post has low views or engagement
suggest up to three priority revisions to a script or title
qualityWhy: The workflow, output template, boundaries and self-check are concrete and followable, though it has no worked example and is written in Chinese for Chinese platforms.
why: Creating social posts, landing copy, blog articles and video scripts is a core node use, and this skill directly evaluates them; it needs no outside service and no stack. Its heuristics are tuned to the Chinese platform context, so results may be less reliable for other markets.

summary: Gives an agent a pre-submission audit routine for iOS App Store releases: checking the archive against current upload floors, reconciling PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy with App Store privacy labels and SDK behavior, and reviewing StoreKit payment paths, ATT use, entitlements, metadata accuracy and screenshots. It also covers how to answer a rejection through Resolution Center. The guidance is written for a developer or agent preparing an iOS app for review, not for building a Fractera site or web app.
tasks: prepare an iOS app for App Store submission
check privacy manifest against privacy labels
respond to an App Store rejection
review in-app purchase compliance before release
qualityWhy: Concrete and well-sectioned with blocking checks, a privacy manifest guide and a submission workflow, though several sections defer details to external references.
why: The skill is entirely about Apple's native iOS App Store review process and has no fit with Fractera's web stack, so it does not serve building or running sites, web apps or content on a node. It would be skipped on a Fractera node because it covers only iOS app submission, not web or content work.

summary: This skill describes how an agent could add text or image watermarks, page numbers, headers, footers and stamps to PDF files, including batch runs over folders. It is written as configuration templates and a short list of options, and it names an external MCP tool for the actual work. It is aimed at people who need to brand, label or protect documents before sharing them.
tasks: add a CONFIDENTIAL watermark to a PDF
number the pages of a report
put a logo and footer on every page
watermark a folder of contracts in one batch
qualityWhy: Mostly markdown templates and option tables with no executable steps, and it admits it only gives guidance, so an agent has little concrete procedure to follow.
why: PDF branding and page numbering are occasionally useful for a node that produces documents, but it is not core to building or running a site or app. It is stack-free and runs no code itself, but it depends on an office-mcp tool that a Fractera node does not provide, so the practical benefit is limited.

summary: This skill teaches an agent to run standard statistical analysis on business data: describing distributions with central tendency, spread and percentiles, spotting trends and seasonality, flagging outliers, and running hypothesis tests such as t-tests, chi-squared and Mann-Whitney. It also gives guidance on interpreting results, including effect size, confidence intervals, and cautions about correlation, multiple comparisons and survivorship bias. It is aimed at analysts and product or business people who need sound conclusions from their numbers.
tasks: analyze whether an A/B test result is significant
describe the distribution of session durations
detect outliers in transaction amounts
forecast next month's signups as a range
check whether a correlation is likely causal
qualityWhy: It gives concrete formulas, Python snippets, decision tables and clear checks for interpreting results, though it has no worked end-to-end example and leaves hypothesis-test code out.
why: Useful for analysing data an agent works with on a node, such as product metrics or sales figures, but it is generic analysis advice and not tied to any stack, so value is some rather than high. Nothing in it calls a service, and the pandas snippets run on local data.

summary: This skill sets the working rules for an agent operating inside an OpenKnowledge project, a markdown knowledge base synced through a CRDT and exposed over MCP. It tells the agent to read, search, write, link and lint markdown only through OpenKnowledge's tools, to cite every factual claim to a local document, and to persist work incrementally. It is written for people maintaining documentation, research notes and decision records.
tasks: write a grounded knowledge base article with cited sources
link related markdown documents into a wiki
consolidate a decision into a canonical document
preview a markdown document in the browser
qualityWhy: The file is detailed and gives concrete tool calls, checks and rules, but it depends on a separate OpenKnowledge system and many referenced files were not included.
needs: OpenKnowledge MCP server configured via ok init
why: Its markdown knowledge base and MCP tool surface duplicate the node's own SQLite data element and do not fit the node's stack, so an agent would have to adapt the rules rather than install them. Its grounding and linking habits can still be useful for content work on a node.

summary: The skill guides an agent through migrating Apache Airflow DAG code from an existing Managed Service for Apache Airflow environment, or a local copy, to Airflow 2.11.1 or Airflow 3. It covers inspecting the source environment, downloading DAG files from a GCS bucket, grep-based scans for breaking provider and core changes, ruff checks, and optional upload and verification with gcloud. It is aimed at engineers moving Airflow pipelines between versions.
tasks: migrate Airflow DAGs to Airflow 3
find breaking provider changes in my DAGs
upgrade DAGs to Airflow 2.11.1
scan DAG files for deprecated operators
qualityWhy: It gives concrete version-by-version breaking-change lists, grep scan commands and remediation steps, though some sections are thin and the Airflow 3 details sit in a separate reference file.
needs: Google Cloud account with access to a Managed Service for Apache Airflow (Cloud Composer) environment
why: The skill is built around the Google Cloud managed Airflow service: it downloads DAGs from a GCS bucket, reads the environment through gcloud, and deploys back to GCS, which is a cloud place to run things. Under the local-first rule that makes it value none and skip, even though the code-migration guidance itself is sound.

summary: This skill guides an agent to generate a project-local verification skill that drives an app the way a user would, covering launch, a read-only health check, scripted interaction, evidence capture, and cleanup. It is written for developers who want a repeatable way to prove UI, CLI or service behaviour in their own repository. The generated output also includes a feature map seeded from routes or commands.
tasks: generate a verification skill for this repo
make a control skill that drives the app like a user
prove a CLI or web UI feature works with captured evidence
seed a feature map of user-facing journeys
qualityWhy: Detailed, ordered steps with explicit proof standards and a referenced example, though it depends on the repo's own tooling and leaves some choices to the agent.
why: It is a generic meta-skill for test-driving any project, useful for building and checking a node's apps, but it is written for Cursor and Claude Code tooling, so an agent would need to adapt its paths and harness choices to Fractera's Next.js and SQLite stack rather than install it as written.

summary: This skill gives an agent a set of templates and rules for handling business invoices and receipts. It covers pulling key fields from an invoice, sorting expenses into categories, naming and filing PDFs by year and vendor, and keeping a register of open and paid invoices. It is aimed at small business owners and bookkeepers who need tidy expense records and tax-ready summaries.
tasks: extract the key fields from an invoice PDF
sort receipts into expense categories
build a filing system for invoices by year and vendor
show unpaid and overdue invoices
summarize expenses for a quarter or tax year
qualityWhy: Most of the file is example tables and illustrative output with no step-by-step procedure, validation checks, or handling of edge cases such as currency conversion or duplicate invoices.
needs: office-mcp server providing PDF and spreadsheet tools
why: Useful for a business that runs a shop or service on a node and needs its own expense records, but it is not a build or content tool. It is written as a plain instruction set with no stack dependencies, though it assumes the office-mcp tools are present, which a node may not have.

summary: The skill guides an agent to sequence work by removing complexity before adding to it. It asks for dead code, redundant validators and stub references to be cut first, and for features to be built only against observed usage rather than speculative edge cases. It is aimed at engineers and agents evolving or rewriting an existing system.
tasks: refactor a module by removing dead code first
simplify prompts and remove redundant instructions
plan a rewrite starting from the smallest working base
remove speculative validators not required by the spec
qualityWhy: It states a clear principle with a short list of rules, but it gives no concrete steps, examples or checks an agent can follow.
why: It is a stack-free design habit that can help when refactoring or planning a node's code, but it is only a short set of principles, so it is useful now and then rather than central to building or selling a product.

summary: The skill describes how an agent could control Spotify playback, such as play, pause, volume and shuffle, and manage playlists by creating them and adding tracks. It also covers finding music through recommendations and reading audio features like energy and tempo. It is aimed at people who want music automation, such as daily mixes or party playlists.
tasks: create a workout playlist from high-energy tracks
generate a daily music mix from recent listening
control playback for a party
analyse the mood of a playlist
qualityWhy: It is mostly YAML sketches and a short API snippet with no setup steps, auth flow, error handling or verification, and the MCP server it depends on is never explained.
why: Spotify is a cloud music service, so playback and playlists live outside the node's local files and data, which makes this a skip under the local-first rule. The skill also depends on an unexplained media-mcp server and is too thin to follow reliably.

summary: This skill gives an agent a command-line tool that pulls stock prices, quotes, fundamentals, earnings dates, dividends, analyst ratings, options chains, price history, and symbol search from Yahoo Finance. It is aimed at someone who wants quick market research from the terminal. It needs no API key, and it runs through uv with inline Python dependencies.
tasks: check the current price of a stock
compare fundamentals of several tech companies
list upcoming earnings dates and dividend history
pull an options chain for an ETF
qualityWhy: The commands and examples are clear, but the bundled yf script is not shown, and the file gives no verification or error-handling steps beyond a short troubleshooting list.
why: Stock data is useful for market research but serves little of what a node is built for, and yfinance scrapes Yahoo Finance without an official API, so results can break; the skill is skipped because its install step pipes a remote script directly into a shell.
risks: The install instructions run a remote script with curl piped into sh (curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh), which executes code downloaded from the internet without a check.

summary: This skill guides an agent to turn raw change inputs, such as commit messages, feature lists or bug reports, into structured changelogs and release notes. It offers a Keep a Changelog layout, a plain-language 'what's new' version for users, and a technical version for developers. It also covers conventional commit types, semantic versioning and tips for writing entries from the user's point of view. The intended readers are product developers and product managers who ship versioned software.
tasks: turn git commits into a changelog
write release notes for version 2.0
draft a user-friendly what's new post
categorize changes by added, fixed and removed
qualityWhy: It gives useful templates and examples but has few concrete steps or checks for building a changelog from real repository history, and it admits it cannot read git.
why: Writing release notes for a product is a direct part of building and running it, and the guidance is stack-free text work. The listed office-mcp tools are optional document export that a node may not have, so the agent should write Markdown directly; the skill itself has no outside service or secret requirement.

summary: This skill gives an agent a working style for software tasks: short replies, careful use of subagents, and checks before anything is called done. It also has a set of playbooks for bugs, features, refactors, performance work, and PR review and merging, with helper scripts that check plan files and watch pull request status through GitHub. It is written for a developer team working inside the Cursor editor.
tasks: review and land a stack of pull requests
triage automated review comments on a PR
diagnose a bug from runtime evidence
plan a multi-phase refactor with checks
qualityWhy: The playbooks are detailed and include checks, but they depend on many other skills and Cursor-only tools that are not included, so an agent cannot follow them standalone.
needs: GitHub account and gh CLI login
Cursor editor with its Task tool and subagent types
why: It helps with engineering process, not with building or running a Fractera product directly, so its value is occasional. It cannot be installed as written because it assumes Cursor's Task tool, its own subagent types, and missing bundled skills, so it should be read for its ideas and rebuilt for the node's own workflow.

summary: This skill guides an agent through building and reviewing SwiftUI views for iOS 26 and newer, covering state ownership with @Observable, @State, @Bindable and @Environment, splitting views into subviews, environment values, async loading with .task, previews with deterministic fixtures, and migration away from older APIs. It is aimed at developers who build native iOS apps. The skill is detailed and points to sibling skills for navigation, layout, animation and Liquid Glass.
tasks: refactor a SwiftUI view into smaller subviews
manage @Observable state in an iOS app
add async data loading to a SwiftUI screen
migrate deprecated SwiftUI APIs
write isolated previews for loading, empty and error states
qualityWhy: The instructions are concrete, with code examples, a workflow, a review checklist and clear references to deeper files, though some details rely on the reader knowing Apple's APIs.
why: The skill is for native iOS apps written in Swift, which a Fractera node (Next.js, React, TypeScript, SQLite) does not serve, so it is not useful on a node and would need a full rewrite to fit the stack.

summary: The skill guides an agent to read meeting transcripts from a local folder and report on the user's communication habits, such as avoiding conflict, filler words, speaking share, interruptions and listening. It returns quoted examples with timestamps, suggested rephrasings, and a summary with next steps. It is aimed at professionals who want to improve their communication and leadership.
tasks: analyze my meeting transcripts for conflict avoidance
count my filler words and speaking ratio across meetings
prepare performance review examples from my meetings
compare my facilitation style between two periods
qualityWhy: The instructions are concrete, with a step-by-step procedure, an output template and worked examples, though they never say how to compute timestamps or speaking ratios from the raw transcript formats.
why: It analyses personal meeting transcripts for communication coaching and does not help build, run, sell or make content for a product, so the value is none. It is a writing-and-review habit rather than a risk, but the use is skip because value is none.

summary: This skill guides an agent to rewrite engineering-team material, such as JIRA comments and technical notes, into plain status updates for engineering leadership, product managers and release managers. It adapts the same content to the channel where it will be read: a JIRA comment, a Slack post, an async standup line, an email, or talking points for a meeting. The rules keep product names, ticket keys and PR numbers while removing function names, file paths and code identifiers, and they forbid inventing facts or owners. Posting is limited to JIRA and only after explicit approval; all other channels are handled by the user copying the draft.
tasks: rewrite a JIRA bug comment as a leadership status update
turn an engineering fix into a Slack post for managers
write a short async standup note about a bug fix
draft talking points for a status meeting with leads
qualityWhy: The skill gives clear channel shapes, tone rules, a worked example across three channels, and explicit approval and posting rules, though it relies on a referenced jira-check flow that is not included.
needs: JIRA account and API access for optional ticket reads and posts
why: It is a writing aid for teams that report engineering work upward, useful now and then for a product that is built and run on a node, but not core to building the product itself. It calls the JIRA API, which the person must configure, and it references a jira-check approval flow that the file does not define.

summary: This skill teaches an agent to find the structure of a scanned or digital document page: text blocks, titles, headings, tables, figures and their reading order. It uses the surya Python library, with Python snippets for detection, layout, reading order and OCR. It suits someone who needs to pull structured content out of PDFs or page images.
tasks: analyze the layout of a document page
find tables and figures in a PDF
determine the reading order of a scanned page
extract headings and paragraphs from a document image
qualityWhy: The skill has concrete snippets and a table of element types, but the description field is empty, several helpers such as boxes_overlap and element.position are undefined, and the surya API calls look unverified and may not match current releases.
why: Document layout analysis can help build content pipelines, but it is a Python tool and the node is TypeScript, so an agent would need to rebuild it on the node's stack rather than install it as written. Surya runs locally, though its models may be downloaded on first use.

summary: This skill guides an agent through AWS security work: reading the configuration and findings of GuardDuty, Inspector, Security Hub, Macie, Detective, Security Lake and Organizations policies, and advising on which security service to adopt or how to improve coverage. It is written for security engineers and cloud administrators who need factual, read-only snapshots of an AWS account's security posture. The procedures are organised as a routing table with per-service reference files and a large set of coverage-gap rules.
tasks: check whether GuardDuty is fully deployed across accounts
summarize open Inspector vulnerability findings
review Security Hub compliance standards and failing controls
recommend which AWS security services to enable for a web app
qualityWhy: The instructions are concrete, with a routing table, evidence states, read-only rules and explicit scope limits, but the sheer number of cross-referenced rules makes it dense and some workflow steps depend on reference files that were not part of the review.
needs: AWS account with credentials for the security services
AWS CLI or AWS MCP access

summary: The skill is a long reference document describing a podcast production pipeline: planning, recording, editing and mastering audio, writing show notes, generating RSS feeds, publishing to podcast platforms, promoting episodes on social media, and tracking analytics. summary: This skill walks an agent through creating a Salesforce Commerce B2B store in the org's setup UI, confirming the store name, listing the Digital Experience sites that were generated, and retrieving the storefront metadata into a project with the sf CLI. summary: This skill guides an agent through designing and building a Model Context Protocol server that lets an LLM call an outside service through well-chosen tools. It covers planning around real agent workflows, input schemas, error messages, Python (FastMCP) and TypeScript (MCP SDK) implementation, and a test harness that scores the server with question-and-answer evaluations. It is aimed at developers who want their agents to reach external APIs.

design agent-friendly tool names and error messages

network access to fetch MCP documentation

The TypeScript guide fits the node's TypeScript stack, while the Python parts are unused there; the evaluation script calls a paid Anthropic API that the person chooses to use.

summary: This skill teaches an agent to write docassemble interview files in YAML: question screens, conditional branches that change with earlier answers, typed input fields, and documents assembled from the answers. It is aimed at people who need intake forms, questionnaires or document-assembly flows, such as legal intake. The skill includes a complete example of a client intake interview.

create a conditional form that changes based on answers
generate a contract from form answers
design a multi-step document assembly interview

The skill does not explain how an interview would connect to the node's data element.

summary: This skill guides an agent through adding user-facing strings to LobeHub's react-i18next setup: flat dot-notation keys in the default locale package, parameter interpolation, namespace export, and how to update existing English text so generated locales get re-translated. It is aimed at developers maintaining the LobeHub codebase rather than at people building their own product.

rename or update an existing locale key

fix missing translations in locale files

why: It is a LobeHub-internal guide tied to its packages/locales layout and lobe-i18n tooling, so it is only useful for node elements that use react-i18next and must be adapted to the node's own locale folders; it is not a stack-free habit. Its i18n conventions (flat keys, namespaces) are still useful ideas for a Fractera site.

summary: This skill guides an agent through auditing a business's Google Business Profile, comparing it with nearby competitors, and mapping its Google Maps visibility with a rank grid. It is written for local businesses and agencies who need to see why a storefront or service area does or does not appear in the local pack. The agent works through the OpenSEO MCP tools, saves findings to project context, and delivers a formatted report with an SVG rank grid.
tasks: audit my Google Business Profile
compare my listing to local competitors
map where my business ranks in Google Maps
find out why I don't show in the local pack
prioritize local SEO fixes for a location
qualityWhy: The instructions are concrete, with ordered steps, tool roles, cost guardrails, and a detailed SVG and widget format, though a few dependencies (seo-report, OpenSEO MCP) are assumed rather than explained.

a Google Business Profile listing to audit
why: Local SEO audits serve businesses that run sites and storefronts, so it is useful now and then, but the skill is built around the OpenSEO MCP and its project-context tools, which a Fractera node does not ship, so it would need adapting to the node's own data and report setup. The per-point paid SERP calls are a cost the person must choose.

summary: The skill lets an agent look up live Azure retail prices from the public Azure Retail Prices API by building OData filters on service, region, SKU and price type. It also covers estimating Copilot Studio agent credit consumption by fetching current Microsoft billing rates and applying simple formulas. It is aimed at people who need Azure cost figures or comparisons for a workload or agent.
tasks: compare D4s v5 VM prices across regions
estimate monthly cost of an Azure Functions app
estimate Copilot Studio credit usage for an agent
check reserved instance versus pay-as-you-go pricing

why: Azure is a cloud platform and administration/pricing service, which a local-first node treats as value none, so it is skipped even though the price lookup itself is read-only and needs no account.

summary: This skill tells an agent to settle the core data structures and types before writing logic, and to trace how the data is accessed. It also covers sequencing setup work (CI, linting, test infrastructure, shared types) ahead of features, and isolating shared state when concurrent actors might modify it. It is written for developers making structural and code-level design choices in any project.
tasks: design the core data types before writing logic
decide the order of setup work versus feature work
check whether shared state needs isolating for concurrent access
avoid premature abstraction when refactoring duplicate code
qualityWhy: It gives useful guiding principles, but it is short and abstract, with no steps, examples or checks an agent can follow directly.
why: It is a stack-free design habit that helps any node project's structural decisions, but it offers little concrete procedure, so its effect depends on how the agent applies it.

summary: This skill teaches an agent to add coss.com to a project for sending email and SMS, one-time codes, and webhooks. It covers getting a development key through the CLI, writing server-side SDK calls that check the returned error object, and giving an AI agent its own inbox. It also explains how to verify webhook signatures, test webhooks locally, and inspect delivery logs. The intended users are developers building apps or agents that need to message their own users.

give my AI agent its own email address
send a one-time login code by SMS
receive and verify webhooks from an email service locally
find out why an email was not delivered
