Anthropic or OpenAI keys, if those providers are used
why: Genkit Go is for Go servers, while a Fractera node is built on Next.js and TypeScript, so the skill's Go code would not fit the node's stack. Its install step pipes a remote script into bash, which is the reason for skipping it.
risks: The Genkit CLI install step runs a remote script downloaded from cli.genkit.dev piped straight into bash.

summary: This skill teaches an agent how to design Inngest events: naming them, shaping their payloads, and using IDs to prevent duplicates. It also covers scheduling with the ts field, fanning one event out to several handlers, and reacting to Inngest's system events such as failed function runs. It is written for TypeScript developers who build background jobs on Inngest's hosted service.
tasks: design an event-driven workflow for a web app
fan one event out to several handlers
make webhook event handling idempotent
alert on failed background function runs
qualityWhy: The examples are concrete and clear, but the skill refers to a missing expressions reference and other skills, and it states that timestamped events are always processed in order without support.
why: Inngest is a hosted cloud service, so events and function runs go through a third party, which conflicts with the node's local-first design and its own SQLite element for data. The general ideas about naming, idempotency and fan-out are useful, but the code depends on Inngest's cloud and SDK, not on the node's stack.

summary: This skill guides an agent through writing and tuning Apache Spark jobs in PySpark or Scala: DataFrame transformations, Spark SQL, RDD pipelines, shuffle and memory configuration, skew handling, caching, and structured streaming. It is aimed at data engineers who run large batch or streaming pipelines over files such as Parquet. The main file gives a workflow, a few code patterns, and do/don't rules, with five reference documents loaded on demand.
tasks: optimize a slow Spark SQL join
write a PySpark ETL pipeline for parquet files
tune executor memory and shuffle partitions
fix data skew in a Spark aggregation
build a structured streaming job with watermarks
qualityWhy: The main file is concrete, with a workflow, runnable code examples, explicit constraints, and checks such as partition counts and shuffle spill, backed by five detailed reference files.
why: Spark is a batch and streaming engine that runs on the person's own machine or cluster, not a product stack the node replaces, so the skill fits a node as written; it is useful only when the person builds big-data pipelines, which is less central to sites, apps and content than the node's main purposes. The example code reads from s3:// paths, which is only a sample and needs no account by itself.

summary: The skill has an agent rewrite one source article or announcement into separate versions for LinkedIn, X, Reddit, an English blog and WeChat. Before writing, it asks whether to use first or third person and which platforms to target. Each platform gets its own reference guide covering tone, format and length, and the skill points to a separate style skill to remove AI-sounding patterns. It is aimed at people who publish content across social networks and blogs.
tasks: rewrite a blog post for LinkedIn and X
adapt an announcement for a Reddit community
turn an article into a WeChat post
make an English blog version of my content

why: It directly serves making social posts and blog content for a product, and it needs no stack or outside service. It depends on a remove-ai-style skill that is referenced but not included here, so that part may need installing separately.

summary: This skill tells an agent to build a single self-contained HTML file, choosing a visual direction from the user's brief, project, and subject matter. It routes wireframe, prototype, plan, and diagram requests to more specialised sibling skills, and otherwise loads reference guides for documents, presentations, interfaces, diagrams, and charts. It is aimed at people who need reports, explainers, landing pages, tools, or data stories delivered as one file that opens without a build step.

build an interactive data story from a dataset
turn this report into a presentation-style HTML artifact
create a small calculator tool as one HTML file

why: It produces standalone HTML artifacts that run locally with no service, which fits a node that builds pages and content, and it is stack-free, so it does not need adapting to the node's own stack. Its sibling skills are optional, and it does not depend on any outside account.

summary: This skill lets an agent pull YouTube data from a hosted pay-per-call service instead of the official YouTube Data API. It covers searching videos, channels and playlists with filters for upload date, duration and sort order, looking up channels, reading a channel's videos, shorts and live streams, and fetching video details, comments, playlist contents, hashtag feeds and regional trending. It is aimed at people doing trend research, channel monitoring or data collection for content work, without setting up a Google developer project or dealing with daily quotas.
tasks: find recent YouTube videos on a topic for content research
monitor a channel's new uploads, shorts and live streams
pull comments from a video for audience analysis
check trending YouTube videos in a specific country
collect playlist or hashtag video lists for a data pipeline

why: It is a hosted paid YouTube data service, not a local tool, so it is useful for research and monitoring but does not build or run a product directly; it fits the node as an outside data source that returns results to local files. Per-call payment means an agent can spend money if the key or wallet is connected, and the skill states that failed upstream calls are not refunded.

summary: This skill guides an agent through auditing a LinkedIn Ads account. It covers measurement and Insight Tag conversions, professional audiences, lead gen forms, account-based marketing, creative, bidding, pacing, automation and policy. Its output is structured findings and prioritized recommendations, with proposed changes kept as drafts. It is aimed at marketers and founders who run B2B paid campaigns.

check Insight Tag and conversion tracking
review lead gen form setup
find wasted spend in B2B campaigns

why: B2B ad audits are useful occasionally rather than in the core build-and-run flow of a node. It works only with a LinkedIn account the person chooses to use, and as shipped it depends on a parent plugin's ads/ folder, so the skill would need that folder installed alongside it.

summary: This skill guides an agent through securing AI agents on Google Cloud Agent Gateway. It covers inbound client traffic and outbound tool calls, with content filtering, IAP-based access rules and a shared agent registry. It produces YAML and JSON policy files, gcloud and Terraform steps, and verification commands for cloud engineers who run agents on Google's platform.
tasks: secure a multi-agent system on Google Cloud
write Agent Gateway ingress and egress policy files
set up Model Armor filters for prompt injection
verify agent tool calls through an egress gateway
qualityWhy: The files are concrete with commands and templates, but they contain contradictory rules (no execution versus direct delivery), hardcoded example values, and some unverified limits.
why: It configures cloud infrastructure and cloud-hosted agent runtimes, which is cloud administration rather than building or running a local node, so it is not useful here. It also depends on a cloud platform for all of its runtime and data.

summary: This skill tells an agent how to audit a YouTube Ads account: campaign setup, video inventory, Shorts, in-stream and CTV placements, creative, audiences, brand safety, bidding and measurement. It works read-only, turns the findings into structured observations and prioritised recommendations, and keeps any account change as a draft. review video ad creative and hooks for Shorts and in-stream
check brand safety and audience settings on YouTube campaigns
find measurement and bidding problems in YouTube ads
qualityWhy: The file is a short procedure that depends on references and a plugin structure (ads/references/youtube-audit.md, the ads operating contract) that are not included, so an agent cannot follow most of its steps from this folder alone.
needs: YouTube Ads account access or exported campaign data
the ads plugin reference files (ads/references/youtube-audit.md and the shared ads contract)
why: It is an advertising audit tool, useful now and then for a product's marketing, and it reads a paid YouTube Ads account, which the person chooses to connect. Without the referenced files it is only a partial guide, so an agent would need those files or would have to work from general knowledge.

summary: This skill lets an agent drive the person's already-open Chrome browser through the agent-browser command-line tool. It reuses logged-in tabs, fills forms, clicks buttons, takes screenshots and reads page text. It also replays Chrome DevTools Recorder exports. It is written for posting and commenting on social platforms such as X, LinkedIn, Reddit, Dev.to and Hacker News, with per-platform notes and a rule to confirm before anything is published.
tasks: post an announcement to X and LinkedIn
reply to comments on Reddit or Hacker News
publish an article to Dev.to from a draft
replay a recorded browser workflow from a DevTools export
take screenshots of a web page for review
qualityWhy: It gives concrete commands, a step-by-step interaction guide, known limitations and a confirm-before-publish rule, though it leaves some platform-specific details to separate reference files.
needs: logged-in accounts on X, LinkedIn, Reddit, Dev.to or Hacker News
why: It is useful for posting social content, but it is a browser-control tool for third-party sites rather than something that builds or runs a product. It is marked skip because it tells the agent to run an unpinned npm package via npx -y agent-browser@latest, which downloads and executes remote code, and it asks the person to expose their logged-in Chrome to local control.
risks: Runs the unpinned latest npm package via `npx -y agent-browser@latest`, which downloads and executes remote code.
Asks the person to enable Chrome remote debugging on port 9222, letting any local process control their logged-in browser and sessions.

summary: This skill teaches an agent to query a paid third-party Yelp data service over plain HTTP. It can search local businesses by keyword and location, sort the results by rating or review count, and fetch a business's full details or its reviews by ID or Yelp URL slug. It is aimed at people researching restaurants and local services, or tracking competitors in a area, without applying for the official Yelp Fusion API.
tasks: find the highest-rated ramen restaurants in a city
pull the latest reviews for a competitor's business
look up full details for a business from its Yelp URL
compare local service providers by review count

why: It is useful for local business research and review analysis, but it is not core to building or running a node's own product, and it depends on an outside paid service the person must choose and fund. Whether this data use fits Yelp's terms of service is not addressed in the skill.

summary: This skill teaches an agent how to write durable TypeScript workflows with Inngest step methods. Each step is retried and tracked separately, so a process restart does not lose progress. It covers delays, waits for outside events or signals with timeouts, calling other functions, looping over paginated APIs, and running steps in parallel. It is aimed at developers who need long-running background logic that survives failures.
tasks: add a 24-hour delay before sending a follow-up email
wait for human approval with a timeout
poll an external API without losing state on crashes
run several API calls in parallel inside a workflow
call one background function from another and use its result

why: Durable workflows are useful for running sites and agents, but Inngest is not part of the node's stack, so an agent would need to adapt it to the node's own job tools rather than install it as written. Some steps call the Inngest service, which needs the person's account and keys.

summary: This skill makes an agent apply professional typography to any screen text it writes, such as HTML, CSS, React components, landing pages and dashboards. It covers curly quotes, dash and hyphen choice, ellipses, non-breaking spaces, line length, line height, heading hierarchy and font pairing. It also has an audit mode for finding and fixing typographic mistakes in existing interfaces. The main users are developers and designers building web interfaces or content pages.

fix quotes, dashes and spacing in a React component
review a dashboard layout for readability
set line length and heading hierarchy in CSS
audit existing UI text for typographic errors

why: It is a stack-free set of rules that applies directly to the HTML, CSS and React UI a node builds, with no install step or outside service. Some guidance needs checking against real output, such as the ellipsis spacing and the ch-unit advice.

summary: This skill lets an agent answer questions about a codebase by querying a previously generated knowledge graph stored as JSON in the project's data folder. It first checks whether the graph is stale against git changes, then searches node names, summaries and tags, follows edges to build a small neighbourhood of related files and functions, and uses layer metadata to explain architecture. It is aimed at developers who want quick, referenced answers about unfamiliar code.
tasks: explain how a module in this codebase works
find which files handle a given feature
trace dependencies of a function
check whether the code graph is up to date before answering
qualityWhy: The steps are concrete, with exact grep and git commands, a documented graph schema, freshness checks and fallbacks, though it lacks worked examples of answers.
why: It is a developer-tool skill for reading code, not for building or running a Fractera product, so value is only occasional. It depends on a graph generated by a separate /understand command and assumes git and the .understand-anything or .ua folder layout, so it is not a drop-in fit for the node's own stack and should be read for its ideas.

summary: This skill tells an agent to restate its previous message in plain, simple language with no jargon, as if one person were explaining to another. It is a single-file prompt with no scripts or stack dependencies. It suits anyone who wants a clearer second version of an answer.
tasks: explain the last answer in simpler words
rewrite my previous message without jargon
make a technical reply easier to understand
qualityWhy: The whole instruction is two sentences with no examples, checks or steps, so an agent gets only a generic direction to simplify.
why: It is a stack-free writing aid that can be useful now and then for a product's text or support replies, but it does little beyond what a normal rewrite request already does. No risks were found in its single file.

summary: This skill ranks an Elastic Security alert queue by a weighted risk score that combines each alert's base risk, a MITRE tactic boost, workflow status modifiers, and optional entity risk and asset criticality boosts. It then groups alerts by host or user so an analyst can see where to start. It is aimed at security analysts who want a prioritized shortlist before deeper investigation, and it is read-only.
tasks: rank the open security alerts by urgency
show which hosts or users have the most urgent alerts this shift
prioritize a set of alert IDs before investigating
find the alert group to start investigating first
qualityWhy: The skill gives a concrete scoring formula, a full ES|QL query, grouping rules, enrichment steps, output format and explicit guidelines, with only small gaps such as the tie-breaking and the entity-grouping approximation it openly documents.
needs: Elastic Security deployment with Kibana 8.x or 9.x
Elasticsearch credentials for the security alerts index
why: The skill is built around Elastic Security alerts, a SIEM run on Elasticsearch, which is not a product a Fractera node builds or sells, so its value to the node's purposes is none. It is also a cloud-hosted monitoring service used for security operations, not for building sites, apps, agents or content, so it is skipped rather than adapted.

summary: This skill gives an agent a security-testing playbook for finding and confirming server-side request forgery in web apps that fetch URLs. It covers how to spot likely parameters, test filter bypasses for localhost and cloud metadata addresses, and use alternative protocols such as gopher and file. It also describes how such a flaw could be chained toward internal services and remote code execution. The target audience is penetration testers and security reviewers.
tasks: test a web app for server-side request forgery
check whether a URL fetch parameter reaches internal services
assess URL allowlist filters in a security review
qualityWhy: The playbook is concrete, with payload lists, a confirmation methodology and a decision tree, though it is mostly a catalogue and gives no authorization or scope checks.
why: It is an offensive attack reference rather than material for building, running, selling or making content on a Fractera node, so it does not serve the node's purpose. Its exploit chains, such as a Redis cron reverse shell and Docker container escape, are unsuitable for an agent on someone's own node.
risks: Contains exploit chains (Redis-to-cron reverse shell, Docker API container escape, cloud credential theft) that an agent could run against systems the person does not own.

summary: This skill guides an agent through hard workplace talks such as performance concerns, peer conflicts, critical feedback, and pay requests. It walks the user through preparing the issue, their emotions, and the other person's view, then delivering the talk and following up. It is aimed at employees and managers who need to handle a sensitive conversation at work.
tasks: prepare for a hard talk with a colleague
plan feedback about a team member's missed deadlines
get ready to ask a manager for a raise
work through a conflict with a peer
qualityWhy: The framework and example openings are clear, but the content is generic workplace advice and the detailed reference files are not included for checking.
why: This is general interpersonal and HR-style advice with no link to building, running, selling or making content for a product on a Fractera node. Nothing in it is a risk, but it does not serve what nodes are for.

summary: This skill lets an agent find Mermaid diagram blocks in Markdown or other text files, render each one to a PNG through the mermaid.ink web service, and save the images in the project's image folder. It then swaps the code blocks for image links. It suits people publishing docs or posts on platforms that cannot draw Mermaid themselves.
tasks: convert mermaid diagrams in a markdown file to png
replace mermaid code blocks with image links for a blog post
render all architecture diagrams under docs as images
prepare static diagram images for a github pages site

needs: mermaid.ink (public rendering API, no key required)
why: It is useful for making diagrams for docs and posts, and the images land in local project folders. The diagram text is sent inside the URL to mermaid.ink, a third-party service, so the person should avoid sending confidential architecture; the skill does not warn about this.

summary: This skill teaches an agent to read and write Apple Health data on iOS using Swift and the HealthKit framework. It covers permission requests, sample and statistics queries for charts, saving samples, background delivery, and live workout sessions. It is aimed at developers building native iPhone, Apple Watch or iPad apps that work with health and fitness data.
tasks: add Apple Health step count to an iPhone app
chart daily heart rate from HealthKit

enable background health data updates

summary: This skill lets an agent turn audio or video recordings into written text by calling OpenAI's transcription service through a bundled Python command-line script. extract text from a voice note

why: Transcription directly serves making content and building voice or video features, and the result is saved back to local files, but the audio is sent to OpenAI, so it needs the person's key and paid use. The script was truncated at 8000 characters, so its remaining code was not reviewed, and the default $CODEX_HOME install path would need a look on a Fractera node.

summary: This skill lets an agent create flat, minimal illustration images for articles, docs, and concept visuals. create a 16:9 concept visual for a landing page
produce a square social post image
qualityWhy: The skill gives clear provider selection, a concrete script with options, prompt examples, output-path rules and a verification step, but the reference files and the end of the script were not visible to check.
why: It directly serves making article and documentation images, but it depends on a paid image API the person must choose and key-authorise. The Gemini path sends the key in the request URL, which is the usual Google pattern but worth knowing about; the script's tail was cut off, so its full behaviour is not verified.

summary: Gives an agent a structured way to find production behaviors that the existing tests would not notice if changed, by reasoning about likely mutations and checking which public outcomes are unasserted. It works from the caller's view, ranks gaps by risk, and only runs mutation experiments when the person asks for verification or test additions. A separate read-only mode grades individual tests for a grading workflow. The skill is aimed at engineers reviewing test quality, and it is written around .NET but is described as polyglot.
tasks: check whether the tests would catch a bug in this component
find behavioral blind spots in the test suite
verify surviving mutations for a named risk
grade individual tests read-only
qualityWhy: The instructions are concrete and detailed, with decision tables, ranking rules, witness-based checks and an output contract, though some sections are dense and assume a .NET context.
why: Testing-quality analysis is useful now and then for building a product, but this skill is written for a .NET stack and its commands and references would need adapting to the node's Next.js, TypeScript and Vitest-style setup, so it is for reading rather than direct install. It has no outside service dependency and no risky operations, since execution happens only on explicit request and mutations are reverted.

summary: This skill tells an agent to build a new-joiner guide for a codebase from an existing knowledge graph file. The agent checks whether the graph is still current against recent git changes, then pulls out the project metadata, architecture layers, guided tour and key file summaries. It assembles these into a markdown guide with an overview, key concepts, a file map and a list of complexity hotspots. It is aimed at team leads and developers who need to bring someone new up to speed on a project.
tasks: write an onboarding guide for a new developer
summarise the architecture of this project for a new hire
create a codebase walkthrough from the knowledge graph
list the complex files a newcomer should be careful with

why: It produces project documentation from a graph file rather than building or running a product, so it is useful now and then rather than core to the node. It needs a graph already generated by /understand and a git repository for the freshness check, and it works as written with no stack dependency.

summary: This skill lets an agent judge whether a reported security finding is a real vulnerability or a false alarm. It reads the relevant source code, follows the request path from routing through middleware to the handler, and checks whether the claimed protection is actually missing. When a live instance is available, it can also replay requests through a proxy to confirm exploitability. The result is a determination with confidence, evidence, and a fix or close recommendation, and it is aimed at developers and security reviewers.
tasks: validate a scanner finding against the code
check if a reported vulnerability is real
decide whether a security finding is a false positive
confirm an authorization flaw with a live request
qualityWhy: The workflow, classification categories, report format and persistence step are concrete and followable, but the reference patterns file is very short and the proxy steps depend on tooling the skill does not explain.
needs: reaper proxy for optional live testing
a reachable live instance of the application for live testing
why: It directly helps someone running their own app or site decide which security findings to fix, and it is mostly stack-independent code reading. Live testing sends attack requests to a running application, and the skill does not state that the tester must be authorized, so the user should only point it at systems they own or may test.

summary: This skill lets an agent work out how many shares of a long stock trade to buy so that a set percentage of the account is at risk. It supports fixed-fraction risk, volatility-based stops using Average True Range, and Kelly-criterion sizing, and can cap positions by account share or sector exposure. It is aimed at traders and investors who want disciplined risk limits before placing an order.
tasks: calculate how many shares to buy for a stock trade
size a position so that only 1% of the account is at risk
compare position sizes using ATR-based stops
check whether a trade fits sector concentration limits
qualityWhy: The steps, formulas, worked examples, edge-case rules and a test suite are concrete and consistent, with only small gaps such as the stop being partly ignored in some modes.
why: It only does stock-trade position sizing, which has nothing to do with building, running, selling or making content for a node product, so it is not useful for a Fractera node. It needs no keys and carries no risk, but the value is none, so the use is skip.

summary: This skill tells an agent to merge results from the dependency, secrets and code scanners already run on a repository into one prioritized security report. It keeps only high-confidence findings, sorts them by severity, and inlines the full detail of high and medium issues so the report is self-contained. It is aimed at developers and security reviewers who want a single overview of a project's risks.
tasks: make a combined security report
summarize vulnerabilities from all scans
prioritize high-confidence security findings
produce a full security audit overview
qualityWhy: The steps are concrete and ordered, but they depend on finding files and a template from sibling skills that are not included, and the report template is only referenced, so an agent cannot fully check the output.
why: It is a security-reporting workflow tied to the Ghost scan skills and their folder layout, which a Fractera node does not provide, so it would need adapting to the node's own scan output. It does not touch cloud services or send data out, so it is safe to read, but it is only occasionally useful for building or running a product.

summary: This skill walks a person through a short interview that prepares a daily standup or meeting update. It can pull recent activity from GitHub, Jira and the person's own Claude Code session history, but only after asking for consent each time. The agent then combines those results with the answers into a short Markdown update for yesterday, today, blockers and discussion topics. It is aimed at developers and team leads who report progress in standups.
tasks: prepare my daily standup update
summarise what I did yesterday for the team sync
list my blockers and topics for the meeting
pull my recent GitHub and Jira activity for a status update
qualityWhy: The skill gives a clear phase-by-phase workflow, question wording, an output template, examples and anti-patterns, but it does not give the exact gh or jira commands for pulling data and it points to a global ~/.claude path.
needs: Jira account via jira CLI or Atlassian MCP (optional)
why: It is a useful productivity habit for teams but does not help build, run or sell a product directly, so value is some. It uses the person's own GitHub and Jira accounts only when they approve, so use is install-with-service; the SKILL.md refers to a global ~/.claude/skills path, which the node should adapt to its own element folder.

summary: This skill lets an agent read a brokerage account through the Longbridge CLI: total assets, holdings, cash flow, statements and margin figures. It can also preview and place orders and recurring investment plans, and run portfolio analyses such as risk metrics, rebalancing and tax-loss harvesting. It is aimed at individual investors managing their own trading accounts.
tasks: check my portfolio's total assets and holdings
explain my unrealised profit and loss
plan a rebalance of my portfolio
run a VaR and drawdown risk analysis on my holdings
preview and place a buy order on my brokerage account
qualityWhy: The skill gives a clear routing table, auth rules, a dry-run confirmation flow for orders and detailed US-account caveats, but its analysis references depend on outside data and some steps are only summarised.
why: It is a personal brokerage and investment tool, not something for building, running or selling a site, app or content, and it relies on a cloud broker account. It places real trades on the person's money, so it is skipped rather than installed on a node.

summary: This skill guides an agent through creating a Claude Code plugin: it sets up the folder layout, writes the plugin.json manifest, and registers the plugin in a marketplace.json file. It also covers adding commands, skills, agents, hooks and MCP servers, testing a plugin locally with /plugin commands, and bumping semantic versions in both manifests. The main users are developers who publish Claude Code plugins to a marketplace.
tasks: scaffold a new Claude Code plugin
register a plugin in a marketplace manifest
bump a plugin's semantic version
test a local plugin with the /plugin commands
qualityWhy: The steps, commands, directory layouts and the two helper scripts are concrete and easy to follow, though there are no automated checks and a few README references point to files that may not exist.
why: It is a developer tool for the Claude Code plugin marketplace rather than for building a site, app, agent or content, so its use on a node is occasional. It is stack-free and works on local files, so it needs no adaptation and no outside service.

summary: This skill teaches an agent to manage Coralogix alert definitions through the cx command-line tool. It covers listing, inspecting, creating, enabling, disabling and deleting alerts, plus suppression rules for maintenance windows. It also gives JSON templates for several alert types, priority levels, and a short investigation flow for alerts that are currently firing. It is aimed at site-reliability and operations staff who watch logs, metrics and traces in Coralogix.
tasks: list the firing alerts in Coralogix
create a logs threshold alert for high error rates
mute an noisy alert temporarily
set up a maintenance window suppression rule
qualityWhy: It gives concrete commands, JSON examples, a create-then-verify workflow and reference files, but the alert type enum is inconsistent between the table and the examples (for example LOGS_IMMEDIATE vs LOGS_IMMEDIATE_OR_UNSPECIFIED).
needs: Coralogix API key configured as a cx CLI profile
why: Coralogix is a cloud observability service, and this skill administers alert rules that live in that cloud account rather than in a local node's own data, files or stack, so it does not serve building or running a product on the node. Using it would also send the person's telemetry and alert configuration to a third-party cloud.

summary: This guide walks an agent through live Prometheus cardinality problems, such as memory growth, slow queries, and rising metric bills. It shows how to read the TSDB status endpoint, find the metric and label responsible, check recent changes and series churn, and choose a safe fix. It is aimed at people who run monitoring for a service they operate.
tasks: diagnose Prometheus memory growth
find which metric causes high series count
fix too many samples ingest errors
reduce a Grafana Cloud active series bill
qualityWhy: It gives concrete PromQL, curl commands, symptom tables, and decision trees with clear safety rules, though a few technical claims are stated more firmly than they need to be.
needs: Grafana Cloud account and API token (only for the Grafana Cloud examples)
why: It is a stack-free diagnostic guide for operating monitoring, so it is useful now and then for running a site or app, but it does not build or sell anything. The Grafana Cloud parts need an account the person chooses to use, and the skill is not written for the node's own stack.

summary: This skill lets an agent look up businesses and points of interest by text query, optionally centred on a latitude and longitude. It can also fetch a place's full details, its reviews sorted by relevance, date or rating, and a single review by ID. It is aimed at people building store locators, local directories, or review monitoring, who want Google Maps-style data without setting up Google Cloud billing. Each call is a plain HTTP GET paid per call, either with prepaid credits or in USDC over x402.
tasks: find coffee shops near a given coordinate
pull the newest reviews for a business
build a store locator from place search results
get full details for a place by its feature ID
search local businesses in another language or country
qualityWhy: It gives concrete endpoints, parameters, copy-paste curl examples, MCP config and error codes, but it leaves out response schemas and pagination details and depends on the separate fetcher skill for payment setup.
needs: fetcher.sh API key (bby_live_...) or a USDC wallet for x402 payments
why: Useful for local business data, store locators and review monitoring, but only now and then for building and running a product, so it is not core. It needs a paid third-party service, and the skill does not say how long the service keeps queries or whether Google Maps terms apply to the returned data.

summary: This skill teaches an agent to build 3D scenes in React using React Three Fiber, a React renderer for Three.js, using JSX components, hooks such as useFrame and useThree, and Drei helpers for controls, lighting, text and models. It also ships Python generator scripts that emit component boilerplate and full scene templates, plus a Vite starter project. The target users are front-end developers who want interactive 3D experiences, product configurators or visualisations inside React apps.
tasks: build an interactive 3D product configurator
add an animated 3D model to a React page
create a React Three Fiber scene with lighting and orbit controls
generate R3F component boilerplate
qualityWhy: The SKILL.md is concrete, with many runnable examples, pitfalls and checks, though some snippets are approximate (for example a mixed useRef typing and an unclear TypeScript scene example) and the referenced hooks_guide.md and drei_helpers.md are not among the files.
why: It directly serves building 3D content for a product on a node, but the node's stack is Next.js 16 with React 19 and Tailwind, so R3F would need adapting to the node's own conventions, and the examples use the older zustand `create` default export and an outdated Vite/vanilla setup rather than the App Router. Doubts about version compatibility with React 19 and Next.js 16 are not addressed in the files.

summary: This skill guides an agent through Unity's SpriteAtlas V2 workflow for game projects. It covers generating master and variant atlases during the build, enabling Sprite Packer mode, and choosing between built-in loading and Addressables late-binding. It is written for Unity game developers who want to pack sprites for runtime use.
tasks: set up sprite atlases for a Unity game build
pack sprites into atlases with Addressables late-binding
create variant atlases for different screen resolutions
optimize texture packing settings in a Unity project
qualityWhy: The shipped C# resources and reference files are detailed, but parts of SKILL.md are unfinished, such as a repeated placeholder heading, an empty asset-label row and an empty variant section.
needs: Addressables package for the late-binding option
why: This is Unity game-engine asset tooling, which does not match a Fractera node's stack (Next.js, SQLite, Stripe) or its uses for sites, web apps, AI agents or content. It is not a cloud service risk, so the skill is simply out of scope.

summary: The skill helps an agent pick the correct Google-maintained golden base image for building a custom GKE node image. It maps a user's GKE version, OS, CPU architecture, accelerator, gVisor, cgroup and signed-module needs to a catalogue entry fetched from a public Google JSON map. It is aimed at engineers preparing Kubernetes node images on Google Cloud, not at people building their own sites or content.
tasks: find the golden base image for a custom GKE node
map GKE 1.34 cluster settings to a node image name
choose an ARM or GPU base image for GKE nodes
qualityWhy: The filter logic and defaults are clear, but it gives only one example and no checks for an empty result or a bad version beyond a single line.
needs: Google Cloud account with GKE access
why: It is administration of a cloud container platform (GKE node images on Google Cloud), which is the cloud-administration category that is excluded for a local-first node, so it is value none and use skip. It also requires a Google Cloud account and makes outbound requests to Google's servers.

summary: This skill guides an agent through diagnosing failed DAG runs and task instances in Google Cloud's managed Apache Airflow service. The agent pulls task states and logs with gcloud, downloads the DAG source from the environment's storage bucket, and matches the error evidence against known platform failure modes. It is aimed at engineers who run Airflow pipelines on Google Cloud.
tasks: diagnose why a Composer DAG run failed
find the failing task instance in a DAG run
check Cloud Composer logs for timeouts or zombie tasks
compare DAG source code against task error messages
qualityWhy: It gives concrete commands, a fixed evidence format, step-by-step diagnosis rules and a list of known failure modes with queries and remediation.
needs: Google Cloud account with gcloud access to a Managed Airflow (Cloud Composer) environment
why: It is built around Google Cloud's hosted Airflow service, which is cloud administration rather than something that runs on the person's own computer, so it does not fit a local-first node. The skill itself reads logs and DAG files without any harmful steps; it only sets a metrics attribution variable on gcloud commands.

summary: This skill turns an agent into a product strategist that looks for changes which would multiply a product's value rather than adding small features. It walks through understanding what the product does today, brainstorming ideas at large, medium and small scales, scoring each one on impact, reach and differentiation, and ranking them into do-now, do-next and explore lists. It is aimed at founders and product leads deciding what to build next. Its output is a dated analysis file under a docs folder, with no code written.
tasks: find 10x opportunities for my product
decide what we should build next
rank feature ideas by impact and effort
review product strategy for a site or app
qualityWhy: The skill gives clear steps, scoring criteria, an output template and rules an agent can follow, though it says little about how to research an existing codebase.
why: It is stack-free product planning that helps decide what a node's builder should make next, so it is useful now and then rather than for every build. It only writes strategy notes to a docs folder and needs no keys or outside services.

summary: This skill teaches an agent to inspect and control macOS applications through the Peekaboo command-line tool. The agent lists running apps, takes annotated screenshots or element snapshots of a window, acts on a specific element, and then checks the result again. It is aimed at someone who needs to test or screenshot a Mac app, or automate a desktop workflow.
tasks: capture a screenshot of a running Mac app window
automate clicks and typing to test a desktop app flow
inspect UI elements of an open macOS application
verify that a macOS app shows the expected result after an action
qualityWhy: The skill gives concrete v4 commands, a snapshot-act-verify workflow, a bridge-socket procedure and troubleshooting steps, though it defers many details to the installed CLI's --help output.
why: It runs locally on macOS and needs no outside service or account, but it serves desktop testing and screenshots rather than building sites or content directly. It requires macOS Screen Recording and Accessibility permissions granted to the host process, and it can move the shared cursor and send keystrokes when foreground interaction is authorized.

summary: This skill lets an agent manage Elastic Security detection rules through the Kibana Detection Engine API. It can find noisy rules, add exceptions, tune queries and thresholds, and create new rules, with Endpoint behaviour rules handled through a separate exception list. It is aimed at SOC analysts and security engineers who run an Elastic SIEM.
tasks: find the noisiest detection rules and tune one
add an exception to exclude a known-good process from a rule
create a new detection rule for a suspicious behaviour
validate a detection query before creating a rule
qualityWhy: The SKILL.md and references give concrete commands, query syntax checks, workflows and a clear tool table, with only small gaps such as a few undefined terms.
why: It serves Elastic SIEM and Endpoint security operations, not building, running or selling a site, app, agent or content, so it is not useful for what a Fractera node is for.
risks: Tells the agent to pass --yes to skip the scripts' confirmation prompts on production write operations such as disable, delete and add-exception.
Tells the agent not to read SKILL.md or list files before acting, which keeps the instructions from being checked first.

summary: This skill tells an agent how to run the knip tool on a JavaScript or TypeScript project to find unused files, unused dependencies and unused exports. It asks the agent to tune knip's configuration first, cutting false positives, and only then remove the reported dead code. Developers who want a leaner codebase are the people it serves.
tasks: clean up unused files and dependencies in a project
find dead exports in my codebase
remove unused npm packages from package.json
configure knip to stop false positives
qualityWhy: The skill gives an ordered workflow, exact commands, configuration rules and confidence levels an agent can follow, though it has no pre-run backup or clean-git-state check before deletions.
why: It is stack-free and runs locally with no outside service, so it suits any Node project on a node, but dead-code cleanup is only occasionally useful. The skill installs knip as a dev dependency, which is a normal step rather than a stack conflict.
risks: The --fix --allow-remove-files command can delete project files without a review step if an agent runs it automatically.

summary: This skill makes an agent map a code repository: it finds the projects inside it, reads their languages, frameworks and dependency files, and writes a structured overview to a repo.md file. The overview then serves as context before further analysis. It is aimed at developers and security reviewers who need a quick picture of an unfamiliar codebase. The skill is meant to work only from local files, without web access.
tasks: map the structure of this codebase
list the projects and frameworks in this repository
write a repository overview before a security review
summarise how the code is organised
qualityWhy: The workflow steps and output checks are concrete, but the detector and summarizer files it relies on were not supplied for review, and the skill-directory lookup searches for 'repo-context' while the skill is named 'ghost-repo-context', which could break it.
why: It is a stack-free repository mapping habit that can give a node's agent a useful overview of a site or app codebase, though its stated purpose is security analysis rather than building content. It writes its cache under the home folder's ~/.ghost directory rather than the node's own folder, and the path mismatch in its setup step needs fixing before it runs reliably.

summary: The skill guides an agent through writing short-form marketing copy such as headlines, calls to action, ad text, landing page sections and email copy. It offers conversion frameworks (PAS, AIDA, BAB, FAB, 4 U's), headline formulas, CTA best practices and an output format. It is aimed at marketers and founders who need persuasive copy for a product or campaign.
tasks: write landing page headline and CTA copy
draft ad copy using PAS or AIDA
improve CTA buttons for a sign-up form
write email subject lines and body copy
qualityWhy: It is clear and organised, but it stays at the level of general frameworks and checklists with no worked examples or verification steps.
why: Short-form marketing copy for landing pages, shops and ads is exactly what a node is used for, and the skill is stack-free, so it can be installed as written. It refers to other skills such as landing-page-generator and cta-generator that the node may not have installed.

summary: Guides an agent through computing CRAP (Change Risk Anti-Patterns) scores for a named .NET method, class, or file by combining cyclomatic complexity with Cobertura code coverage. It insists on real coverage data, runs or reuses a repository-compatible coverage command, counts complexity from current source, and computes scores with a calculator. The output is a sorted risk table with recommendations on which tests to add or where to reduce complexity. The intended users are .NET developers prioritising tests for a specific piece of code.
tasks: calculate CRAP score for a .NET method
find risky methods in a class by coverage and complexity
decide which tests to prioritize in a named file
compute how much coverage a method needs to drop below CRAP 15
qualityWhy: The steps, formula, decision tables, fallback rules and validation checks are concrete and complete, though it depends on other skills like run-tests and coverage-analysis that are not included.
why: It is a .NET-only code-quality analysis that runs on local source and local coverage reports, so it is useful for building a product, but it is not a site, app, agent or content tool for the node's stack and its value is limited to that niche. It also delegates to other skills, and its use would be a test-quality aid rather than a core node feature. Value is set to none only because the skill serves a narrow .NET testing audience outside what nodes are for; the instruction itself is sound.

summary: This skill guides an agent through building scroll-driven motion in vanilla JavaScript, React or Next.js. It covers GSAP ScrollTrigger for pinning, scrubbing, snapping and horizontal scroll, and Framer Motion (Motion v12) for scroll-linked values and in-view entrance animations. It gives copy-ready code patterns for fade-ins, parallax, pinned timelines and scroll progress, plus rules on reduced-motion accessibility and performance. It is aimed at front-end developers and designers who want polished scroll effects on a site or landing page.
tasks: add fade-in animations as the user scrolls
build a pinned scroll section with a timeline
create a parallax effect on a hero image
make a scroll progress bar
add horizontal scroll to a page section
qualityWhy: The SKILL.md gives concrete code, a library selector, critical rules and checks, though the detailed recipes sit in reference files that were not part of this review.
why: Scroll animation is a direct part of building polished sites and landing pages, and both libraries run locally in the node's React and Next.js stack without an external service. The skill is generic and does not replace the node's stack, so it can be installed as written, though the reference files were not reviewed here and the Copilot-specific prompting tips are not useful to a node agent.

summary: This skill is a single prompt-rewriting routine invoked by a /sharpen command. It asks the agent to make a task deeper rather than larger by naming what a top professional would add, the raw source material they would start from, the specific methods and tools they would use, and the independent checks that would confirm the result. The agent then rewrites the person's prompt to request exactly that, leaving their own decisions open. It is aimed at people who want more rigorous work product from a request.
tasks: deepen a vague request into a professional-grade prompt
rewrite my prompt to ask for raw sources and proper methods
add independent verification steps to a task
qualityWhy: The instructions are clear and short with four concrete questions and a rewrite step, but they give no example, output format or checks beyond the four questions.
why: It is a stack-free thinking habit that could help an agent on a node draft better prompts for building or content work, but it is useful only now and then. Nothing in the file calls an outside service or touches data.

summary: This skill lets an agent turn text into speech, generate background music, create sound effects, and clone a voice from a sample. It routes each request to a model, mainly ElevenLabs for speech and sound effects and fal.ai for music, and returns an audio file or URL. It is aimed at people who need voice-overs, soundtracks or effects for videos, podcasts and other content without managing several audio APIs.
tasks: make a voice-over for a product video
generate background music for a podcast
create a sound effect such as a door opening
clone a voice from a short audio sample
qualityWhy: The instructions contradict each other: the Quick Reference and routing section point music to the text_to_sound_effects MCP tool while the notes say cassetteai-music, and the MCP server it starts is never called by cli.js, which talks to a separate proxy.
needs: FAL_KEY (optional, for music and SFX via fal.ai)
a self-hosted proxy or hosted audiomind-proxy.vercel.app
why: Audio generation is directly useful for making content, but the default path sends the person's text and optional key to a third-party hosted proxy that SKILL.md does not clearly describe, so it should not be installed as written. The start script also adds a local 100-use trial limit with an upgrade placeholder, and the skill is thin and internally inconsistent, so it would need rework before use.
risks: By default cli.js sends the person's text prompts and any AUDIOMIND_API_KEY to a third-party hosted proxy (audiomind-proxy.vercel.app), and SKILL.md does not clearly say that the content leaves the machine.

summary: This skill lets an agent analyze a local git repository's history to see which people have touched which files, then flags sensitive code (auth, crypto, secrets) that few people maintain or that has gone stale. It computes bus factor, finds files that tend to change together, and groups them into clusters. Results can be exported as CSV or JSON for graph tools, and small query commands return bounded slices of the output.
tasks: find security-sensitive files with only one maintainer
check whether CODEOWNERS matches who really changes auth code
show which files usually change together in this repo
export the contributor-to-file graph for Neo4j or Gephi
qualityWhy: The skill gives concrete commands, output file descriptions, default rules and query examples, but one script (run_ownership_map.py) was not visible and some paths assume a particular repo layout.
why: It analyzes the code history of the person's own repository on their computer, which suits maintaining a product's security, but it is not a builder or content tool. It is not tied to another stack, and its data stays local. I could not read run_ownership_map.py, so its behaviour is unverified.

summary: The skill guides an agent through calling native C and C++ libraries from .NET with P/Invoke, using DllImport or the source-generated LibraryImport. It covers mapping C types to .NET types, string encoding, memory ownership, SafeHandle wrappers, callbacks and cross-platform library loading. It is aimed at developers who wrap or debug native interop code.
tasks: wrap a C library for use in .NET
fix an AccessViolationException at the native boundary
migrate DllImport declarations to LibraryImport
review P/Invoke signatures against a C header
qualityWhy: The skill gives concrete steps, type-mapping rules, code examples for each pattern, a review checklist and runnable validation steps.
why: Useful when a Fractera node's C# code needs native libraries, but most node work is Next.js and TypeScript, so it is only occasionally relevant. It is stack-free within .NET and needs no outside service, so it can be installed as written.

summary: This skill gives an agent a single toolkit for pulling public social media data (YouTube, TikTok, Instagram, LinkedIn and more), China and Southeast Asian e-commerce listings through Apify actors, and fallback page extraction for pages that block plain fetching. It also includes a site-audit method that checks links, sitemaps and buttons in a real browser without deciding by itself what is broken. It is aimed at people doing market research, content work or site QA. The bundled helpers route every call through a proxy that injects credentials, so the agent never needs a user key.
tasks: download a YouTube transcript and video metadata
scrape a TikTok or Instagram profile's recent posts
audit a website for broken links and non-working buttons
pull Xiaohongshu or Taobao product listings
recover an article behind a paywall from an archive snapshot
qualityWhy: The instructions are concrete, with endpoint tables, cost caps, error-to-action mappings, worked examples and unit tests, though the files are long and a few sections are cut off.
why: Social and web data extraction is useful for building and making content, but every data source here is an external scraping service, which fits the install-with-service category. The skill also depends on a platform proxy (core.http_client) and a skill-tools loader that a node may not provide, and it asks the agent to use paid per-result actors, so the cost and the proxy dependency should be checked before use.
risks: Skill tells the agent to route scraping through a proxy that injects credentials, so calls send requests and URLs to third-party services on the user's behalf without an explicit per-call consent step.

summary: This skill lets an agent turn a dataset into a self-contained interactive chart page built on ECharts, with templates for line, bar, pie, candlestick, scatter, radar, heatmap, waterfall, dual-axis, multi-panel and dashboard layouts. Each chart is saved in its own project folder with the HTML, the generation script, a data snapshot and a README, so it can be reopened and changed later. Export works through buttons that download, copy or save a PNG, or through a headless browser screenshot. It is aimed at analysts, business-intelligence work and anyone who needs a chart image for a report or post.
tasks: plot BTC against gold prices over the last year
make a bar chart of revenue by quarter
compare two return series on one chart
build a KPI dashboard page with several charts
export a chart as a PNG for a social post
qualityWhy: The steps, template list, code signatures and checks are concrete and easy to follow, but hard-coded /data/workspace paths, a truncated export script and a few doc inconsistencies leave small gaps.
why: It is local-first: the charts, data and PNGs are written to the project folder, and no account or key is required. It is stack-free and works with Python and plain HTML, though the default /data/workspace paths need changing to the node's own folder, and the page loads ECharts from a public CDN when viewed. Parts of the export script were cut off in the files, so that code could not be fully checked.

summary: This skill lets an agent send a user's original question to the Wind Alice financial research service and name a specific Alice sub-skill, such as a one-page investment memo, a stock due-diligence question list, or a credit analysis. It streams the result back and saves any report attachments into a local folder. It is aimed at investment analysts, researchers and finance professionals who want Chinese-market analysis. The skill also tells the agent how to handle quota, credit and blocked-request responses.
tasks: write a one-page investment memo for a listed company
prepare management interview questions for a stock
run a credit analysis on a bond issuer
fact-check a financial claim
qualityWhy: The SKILL.md gives concrete commands, exit-code handling, output rules and a skill-name table, though it is long and tied to one vendor's portal.
why: The background update check silently fetches and reinstalls remote code, which is a risk, so the skill should not be installed as written. Beyond that, it is a paid cloud financial-research service: useful for investment analysis but not for building or running a product, and the user's prompts go to a third party.
risks: A background process silently auto-updates the skill from a remote git source, running fetched code without the person's knowledge or consent.
The update check is detached and produces no output, so the person cannot see these actions.

summary: The skill has an agent research five direct competitors of a product or market, using web search to gather their positioning, features, pricing and go-to-market details. It then writes a structured brief covering market overview, competitor profiles, strengths and weaknesses, business models, and differentiation opportunities with a positioning recommendation. It is aimed at product managers and strategists preparing competitive research.
tasks: analyze competitors for my product
prepare a competitive brief for a market
find differentiation opportunities against rivals
map the competitive landscape of an industry
qualityWhy: The output structure is detailed and useful, but the instructions are generic, give no method for verifying sources, and leave the steps for finding competitors thin.
why: It is a stack-free research habit that helps plan a product, but it is not about building or running a site or app, so its use is occasional. It needs live web search to produce current results, which is a service the person chooses.

summary: This skill tells an agent to turn a finished ad brief and brand profile into image ads for paid campaigns. The agent builds prompts from the concept, subject, setting, brand colours and platform size rules, then sends only approved variants to an image provider the person has configured. It checks each image's file type, dimensions, safe zones and copy, and records hashes and cost in a manifest so that every asset can be traced. It is aimed at marketers and product teams who make campaign visuals.
tasks: generate ad images from a campaign brief
create social media ad creatives for several platforms
make campaign visuals in the brand style
produce image variants within a budget
qualityWhy: The steps are a sensible outline with some checks, but they depend on undefined inputs (brief, brand profile, provider capability) and give no commands, schemas, prompt examples or file layout an agent could follow directly.
needs: an explicitly configured image generation provider and its API key or account (not named in the skill)
why: It directly serves making ad images for a product, but it only works once the person chooses and configures an image provider, and the skill names none. Its instructions are abstract, so an agent would need to fill in the missing parts itself.

summary: This skill guides an agent through building full-stack React apps with TanStack Start, covering project setup, server functions for typed client-server calls, middleware for auth and logging, API routes, streaming SSR, and deployment presets. It is aimed at developers who want a TanStack-based alternative to other React frameworks.
tasks: set up a full-stack React app with TanStack Start
add a server function with validated input
protect routes with auth middleware
add an API route for users
configure SSR streaming and deployment
qualityWhy: The examples are concrete, but the skill is thin, marked RC, and several APIs (defer, Await, createAPIFileRoute, the validator chain) may be outdated or incomplete, with no verification steps.
why: It builds on a different framework than the node's Next.js 16 stack, so an agent should read it for patterns (server functions, middleware, SSR) and build them the node's way rather than install it as written. Its API accuracy is unverified and it is still an RC.

summary: The skill guides an agent through Apple's Vision framework on iOS: running on-device text recognition, face and barcode detection, segmentation, object tracking and document scanning, plus running custom Core ML models through Vision. It also covers VisionKit's live camera scanner. It is written for iOS app developers, not for web nodes.
tasks: add text recognition to an iOS app
scan barcodes and QR codes with the camera
detect faces and landmarks in photos
run a custom Core ML model on camera images
qualityWhy: The file gives concrete Swift code, a legacy-versus-modern comparison, common mistakes and a review checklist, though much detail is pushed into reference files that were not included in the review.
why: The skill is for native iOS and macOS apps in Swift, which a Fractera node does not build, so it does not serve the node's web stack. Nothing in it is risky, but it cannot be installed usefully on a node.

summary: This skill makes an agent review variable, function, class, file and column names in a codebase and propose clearer replacements. It checks for vague, abbreviated, misleading and inconsistently cased names, and applies language conventions for JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, Java and Go. It is aimed at developers who want more readable code in their projects.
tasks: review variable and function names in a project
suggest clearer names for confusing identifiers
check naming conventions for a language
rename misleading boolean or constant names
qualityWhy: It gives a clear procedure, per-language conventions and concrete bad-versus-good examples, but it does not say how to verify that renames update every reference.
why: It is a stack-free code-quality habit that an agent on a node can use while building a site or app, though it is useful only now and then rather than for core node work. It has no scripts or outside services, so it can be installed as written.

summary: This skill makes an agent run a multi-agent security audit of native C or C++ code, looking for memory corruption, integer overflows, race conditions and platform-specific bugs. It asks for the threat model, severity filter and scope, then runs a workflow that splits the code into units, reviews them in parallel, sweeps for missed bug classes and assembles a report with findings and a coverage gate. It is written for security reviewers auditing C/C++ daemons, services and userspace libraries.
tasks: audit a C daemon for memory safety bugs
find integer overflows in a C parser
review a C++ service for race conditions
produce a SARIF security report for a native codebase
qualityWhy: The steps, parameter table, phase breakdown, failure handling and rationalization checks are concrete and complete, but the workflow script, worker agent and assembler it depends on are not included in the files, so it cannot run as shipped.
why: The skill audits native C/C++ userspace code, which is not part of what Fractera nodes are for (Next.js, TypeScript and content or product building); it does not serve building, running, selling or making content with a node. It is not a cloud service, so the skip comes from the subject, not from a cloud-dependency rule.

summary: This skill lets an agent tidy a raw screen recording before it is published. It cuts out long pauses and low-level keyboard noise with FFmpeg, then speeds the cleaned video up slightly. It is aimed at people who make screencasts or tutorial clips for social posts, landing pages, or blogs.
tasks: remove pauses from a screen recording
clean up a screencast before publishing
speed up a tutorial video slightly
preview which silent parts would be cut
qualityWhy: The skill gives concrete commands, tuned parameters, a dry-run check and a list of custom scenarios, but its claim that remove_silence uses stream copy contradicts the script, which re-encodes.
why: It directly serves making video content for a product and runs entirely on local files with no outside service. FFmpeg and uv must already be installed, and the SKILL.md text about stream copy is wrong because the code re-encodes, so an agent should trust the code and the printed summary.

summary: This skill is a deprecation notice for an older Angular SSR guide. It says the skill is unmaintained and points the agent to the official Angular skills repository, where SSR guidance now lives. It contains no setup steps, hydration fixes or prerendering instructions of its own.
tasks: set up server-side rendering in an Angular app
fix a hydration mismatch
prerender static routes in Angular
qualityWhy: The file is a stub that only points to another repository and contains no actionable instructions.
why: The skill only redirects to the official angular/skills repository and has no usable guidance for a Fractera node; the redirect command is a normal npx install of another skill set, not a risk in itself.

summary: This skill lets an agent look up iOS apps and bundles on the Apple App Store through a paid data API. It can search by keyword in any country's storefront, fetch full app details, read reviews sorted by recent or helpful, find similar apps, and list a developer's catalog. It suits people doing app store optimization, competitor tracking, or market research who lack Apple Developer Program access. Each call is a plain HTTP GET, paid either with prepaid credits or per call in USDC through x402.
tasks: search iOS apps by keyword in a specific country
compare an app's reviews by helpfulness
find competitor apps similar to a given app
list all apps published by a developer
research app store keywords for ASO
qualityWhy: The skill gives a clear endpoint table, parameter rules, concrete curl examples for each scenario, auth options and error codes, though it has no scripts and few validation checks.
needs: fetcher.sh prepaid API key (bby_live_ prefix) or an x402-capable USDC wallet
why: It is a useful data source for app store research, but it is a third-party paid service rather than something the node itself builds with, so its value is occasional. It calls an outside service and needs a fetcher.sh key or a wallet for x402 payments, which the person chooses to provide.

summary: Guides an agent to build a public-safe brand and offer profile for paid advertising from a website the operator is authorised to analyse. It covers the brand name, offer, audience, proof points, voice, colours, typography, imagery, accessibility and claims, while separating what was directly seen from what is inferred. Results are written to a project state folder with source URLs and capture dates, so ad teams can use them as creative context.
tasks: extract a brand profile from our website
summarise our brand voice and visual style for ad creative
list the offer, audience and proof points from a landing page
prepare a style guide for a paid campaign
qualityWhy: The steps are clear and safety-minded, but they are short and generic, with no concrete extraction method, output schema or examples.
why: Useful for ad and brand work on a node that builds landing pages and campaigns, though it is a thin procedure rather than a tool. It is stack-free, so it can be installed as written, and it does not require any outside service or key.

summary: The skill guides an agent through setting up, diagnosing and fixing pixel-perfect 2D rendering in Unity, first detecting whether the project uses URP or the Built-in pipeline and then choosing the matching PixelPerfectCamera component. It covers sprite import settings such as point filtering and disabled mipmaps, camera and quality settings, grid snapping, tilemap gaps, Cinemachine conflicts and common symptoms. It is aimed at developers making retro or pixel-art 2D games in Unity, not HD 2D work.
tasks: fix blurry pixel art sprites in Unity
set up a pixel perfect camera for a retro 2D game
diagnose jittery or misaligned 2D sprites
fix tilemap gaps between tiles
qualityWhy: The file gives a clear pipeline-first workflow, a diagnostic checklist, concrete fixes and a list of known limitations, with code references, though the supporting code files were not reviewed here.
why: It is a Unity-specific skill, and Fractera nodes do not run Unity projects, so an agent could only use it as reference for pixel-art rendering ideas, not as an install. Its guidance is local and has no cloud or key requirements.

summary: This skill lets an agent search Chinese e-commerce platforms such as Taobao, JD, Pinduoduo, Douyin and Kuaishou for a product keyword and get back a CSV list with prices, coupons, shop names and sales. It can also fetch a product's detail, a buy link and a copyable share code. It is aimed at shoppers looking for the lowest price or a discount. It works by calling a third-party app API through a small Python script.
tasks: find the cheapest price for a product across Chinese shopping sites
get the coupon or discount link for an item
compare prices of a product on Taobao, JD and Pinduoduo
qualityWhy: The commands are concrete and the script runs, but SKILL.md is short, the source codes in its table do not match the script's defaults, and there are no error checks or examples of output.
needs: maishou88 third-party app API (no user key, but it uses a fixed openid and invite code)
why: It is a consumer shopping tool with no use for building, running, selling or making content for a product, and it relies on a third-party service that is not local-first. The script also sends the buyer's search keywords to that service and attaches a hardcoded invite code, which the SKILL.md never mentions.
risks: The script embeds a fixed openid and a default invite code (6110440) that are not disclosed in SKILL.md, so the buyer's purchase links and API calls go out under the author's referral and identity without telling them.
The script sends the buyer's search keywords to a third-party server (appapi.maishou88.com) without telling them.

summary: This skill points an agent to Remotion's official licensing material: the license page, the license FAQ, and the terms and conditions. It answers questions about what the license covers and where to purchase one. It is aimed at developers and teams using Remotion who need to check their obligations.
tasks: check whether my project needs a Remotion license
find the Remotion license FAQ
buy a Remotion license
read Remotion terms and conditions
qualityWhy: It is a short wrapper that only links to external documents with no steps, checks or summary of the license rules.
why: Useful when a person asks licensing questions about Remotion, but it only points elsewhere and does not explain the terms itself. It has no stack dependency and no outside service calls, so it can be installed as written.

summary: This skill guides an agent through planning a large piece of work that a single session cannot hold, by building a shared map of decision tickets in a repo issue tracker and resolving them one at a time until the route to a chosen destination is clear. It is aimed at engineers and planners who want to chart an effort before building it. Planning is the default, and execution is only added when the map's notes say so.
tasks: plan a large project as decision tickets
map out the route to a spec or decision
resolve the next open planning ticket
chart an effort before handing it off
qualityWhy: The SKILL.md gives clear modes, ticket types, labels, and step lists, though it depends on a tracker doc and setup command it does not include and is written in a dense, abstract style.
needs: an issue tracker with native blocking links, or the local-markdown fallback
why: It is a planning method, not a product-building tool, so its value to a Fractera node is only occasional. It assumes an external repo issue tracker and Matt Pocock's skill set (grilling, domain-modeling, prototype), so an agent would need to adapt it to the node's own project tooling rather than install it as written.

summary: This skill lets an agent pull Google News headlines and keyword search results as JSON from a paid hosted API, without scraping Google's RSS feeds. It covers searching by keyword within a chosen language edition, fetching section headlines such as technology or business, looking up topic IDs, and turning Google News redirect links into real article URLs. It is aimed at people who monitor news, track media mentions, or gather headlines for research or content work. Payment is either a prepaid credit key or per-call USDC via x402.
tasks: track press mentions of my brand
pull this week's technology headlines
search Google News for a keyword in the UK edition
resolve Google News links to the original article URLs
build a daily news digest from section headlines
qualityWhy: It gives clear endpoints, parameters, copy-paste curl examples, MCP config and error codes, but the payment and credit mechanics are deferred to another skill.
needs: fetcher.sh prepaid API key or a USDC wallet on Base, Polygon, Arbitrum, Monad or Solana for x402 payments
why: News monitoring and headline gathering are useful for content and product work, but this is a paid external service rather than a local tool, so it is used only when the person chooses it. The x402 flow signs payments automatically from a wallet, so the person should set a spending limit or use prepaid credits.

summary: This skill guides an agent through a read-only audit of a Microsoft Advertising account, covering conversion tracking, search and audience campaigns, keywords, creative, bidding, budgets and policy compliance. It asks for the campaign objective, date window, currency and data sources, then returns structured findings and a prioritized list of recommendations. The audit itself depends on several reference files that are not included in this package, so an agent cannot run it from the skill alone. Changes to campaigns are routed to a different skill.
tasks: audit my Microsoft Advertising account
check UET conversion tracking on my Bing campaigns
review keywords and bidding for Microsoft Ads
find policy and creative problems in my search ads
qualityWhy: The file is mostly a procedure that points to missing reference documents and a conductor, leaving the actual checks unspecified for an agent to follow.
needs: Microsoft Advertising account with API or export access
why: It serves a product that sells through ads, but only occasionally, and it needs a Microsoft Advertising account. Its referenced files are absent from the package, so the skill is incomplete as shipped.

summary: This skill guides an agent through finding why a .NET solution builds slowly, using MSBuild binary logs and the target and task performance summaries. It covers common bottlenecks such as slow assembly reference resolution, costly Roslyn analyzers, serialized builds, heavy file copying and restore overhead, with thresholds for judging each one. It is aimed at .NET developers and build engineers who already have a baseline measurement.
tasks: find why a .NET solution builds slowly
analyze an MSBuild binlog for slow targets
check whether Roslyn analyzers slow down the C# compile
reduce restore and copy overhead in a .NET build
qualityWhy: The skill gives concrete commands, thresholds, fixes and checklists an agent can follow, though some steps depend on a bundled MCP server and cross-references to other skills that are not included.
why: The node builds Next.js, React and TypeScript products, and this skill only applies to MSBuild-based .NET builds, so it does not serve those uses. It is a read-only diagnostic guide with no risky behaviour, so skipping it is about fit, not safety.

summary: This skill tells an agent to add a binary log switch to every MSBuild-based .NET command, such as dotnet build, test, pack, publish and restore, so each run leaves a full execution trace on disk. It covers the unique {} filename placeholder, PowerShell quoting, fixed-name fallbacks for older MSBuild versions, checking that the log was written, and keeping logs when cleaning a git repository. It is written for developers working on .NET solutions who need to diagnose build errors or slow builds afterwards.
tasks: capture a binlog for a failing dotnet build
keep separate build logs to compare before and after a change
check that a build produced a binlog before analysing it
clean a git repo without deleting build logs
qualityWhy: The instructions are concrete, with correct and wrong examples, a verification step and fallbacks for older MSBuild versions, though they are narrow and short on troubleshooting detail.
why: Fractera nodes run Next.js, TypeScript and SQLite, not .NET or MSBuild, so this build-log technique does not serve building, running or selling what a node is for. It would only help with a separate .NET project.

summary: The skill gives an agent guidance for planning and judging A/B and multivariate content experiments. It covers writing hypotheses, choosing metrics, estimating sample size, reading p-values and confidence intervals, wiring variants into a CMS, and avoiding common analysis mistakes. It is aimed at marketers, product owners and developers who run conversion or engagement tests on web content.
tasks: plan an A/B test for a landing page headline
calculate sample size for a conversion experiment
check whether a test result is statistically significant
set up CMS-managed content variants for testing
review an experiment for common analysis pitfalls
qualityWhy: The skill is organised as a reference set with clear sections on design, statistics, CMS integration and pitfalls, but only the index file was provided in full here, so depth in the other files could not be fully verified.
why: It is stack-free methodology that helps a node's owner design and read experiments for their site or shop, and it does not depend on a cloud service. Its CMS section is generic, so the agent would need to map variant handling onto the node's own SQLite data and Blocks catalogue rather than a particular CMS.

summary: This skill gives an agent a checklist for testing login systems for authentication bypass.
